0217: \begin{definition}[Sufficient maximum-window hypothesis H1]
0218: \label{hyp:normal-window}
0219: For every $\varepsilon>0$,
0220: \[
0221:  \#\{n\le x:\log R(n)>\varepsilon\omega(n)\}=o(x).
0222: \tag{H1}
0223: \]
0224: \end{definition}
0225: 
0226: \begin{definition}[Sufficient maximum-window hypothesis H2]
0227: \label{hyp:mean-window}
0228: One has
0229: \[
0230:  \sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log R(n)
0231:  =o\bigl(x(\log\log x)^2\bigr).
0232: \tag{H2}
0233: \]
0234: \end{definition}
0235: 
0236: \begin{proposition}[Conditional obstruction from Fibonacci prime divisors]
0237: \label{prop:blms-obstructs-mean-window}
0238: Assume Conjecture~5.1 of Bugeaud--Luca--Mignotte--Siksek
0239: \cite{BugeaudLucaMignotteSiksek2005FewPrimeDivisors}, namely that
0240: $\omega(F_n)\gg\log n$ for composite $n$. Then, for every fixed
0241: $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<1-\log2$,
0242: \begin{equation}\label{eq:blms-normal-window-obstruction}
0243:  \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac1x
0244:  \#\{n\le x:\log R(n)>\varepsilon\omega(n)\}
0245:  \ge\frac6{\pi^2},
0246: \end{equation}
0247: and
0248: \begin{equation}\label{eq:blms-mean-window-obstruction}
0249:  \liminf_{x\to\infty}
0250:  \frac{\sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log R(n)}
0251:  {x(\log\log x)^2}
0252:  \ge\frac6{\pi^2}(1-\log2)>0.
0253: \end{equation}
0254: In particular, under that published conjecture, both sufficient
0255: maximum-window hypotheses \textup{(H1)} and \textup{(H2)} are false.
0256: \end{proposition}
0257: 
0258: \begin{proof}
0259: Let $n$ be squarefree and put $k=\omega(n)$. The exact-rank partition of the
0260: prime divisors of $F_n$ gives
0261: \[
0262:  \omega(F_n)=\sum_{d\mid n}a(d).
0263: \]
0264: For squarefree $n$, every nonempty support $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ has the
0265: single rank $d=\prod_{\ell\in J}\ell$ in its window. Since $a(1)=0$, the
0266: pigeonhole principle and \eqref{eq:prime-window-versus-R} give
0267: \begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-blms-pigeonhole}
0268:  R(n)\ge\max_{d\mid n}a(d)
0269:  \ge\frac{\omega(F_n)}{2^k-1}.
0270: \end{equation}
0271: Under the stated conjecture, for every sufficiently large squarefree composite
0272: $n$,
0273: \[
0274:  \log R(n)\ge\log\log n-k\log2+O(1).
0275: \]
0276: The Hardy--Ramanujan theorem has an exceptional set of $o(x)$ integers, so on
0277: all but $o(x)$ squarefree integers one has
0278: $k=(1+o(1))\log\log n$. Consequently
0279: \[
0280:  \omega(n)\log R(n)
0281:  \ge(1-\log2+o(1))(\log\log n)^2
0282: \]
0283: on this set. Squarefree integers have density $6/\pi^2$, and squarefree prime
0284: indices have density zero. Moreover,
0285: \[
0286:  \frac{\log R(n)}{\omega(n)}\ge1-\log2+o(1)
0287: \]
0288: on the same set. This proves
0289: \eqref{eq:blms-normal-window-obstruction}; summation over squarefree composite
0290: indices proves \eqref{eq:blms-mean-window-obstruction}.
0291: \end{proof}
0292: 
0293: \begin{corollary}[Purely conditional consequences of H1 and H2]
0294: \label{cor:conditional-orders}
0295: Assuming hypothesis \textup{(H1)} in Definition~\ref{hyp:normal-window},
0296: \begin{equation}\label{eq:conditional-normal-order}
0297:  L(n)\sim\frac{\log2}{4}(\log\log n)^2
0298:  \quad\text{for almost all }n.
0299: \end{equation}
0300: Assuming hypothesis \textup{(H2)} in Definition~\ref{hyp:mean-window},
0301: \begin{equation}\label{eq:conditional-mean-order}
0302:  \sum_{3\le n\le x}L(n)
0303:  \sim\frac{\log2}{4}x(\log\log x)^2.
0304: \end{equation}
0305: These are implications only: neither conclusion is unconditional, and no
0306: positive arithmetic evidence for either sufficient hypothesis is presently
0307: known. Proposition~\ref{prop:blms-obstructs-mean-window} shows that the
0308: published Bugeaud--Luca--Mignotte--Siksek conjecture predicts that both
0309: hypotheses fail.
0310: \end{corollary}
0311: 
0312: \begin{proof}
0313: For the first assertion, intersect the density-one set in
0314: Definition~\ref{hyp:normal-window} with the Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order set.
0315: Then the error $\omega(n)\log R(n)+O(\omega(n))$ in
0316: \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order} is $o(\omega(n)^2)$. For the second,
0317: sum the upper bound in \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}, use
0318: Definition~\ref{hyp:mean-window}, \eqref{eq:omega-second-moment}, and
0319: $\sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)=O(x\log\log x)$, and compare with the unconditional
0320: lower mean bound \eqref{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}.
0321: \end{proof}

0323: \begin{remark}[Exact residual arithmetic interface]
0324: \label{rem:exact-average-open-interface}
0325: Supplementary Corollary~\ref{supp-cor:theta-refined-connected-entropy} and
0326: Theorem~\ref{thm:minimal-generator-growth} determine the contribution of the
0327: multiplicity-free minimal-cover model used here: $\log2/4$ is its exact
0328: quadratic coefficient, the fixed-choice rank-pure sector supplies its
0329: theta-refined lower terms, and the private-coordinate upper bound retains the
0330: term $\omega(n)\log R(n)$. Proposition~
0331: \ref{prop:rank-jump-family-ladder-slots} gives the rank-window description for
0332: every support size:
0333: prime jump families are finite disjoint unions of the rank
0334: classes $\Pi_\alpha(d)$, while ladder families are singletons. Thus
0335: Hypotheses \textup{(H1)} and \textup{(H2)} in Definitions~
0336: \ref{hyp:normal-window} and \ref{hyp:mean-window} ask precisely for sufficient
0337: upper distributional control of
0338: exact-rank prime multiplicities in those rank windows.
0339: 
0340: The pointwise estimate \eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} proves only the
0341: consequence obtained by combining the fibotomic size identity with the
0342: divisibility of the exact-rank radical and the congruences
0343: $p\equiv\pm1\pmod d$. Supplementary Remark~
0344: \ref{supp-rem:cumulative-rank-estimates-insufficient} shows that even its
0345: Euler-factor scale does not by itself imply either maximum-window hypothesis. The
0346: manuscript does not prove that these inputs exhaust the information available
0347: from fibotomic arithmetic, or that
0348: \eqref{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy} is optimal within any information class. Such
0349: an optimality theorem would require, at minimum, a precise axiom class of
0350: admissible information and a realizable extremal model satisfying those
0351: axioms. Neither is supplied here. Whether stronger unconditional dispersion or
0352: concentration consequences follow from fibotomic arithmetic is therefore an
0353: open interface.
0354: 
0355: The closest distribution theorems do not close this interface.  In the
0356: notation of a nondegenerate Lucas sequence $U$ with nonsquare discriminant
0357: $\Delta$ and squarefree discriminant part $\Delta_0$, Sanna's Theorem~1.1
0358: \cite{Sanna2022RankDivisibility} gives, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula
0359: for
0360: \[
0361:  \#\{p\le x:d\mid\rho_U(p)\}
0362: \]
0363: when $d$ is odd, with $3\nmid d$ if $\Delta_0=-3$, and
0364: $x>\exp(Be^{8\omega(d)}d^8)$.  The condition counted is
0365: $d\mid\rho_U(p)$, not the exact-rank condition $\rho_U(p)=d$; for example,
0366: $3\mid\alpha(17)=9$ although $\alpha(17)\ne3$.  Sanna's Theorem~1.1 on the
0367: index of appearance \cite{Sanna2024IndexAppearance} instead assumes GRH and,
0368: for a fixed positive integer $t$, counts primes having
0369: $\iota_U(p)=t$ uniformly for $x>t^3$. Cera Da Concei\c c\~ao removes the
0370: restrictions in the fixed rank-divisibility density problem and gives
0371: explicit densities for all Lucas sequences and fixed $d$
0372: \cite{CeraDaConceicao2026PrimeDensities}; the condition remains
0373: $d\mid\rho_U(p)$ and still does not isolate a growing exact fiber. In the
0374: Fibonacci case,
0375: $\alpha(p)=d$ and $\iota_F(p)=t$ imply
0376: \[
0377:  p=td+\left(\frac5p\right)=td\pm1.
0378: \]
0379: Taking $x$ on the scale of this candidate prime restricts that theorem to
0380: $t^2\ll d$, and its cumulative fixed-index count still does not isolate the
0381: single rank $d$. Thus none of these results controls the growing exact fibers
0382: $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ required in \eqref{eq:visible-single-rank-interface}.
0383: 
0384: The primitive-divisor theorems of Carmichael and Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier give
0385: existence in the Fibonacci setting. Granville proves an odd-multiplicity
0386: primitive-factor theorem for a class of second-order Lucas recurrences with
0387: $c\equiv2\pmod4$ and explicitly leaves the odd-$b,c$ case, including the
0388: Fibonacci recurrence $b=c=1$, outside that theorem
0389: \cite{Granville2012PrimitivePrimeFactors}. Thus it is a neighboring
0390: Lucas-sequence result, not a Fibonacci multiplicity input here. Kiss treats
0391: related Lucas-sequence primitive-divisor questions
0392: \cite{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}. Hong proves that, for each fixed positive
0393: integer $\kappa$ and all sufficiently large $n$ with an explicit threshold,
0394: $F_n$ has a primitive divisor at least $(\kappa+1)n-1$
0395: \cite{Hong2025BigPrimitiveDivisors}. These results concern existence, parity of
0396: one primitive factor's multiplicity in the stated Lucas class, or the size of
0397: one Fibonacci primitive divisor; they do not provide the required average
0398: dispersion or critical concentration estimates for Fibonacci exact-rank prime
0399: multiplicities in visible divisor windows. The
0400: Hardy--Ramanujan and
0401: Tur\'an theorems control the additive function $\omega(n)$ but not the prime
0402: factorization of $F_d$ across exact apparition ranks. Likewise, the
0403: Erd\H{o}s--Wintner theorem \cite{ErdosWintner1939Additive} concerns limiting
0404: distributions of additive arithmetic functions, whereas $L(n)$ and $R(n)$
0405: are not additive. No implication from RH or ERH to either rank-window
0406: conjecture is presently known. Accordingly, the normal and mean equivalents
0407: \eqref{eq:conditional-normal-order} and
0408: \eqref{eq:conditional-mean-order} are conditional; the unconditional
0409: statements are \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order} and
0410: \eqref{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}, together with the stronger connected lower
0411: bound in Supplementary Corollary~
0412: \ref{supp-cor:theta-refined-connected-entropy}.
0413: None of these estimates implies that the disconnected part of $\mathcal M_n$
0414: is negligible; the strictly stronger blockwise hypothesis needed for that
0415: conclusion is isolated in Supplementary Theorem~
0416: \ref{supp-thm:blockwise-connected-dominance}.
0417: \end{remark}

0001: \section{Further questions}\label{sec:questions}
0002: %% ====================================================================
0003: 
0004: The theorem attempt leaves a two-sided arithmetic interface.  First,
0005: determine the normal order of the weighted excess $\mathcal W(n)$ in
0006: \eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.  In particular, prove or disprove
0007: \[
0008:  \log\mathcal W(n)=o((\log\log n)^2)
0009: \]
0010: for almost all odd $n$.  By
0011: Corollary~\ref{cor:odd-weighted-cover-obstruction}, this is necessary for the
0012: target asymptotic and concerns only the explicit exact-rank-prime sector.
0013: On squarefree indices Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} identifies
0014: this sector canonically as the minimal squarefree part of $\alpha^{-1}(n)$.
0015: Proposition~\ref{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction} also shows exactly
0016: why a bound for the cumulative quantity $\omega(F_n)$ alone cannot settle the
0017: question: at fixed total exact-rank mass, full-support concentration attains
0018: the minimum possible weighted cover sum. Thus resolving a conjecture about
0019: $\omega(F_n)$ is not a substitute for locating that mass among exact ranks.
0020: 
0021: Second, bound the complementary witness covers containing ladder jumps or
0022: prime jumps from sub-full rank windows. On squarefree indices this is exactly
0023: the nonsquarefree part of $\mathcal M_n$. The example
0024: $169\in\mathcal M_{91}\setminus\mathcal R_{91}^{\rm rp}$ shows that this
0025: sector cannot be discarded even on odd squarefree layers.  A complete
0026: almost-all upper bound must show that the combined contribution of this
0027: complement and the weighted rank-pure excess is
0028: $\exp(o((\log\log n)^2))$ relative to the unweighted cover scale.
0029: 
0030: The sufficient maximum-window hypotheses H1 and H2 in
0031: Definitions~\ref{hyp:normal-window} and \ref{hyp:mean-window} formulate
0032: upper bounds strong enough for both tasks.  Theorem
0033: \ref{thm:mean-rank-window-deaggregation} reduces the mean version to the
0034: visible single-rank maximum \eqref{eq:visible-single-rank-interface}, while
0035: Proposition~\ref{prop:blms-obstructs-mean-window} shows that a published
0036: candidate lower bound for \(\omega(F_n)\) would force both H1 and H2 to fail.
0037: None of the
0038: cited primitive-divisor theorems, RH, or ERH currently supplies the required
0039: growing exact-rank distribution estimate.

0001: \begin{theorem}[Multiplicity-free support entropy with arithmetic remainder]
0002: \label{thm:minimal-generator-growth}
0003: For every integer $n\ge3$, put $k=\omega(n)$ and
0004: $L(n)=\log\#\mathcal M_n$. Then $\mathcal M_n$ is nonempty. If $k\ge3$ and
0005: $r=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, then
0006: \begin{equation}\label{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}
0007:  (2^r-1)^{k-r}
0008:  \le \#\mathcal M_n
0009:  \le \sum_{s=1}^{k}\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}.
0010: \end{equation}
0011: In particular, uniformly along every sequence for which $\omega(n)\to\infty$,
0012: \begin{equation}\label{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}
0013:  \frac{\log2}{4}\,\omega(n)^2-O(1)
0014:  \le L(n)
0015:  \le \frac{\log2}{4}\,\omega(n)^2
0016:       +\omega(n)\log R(n)+O(\omega(n)).
0017: \end{equation}
0018: No exact quadratic coefficient for the full quantity $L(n)$ is claimed.
0019: The coefficient $\log2/4$ is exact only for the multiplicity-free
0020: minimal-cover contribution: the lower construction embeds the unweighted
0021: cover count, and the private-coordinate encoding gives the same quadratic
0022: support term in the upper bound. The display is not an asymptotic formula for
0023: $L(n)$ unless $R(n)=\exp(o(\omega(n)))$; no such unconditional estimate for
0024: $R(n)$ is proved here. In particular, the displayed coefficient is not
0025: claimed to be optimal among all deductions from fibotomic or exact-rank
0026: arithmetic information.
0027: 
0028: For comparison, the crude support-count estimate gives
0029: \begin{equation}
0030: \label{eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}
0031:  \#\mathcal M_n
0032:  \le \sum_{r=0}^{k}\binom{\Omega(F_n)}{r}
0033:  \le n^k.
0034: \end{equation}
0035: Combining only the last inequality with the classical maximal order of
0036: $\omega(n)$ gives the crude corollary
0037: \begin{equation}
0038: \label{eq:crude-maximal-order}
0039:  \limsup_{n\to\infty}
0040:  \frac{L(n)\log\log n}{(\log n)^2}\le1.
0041: \end{equation}
0042: This envelope has scale $(\log n)^2/\log\log n$, a factor $\log\log n$
0043: above the witness-cover entropy scale; it is not a consequence of
0044: \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}.
0045: At the coarser divisor-lattice scale, the antichain property and Wigert's
0046: theorem give the Sperner-type envelope
0047: \begin{equation}
0048: \label{eq:sperner-wigert-envelope}
0049:  L(n)\le\log\tau(F_n)
0050:  \le (\log2\,\log\varphi+o(1))\frac{n}{\log n},
0051:  \qquad \varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2};
0052: \end{equation}
0053: in fact \eqref{eq:crude-maximal-order} is stronger and implies
0054: $L(n)=o(n/\log n)$.
0055: 
0056: Moreover, as $x\to\infty$,
0057: \begin{equation}
0058: \label{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}
0059:  \left(\frac{\log2}{4}+o(1)\right)x(\log\log x)^2
0060:  \le \sum_{3\le n\le x}L(n)
0061:  \le (1+o(1))x\log x\,\log\log x.
0062: \end{equation}
0063: 
0064: \end{theorem}

0066: \begin{proof}
0067: First, $F_n\in B_n$ for every $n\ge3$.  Indeed,
0068: $F_n\mid F_d$ implies $F_n\le F_d$, and strict increase of the Fibonacci
0069: sequence from index $2$ onward forces $d\ge n$; hence $\alpha(F_n)=n$.
0070: Because $B_n$ is a nonempty finite poset, it has a minimal element, so
0071: $\mathcal M_n\ne\varnothing$ and $L(n)$ is defined.
0072: 
0073: We first prove the explicit finite private-cover bound in
0074: \eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}. Fix $k\ge3$, and give
0075: $\mathcal P(n)$ an arbitrary order. Put
0076: \[
0077:  X=\mathcal P(n)\cap\{2,3\},\qquad r=\lfloor k/2\rfloor.
0078: \]
0079: Since $k-\#X\ge k-2\ge r$, choose an $r$-element set
0080: $P\subseteq\mathcal P(n)\setminus X$, and put
0081: $Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. For every map
0082: \[
0083:  H:Q\longrightarrow 2^P\setminus\{\varnothing\}
0084: \]
0085: and every $i\in P$, define
0086: \[
0087:  T_i=\{i\}\cup\{q\in Q:i\in H(q)\}.
0088: \]
0089: The index $n_{T_i}=\prod_{\ell\in T_i}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n)}$ has a prime
0090: divisor outside $\{2,3\}$, because $i\in P$. Hence $n_{T_i}\ge5$ and
0091: $n_{T_i}\notin\{6,12\}$. Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors} supplies a
0092: prime $\pi_{T_i}$ with $\alpha(\pi_{T_i})=n_{T_i}$; fix one such prime for
0093: each support that occurs.
0094: 
0095: The supports $T_i$ cover $\mathcal P(n)$ because $H(q)$ is nonempty for every
0096: $q\in Q$. Moreover, $i$ belongs to $T_i$ and to no $T_j$ with $j\ne i$.
0097: Each $\pi_{T_i}$ is a prime jump, so
0098: $E_n(\pi_{T_i})=T_n(\pi_{T_i})=T_i$. Thus
0099: $\{\pi_{T_i}:i\in P\}$ is an $n$-witness cover. Distinct supports have
0100: distinct ranks and therefore distinct underlying primes. If two maps $H$
0101: differ, then their support families differ, since the edge containing the
0102: private coordinate $i$ identifies $T_i$; unique factorization then gives
0103: different minimal generators. There are
0104: $(2^r-1)^{\#Q}=(2^r-1)^{k-r}$ maps $H$, proving the lower bound in
0105: \eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}.
0106: 
0107: For the upper bound, let $\Theta$ be an $n$-witness cover with $s$ rank-jump factors. For
0108: each $\theta\in\Theta$, choose the least coordinate
0109: \[
0110:  x_\theta\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
0111:  \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta\setminus\{\theta\}}T_n(\eta).
0112: \]
0113: These private coordinates are distinct; write
0114: $P=\{x_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ and
0115: $Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. If $x_\theta=x$, then
0116: \[
0117:  T_n(\theta)=\{x\}\cup U_\theta,\qquad U_\theta\subseteq Q,
0118: \]
0119: because every other member of $P$ is private to another rank-jump factor. By the
0120: prime--ladder alternative in Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, either
0121: $E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$ or $E_n(\theta)=\{x\}$. Hence there are at most two
0122: support-pair alternatives, and the definition
0123: \eqref{eq:rank-window-multiplicity} allows at most $R(n)$ rank-jump factors for each.
0124: Thus, once $P$ is fixed, the rank-jump factor indexed by each
0125: $x\in P$ has at most $2R(n)2^{k-s}$ choices. Ignoring coverage and
0126: coprimeness only enlarges the count, so summing over the
0127: $\binom{k}{s}$ possible sets $P$ and over $1\le s\le k$ proves the upper
0128: bound in \eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}.
0129: 
0130: Now $r(k-r)=\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor$ and
0131: $(k-r)\log(1-2^{-r})=O(1)$. Hence the logarithm of the lower bound is
0132: $(\log2)k^2/4+O(1)$. For the upper bound, use
0133: $s(k-s)\le k^2/4$, $s\le k$, and
0134: $\sum_s\binom{k}{s}\le2^k$ to obtain
0135: \[
0136:  \log\sum_{s=1}^{k}\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}
0137:  \le\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+k\log R(n)+O(k).
0138: \]
0139: This proves \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}.
0140: 
0141: Let
0142: \[
0143:  \mathcal Q_n=\{p^e:p\mid F_n,\ 1\le e\le\nu_p(F_n)\}.
0144: \]
0145: This set has cardinality $\Omega(F_n)$.  By unique factorization, the map
0146: \[
0147:  m\longmapsto\{p^{\nu_p(m)}:p\mid m\}
0148: \]
0149: is injective from $\mathcal M_n$ into the subsets of $\mathcal Q_n$.
0150: Corollary~\ref{cor:support-bound} says that every image has at most
0151: $k=\omega(n)$ members.  This proves the first inequality in
0152: \eqref{eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}.
0153: 
0154: Since every prime factor of $F_n$ is at least $2$,
0155: $2^{\Omega(F_n)}\le F_n$.  Also $F_n<2^{n-1}$ for $n\ge3$, by the elementary
0156: induction $F_{j+1}=F_j+F_{j-1}<2^j$.  Hence
0157: $\Omega(F_n)\le n-2$.  A subset of an $N$-element set having at most $k$
0158: members can be encoded injectively by its increasing list padded to length
0159: $k$ with a new symbol; therefore
0160: \[
0161:  \sum_{r=0}^k\binom Nr\le(N+1)^k.
0162: \]
0163: Taking $N=\Omega(F_n)$ gives the second inequality in
0164: \eqref{eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}.
0165: 
0166: The classical maximal-order formula for $\omega(n)$
0167: \cite[Theorem~22.11]{HardyWright2008Introduction}
0168: \[
0169:  \limsup_{n\to\infty}
0170:  \frac{\omega(n)\log\log n}{\log n}=1
0171: \]
0172: now combines with $L(n)\le\omega(n)\log n$ to prove
0173: \eqref{eq:crude-maximal-order}. This argument uses only the crude estimate
0174: $\#\mathcal M_n\le n^{\omega(n)}$, not the witness-cover entropy bound. On
0175: the other hand,
0176: $\mathcal M_n$ is an antichain in the divisor lattice of $F_n$, so
0177: \[
0178:  \#\mathcal M_n\le\widthop(\operatorname{Div}(F_n))\le\tau(F_n).
0179: \]
0180: Wigert's maximal-order theorem \cite{Wigert1907Divisors} states that
0181: \[
0182:  \log\tau(N)\le(\log2+o(1))\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}.
0183: \]
0184: Binet's formula gives $\log F_n=n\log\varphi+O(1)$ and
0185: $\log\log F_n=\log n+O(1)$, yielding
0186: \eqref{eq:sperner-wigert-envelope}.  Finally,
0187: $(\log n)^2/\log\log n=o(n/\log n)$, so
0188: \eqref{eq:crude-maximal-order} gives the stated strict improvement.
0189: 
0190: For the mean upper bound, use the classical mean-value estimate
0191: \cite{HardyRamanujan1917NormalPrimeFactors}
0192: \begin{equation}
0193: \label{eq:mean-omega-input}
0194:  \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)=x\log\log x+O(x),
0195: \end{equation}
0196: together with $L(n)\le\omega(n)\log n$.  Uniformly for $n\le x$,
0197: $\log n\le\log x$, and hence
0198: \[
0199:  \sum_{3\le n\le x}L(n)
0200:  \le\log x\sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)
0201:  =(1+o(1))x\log x\,\log\log x.
0202: \]
0203: 
0204: Tur\'an's second-moment form of the Hardy--Ramanujan theorem
0205: \cite{Turan1934HardyRamanujan} gives
0206: \begin{equation}\label{eq:omega-second-moment}
0207:  \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)^2=(1+o(1))x(\log\log x)^2.
0208: \end{equation}
0209: After enlarging the absolute constant in the lower half of
0210: \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}, it holds as
0211: $L(n)\ge(\log2)\omega(n)^2/4-O(1)$ also for $\omega(n)<3$.
0212: Summation and \eqref{eq:omega-second-moment} prove the lower half of
0213: \eqref{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth} and complete the proof.
0214: \end{proof}

0151: The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
0152: \cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
0153: polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
0154: \cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
0155: Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
0156: \cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
0157: definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
0158: Thus $\Psi_d(1)$ is the standard Fibonacci cyclotomic, or fibotomic,
0159: integer; only the notation $\mathfrak F_d$ below is local to this paper.

0161: \begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
0162: \label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
0163: Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
0164: \[
0165:  \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
0166: \]
0167: Then
0168: \begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
0169:  \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
0170: \end{equation}
0171: and
0172: \begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
0173:  \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
0174: \end{equation}
0175: For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
0176: $d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
0177: is $1$.
0178: \end{lemma}
0179: 
0180: \begin{proof}
0181: The polynomial factorization
0182: \[
0183:  F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
0184: \]
0185: and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
0186: functions give
0187: \[
0188:  \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
0189: \]
0190: Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
0191: $\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
0192: value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
0193: negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
0194: 
0195: If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
0196: divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
0197: $F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
0198: $p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
0199: $\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
0200: exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
0201: any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
0202: follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
0203: primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
0204: \end{proof}

0206: \begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
0207: \label{thm:fibotomic-rank-entropy}
0208: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, let $\phi_{\rm E}$ denote Euler's totient
0209: function, and, for $d\geq3$, put
0210: \[
0211:  \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
0212: \]
0213: For $k\geq0$, set $m=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ and
0214: \[
0215:  \mathcal H_d(k):=
0216:  k\log\frac{2d}{3}+2\log(m!)+(k-2m)\log(m+1).
0217: \]
0218: There is an absolute constant $C_F$ such that, for every $d\geq3$,
0219: \begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy}
0220:  \mathcal H_d(a(d))\leq \phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi+C_F.
0221: \end{equation}
0222: More generally, every finitely supported family of nonnegative real numbers
0223: $(\lambda_d)_{d\geq3}$ satisfies
0224: \begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-fibotomic-rank-entropy}
0225:  \sum_{d\geq3}\lambda_d\mathcal H_d(a(d))
0226:  \leq (\log\varphi)\sum_{d\geq3}\lambda_d\phi_{\rm E}(d)
0227:        +C_F\sum_{d\geq3}\lambda_d.
0228: \end{equation}
0229: Uniformly as $d\to\infty$,
0230: \begin{equation}\label{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound}
0231:  a(d)\leq
0232:  \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
0233:  \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(d)}{\log d}.
0234: \end{equation}
0235: Consequently, uniformly as $n\to\infty$,
0236: \begin{equation}\label{eq:visible-exact-rank-bound}
0237:  A^*(n)\leq
0238:  \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
0239:  \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{\log n}.
0240: \end{equation}
0241: \end{theorem}
0242: 
0243: \begin{proof}
0244: Binet's formula, in the form
0245: \[
0246:  F_r=\frac{\varphi^r}{\sqrt5}
0247:  \bigl(1-(-\varphi^{-2})^r\bigr),
0248: \]
0249: and the identities
0250: $\sum_{r\mid d}\mu(d/r)=0$ and
0251: $\sum_{r\mid d}r\mu(d/r)=\phi_{\rm E}(d)$ show that
0252: \begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-binet-error}
0253:  \log\mathfrak F_d=\phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi+E_d,
0254:  \qquad
0255:  |E_d|\leq
0256:  C_F:=\sum_{j\geq1}
0257:  \left|\log\bigl(1-(-\varphi^{-2})^j\bigr)\right|.
0258: \end{equation}
0259: The series defining $C_F$ converges geometrically.
0260: 
0261: Lemma~\ref{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical} gives the exact-rank radical
0262: divisibility with no cancellation ambiguity.
0263: For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, the classical rank congruence gives
0264: \[
0265:  d=\alpha(p)\mid p-\left(\frac5p\right),
0266: \]
0267: see \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm,Vinson1963RankApparition}. Thus
0268: $p\equiv\pm1\pmod d$. The ranks $d=3,5$ have respectively the single
0269: exact-rank primes $2,5$ and satisfy the estimate directly; the layers
0270: $d=6,12$ are empty and also satisfy it. For every remaining $d$, write the
0271: exact-rank primes in increasing order as
0272: $p_1<\cdots<p_k$. There are at most two candidates in each pair of residue
0273: classes $jd\pm1$, whence
0274: \[
0275:  p_i\geq d\left\lceil\frac i2\right\rceil-1
0276:  \geq\frac{2d}{3}\left\lceil\frac i2\right\rceil.
0277: \]
0278: It follows that, with $m=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$,
0279: \begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-congruence-product-bound}
0280:  \prod_{i=1}^kp_i\geq
0281:  \left(\frac{2d}{3}\right)^k(m!)^2(m+1)^{k-2m}.
0282: \end{equation}
0283: Combining \eqref{eq:fibotomic-binet-error}--
0284: \eqref{eq:rank-congruence-product-bound} and taking logarithms proves
0285: \eqref{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy}. Multiplication by $\lambda_d\geq0$ and
0286: finite summation proves \eqref{eq:weighted-fibotomic-rank-entropy}.
0287: 
0288: Stirling's lower bound applied in \eqref{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy} gives,
0289: with an absolute implied constant,
0290: \begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-entropy-coarse}
0291:  a(d)\bigl(\log d+\log\max\{1,a(d)\}-O(1)\bigr)
0292:  \leq \phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi+O(1).
0293: \end{equation}
0294: Fix $\varepsilon>0$. If $a(d)\leq\phi_{\rm E}(d)/(\log d)^2$, then
0295: \eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} follows immediately. Otherwise the
0296: standard uniform lower bound
0297: $\phi_{\rm E}(d)\gg d/\log\log(3d)$
0298: \cite{HardyWright2008Introduction} implies
0299: \[
0300:  \log a(d)=\log d+O(\log\log d)=\log d+o(\log d).
0301: \]
0302: Substitution in \eqref{eq:rank-entropy-coarse} yields, for all sufficiently
0303: large $d$ depending only on $\varepsilon$,
0304: $(2+o(1))a(d)\log d\leq\phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi$, proving
0305: \eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} with its $o(1)$ uniform over every
0306: $d$ beyond that threshold.
0307: 
0308: For \eqref{eq:visible-exact-rank-bound}, the case $A^*(n)=1$ follows from
0309: $\phi_{\rm E}(n)/\log n\to\infty$. Otherwise choose
0310: $d_n\in\mathcal D^+(n)$ with $A^*(n)=a(d_n)$. The preceding estimate has
0311: the coarse consequence $a(d)\ll d/\log(2d)$. If
0312: $d_n\leq n/(\log n)^3$, the lower bound for $\phi_{\rm E}(n)$ gives
0313: \[
0314:  a(d_n)=o\left(\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{\log n}\right).
0315: \]
0316: If $d_n>n/(\log n)^3$, then
0317: $\log d_n=(1+o(1))\log n$ and, since $d_n\mid n$,
0318: $\phi_{\rm E}(d_n)\leq\phi_{\rm E}(n)$. Applying
0319: \eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} at $d_n$ completes the proof. The two
0320: cases use thresholds depending only on $\varepsilon$, so the final $o(1)$ is
0321: uniform over all $n$ beyond a common threshold.
0322: \end{proof}

0001: # Reproducing the finite computations
0002: 
0003: This directory is the computational supplement for the manuscript. All
0004: integer arithmetic is exact. The verification was run with:
0005: 
0006: - Python 3.10.11;
0007: - SymPy 1.13.1;
0008: - SymPy's `factorint` integer-factorization routine.
0009: 
0010: The factorization cost is not part of any theorem or complexity claim. The
0011: archive `fibonacci_factorizations_2_210.tsv` records every exact factorization
0012: of `F_n` used for `2 <= n <= 210`; the verifier checks that every row
0013: multiplies back to the stated Fibonacci number.
0014: 
0015: ## Files
0016: 
0017: - `compute_birth_layer_table.py`: exhaustive divisor/rank enumeration for
0018:   `2 <= n <= 30` and generation of the TeX table.
0019: - `verify_finite_claims.py`: independent direct and structural computations,
0020:   finite-bound checks, exact minimal-cover and connected-cover enumeration,
0021:   theta-normalized and discrete local-limit checks, rank-pure sector checks,
0022:   exact total and connected support-spectrum checks and the extremal
0023:   atomic-product count,

0025:   weighted rank-pure product membership and the strict ladder example at
0026:   `n=91`, refined
0027:   private-coordinate upper bounds, fibotomic rank-entropy and exact-rank
0028:   radical checks, the finite Jarden consequence, exact-rank prime existence
0029:   through rank 210, a prime inverse-ray prefix, the exceptional path to the
0030:   fixed point 12, environment reporting, and
0031:   factorization-archive generation and validation.
0032: - `test_verify_finite_claims.py`: unit tests for the arithmetic routines,
0033:   finite bounds, archive round trip, and report contents.
0034: - `../scripts/verify_deepening_delta.py`: independent legacy verification
0035:   battery for the finite upper-fiber and growth-law checks.

0061: ## Commands
0062: 
0063: Run these commands from the manuscript directory:
0064: 
0065: ```powershell
0066: python -m unittest discover -s artifacts -p "test_verify_finite_claims.py" -v
0067: Push-Location scripts; python -m unittest -v test_verify_squarefree_slice.py; Pop-Location

0072: ```
0073: 
0074: The first verification route enumerates every divisor of `F_n`, computes its
0075: rank directly, and minimizes the resulting birth layer. On `2 <= n <= 60`,
0076: the second route constructs the upper fiber from the maximal proper Fibonacci
0077: divisors and constructs the minimal elements from the witness threshold
0078: conditions. The report compares the actual sets, not only their cardinalities:
0079: 
0080: ```text
0081: B_n direct = B_n upper fiber: 59/59 set equalities
0082: M_n direct = M_n witness: 59/59 set equalities
0083: ```
0084: 
0085: For `61 <= n <= 210`, the structural route checks the stated finite upper and
0086: lower bounds. On every layer `3 <= n <= 210`, it also enumerates the rank-pure
0087: sector (all layers in this range have at most four prime coordinates), checks
0088: the exact-rank-prime Mobius formula on every nonempty support, and verifies that
0089: every canonical and weighted rank-pure product belongs to the independently
0090: constructed minimal-generator set. It also confirms that the rank-pure sector
0091: is strict at `n=91`, where `169` is a ladder generator. The exact
0092: Hearne--Wagner and connected-cover counts are
0093: cross-checked against direct cover enumeration for `1 <= k <= 4`. Exact counts
0094: through `k=80` also check convergence to the parity-dependent theta
0095: normalization, the connected-cover ratio, and the central discrete local
0096: limit. On every `3 <= n <= 210` layer the report also checks the pointwise
0097: rank-window deaggregation inequalities and the refined private-coordinate
0098: upper bound; on every squarefree layer it checks the exact-rank partition and
0099: the BLMS pigeonhole inequality. It also reconstructs the fibotomic integer on
0100: every rank in this range, verifies its exact-rank radical divisibility and the
0101: rank-congruence spacing used in the entropy bound, and checks `a(10p) >= 2`
0102: for the five eligible prime values with `10p <= 210`. In addition, it extracts
0103: the positive-coordinate rank hypergraph of every minimal generator, verifies
0104: the total and connected support spectra on all 208 layers, and checks that the
0105: top-support slice has the product cardinality of its singleton diagonal atomic
0106: families. It confirms that the only empty exact-rank prime fibers on
0107: `3 <= d <= 210` are `d=6,12`, verifies
0108: `7 <- 13 <- 233 <- 139801`, and checks `7 -> 8 -> 6 -> 12` by direct modular
0109: rank computation. These finite checks support, but do not prove, the infinite
0110: inverse-ray theorem; infinitude uses the classical exact-rank existence
0111: theorem. These finite checks do not resolve the
0112: asymptotic behavior of `R(n)`, establish (H2) or (BW), or compare the total
0113: connected and disconnected arithmetic sectors without those hypotheses.
0114: 
0115: The squarefree-slice verifier independently enumerates all irredundant covers
0116: for `1 <= k <= 4`, checks 36 exact full-support equality profiles for the
0117: sharp weighted-cover lower bound, and compares direct rank-pure products with
0118: the squarefree elements of the independently constructed `M_n` for every
0119: squarefree `3 <= n <= 210`. The stored run contains 127 set equalities and 427
0120: squarefree minimal generators. These checks do not show that the abstract
0121: fixed-total extremizer is realizable by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.

0001: \section{Numerical evidence}\label{sec:numerical}
0002: %% ====================================================================
0003: 
0004: Table~\ref{tab:birth-layer-data-generated} displays the rank level set cardinality $A(n)$
0005: and the number of minimal generators $\#\mathcal M_n$ for $2\le n\le 30$,
0006: computed by exhaustive enumeration. The table is illustrative only: the
0007: unconditional inequalities in Theorem~\ref{article-thm:minimal-generator-growth} do
0008: not rely on this finite sample. Several features visible in the
0009: data agree with the structural results of the preceding sections.
0010: First, $\#\mathcal M_n=1$ whenever $\omega(n)=1$ and
0011: $n\notin\{19,25,27\}$; the exceptions arise from composite Fibonacci numbers
0012: with multiple rank-jump families at the same prime-power index.
0013: Second, the jump at $n=12$ ($A(12)=10$, $\#\mathcal M_{12}=3$) and at $n=24$
0014: ($A(24)=55$, $\#\mathcal M_{24}=4$) reflects the interaction of the
0015: exceptional prime $2$ with the layers having no exact-rank prime at indices
0016: $6$ and $12$.
0017: Third, the first nonempty three-coordinate layer occurs at $n=30$ and has
0018: $\#\mathcal M_{30}=5$; the displayed witness covers realize exactly the
0019: types $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_4$, $\Gamma_5$, $\Gamma_7$, and $\Gamma_8$.
0020: The remaining admissible shapes $\Gamma_3$, $\Gamma_6$, and $\Gamma_9$ are
0021: not realized at $n=30$. This exact five-type assertion, including the three
0022: nonrealization proofs, is Proposition~\ref{prop:n30-five-type-classification};
0023: it is not inferred from the table.
0024: 
0025: The table was produced by the finite divisor/rank computation in the next
0026: proposition, applied exhaustively for $2\le n\le30$.  The manuscript source
0027: includes the short script that performs this enumeration and the generated
0028: table file input below; these files are supplementary to the mathematical
0029: criterion rather than part of the theorem stream. For the classical
0030: factorization literature, see the tables of Brillhart--Montgomery--Silverman
0031: \cite{BrillhartMontgomerySilverman1988Tables}.
0032: 
0033: \begin{proposition}[Finite divisor/rank verification with supplied factorization]
0034: \label{prop:effective-birth-layer-computation}
0035: Let $n\ge2$ and suppose the integer factorization of $F_n$ is known. Then
0036: $B_n$, $A(n)$, and $\mathcal M_n$ are recovered exactly by the following finite
0037: divisor/rank test.
0038: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
0039: \item Enumerate the divisor set $D_n=\operatorname{Div}(F_n)$ from the
0040:  factorization of $F_n$.
0041: \item Enumerate the divisor set $\operatorname{Div}(n)$. For each
0042:  $q\in D_n$, compute
0043:  \[
0044:  \alpha_n(q):=\min\{d\mid n:q\mid F_d\}.
0045:  \]
0046: \item Set $B_n=\{q\in D_n:q\ge2,\ \alpha_n(q)=n\}$ and
0047:  $A(n)=\#B_n$.
0048: \item Sort $B_n$ by divisibility-compatible order, for instance by size, and
0049:  retain exactly those $m\in B_n$ for which no previously retained element
0050:  divides $m$; the retained set is $\mathcal M_n$.
0051: \end{enumerate}
0052: \end{proposition}
0053: 
0054: \begin{proof}
0055: Since every $q\in D_n$ divides $F_n$, Proposition~\ref{article-prop:rank-basics}
0056: shows that $q\mid F_d$ for some $d$ if and only if $\alpha(q)\mid d$. In
0057: particular $q\mid F_n$ implies $\alpha(q)\mid n$, so the least positive index
0058: at which $q$ appears is exactly
0059: \[
0060: \alpha(q)=\min\{d\mid n:q\mid F_d\}=\alpha_n(q).
0061: \]
0062: Hence the test in step (c) gives precisely the definition
0063: $B_n=\{q\in D_n:\alpha(q)=n\}$, with the harmless exclusion of $q=1$ already
0064: consistent with the convention $\alpha(1)=1$ and $n\ge2$. Counting this set
0065: gives $A(n)$.
0066: 
0067: It remains to justify step (d). The set $B_n$ is finite. If its elements are
0068: processed in increasing size, then every proper divisor of the current element
0069: has already been processed. We claim inductively that every discarded element
0070: has a retained minimal divisor. The claim is vacuous before the first element.
0071: If the current element is discarded, it has a previously retained divisor by
0072: the algorithm, so the claim holds for it; if it is retained, it is its own
0073: retained divisor. Thus every earlier divisor, retained or discarded, has a
0074: retained divisor below it. Consequently the current element is retained if and
0075: only if no smaller element of $B_n$ divides it, which is exactly minimality in
0076: the divisibility poset. The retained set is therefore $\mathcal M_n$.
0077: \end{proof}
0078: 
0079: \begin{remark}[Reproducibility scope]
0080: The preceding proposition is used only to document the finite verification
0081: interface for the table, not as a complexity theorem.  After the factorization
0082: of $F_n$ has been supplied, the displayed loops involve only the finite divisor
0083: sets of $F_n$ and $n$, ordinary divisibility tests $q\mid F_d$, and divisor
0084: comparisons inside $B_n$.  The manuscript makes no bit-complexity assertion and
0085: does not include the cost of factoring $F_n$ in the numerical evidence.
0086: \end{remark}
0087:

0089: The reproducibility files
0090: \[
0091: \text{\texttt{artifacts/compute\_birth\_layer\_table.py}},\qquad
0092: \text{\texttt{artifacts/tab\_birth\_layer\_data.tex}}
0093: \]
0094: are included with the manuscript source. Running the command in
0095: \texttt{artifacts/REPRODUCE.md}
0096: \[
0097: \texttt{python artifacts/compute\_birth\_layer\_table.py}
0098: \]
0099: regenerates the table input from the divisor/rank method of
0100: Proposition~\ref{prop:effective-birth-layer-computation}.  The printed table is
0101: therefore an exhaustive enumeration of $A(n)$ and $\#\mathcal M_n$ for
0102: $2\le n\le30$ using only the finite tests proved above; the displayed
0103: factorizations of the small integers $F_n$ are produced by the script's exact
0104: integer trial-division routine. Its complete console output is supplied as
0105: \path{artifacts/birth_layer_table_output.txt}.
0106: \input{generated/tab_birth_layer_data.tex}

0108: \paragraph{Finite verification.}
0109: The supplementary script
0110: \texttt{artifacts/verify\_finite\_claims.py} independently compares the actual
0111: sets obtained by direct divisor/rank enumeration with the upper-fiber and
0112: witness constructions through $n=60$. It
0113: then uses the latter formula through $n=210$: inclusion--exclusion computes
0114: \[
0115:  A(n)=\sum_{S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}(-1)^{|S|}
0116:  \tau\!\left(F_{n/\prod_{p\in S}p}\right),
0117: \]
0118: and the minimal threshold covers of the conditions
0119: $q\nmid F_{n/p}$ compute $\mathcal M_n$.  The script checks
0120: \eqref{article-eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}, the simplified bound
0121: $\#\mathcal M_n\le n^{\omega(n)}$, the odd Bell lower bound, and both finite
0122: private-cover bounds in \eqref{article-eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}. It also
0123: computes $R(n)$, checks the pointwise deaggregation bounds
0124: \eqref{article-eq:prime-window-versus-R} and
0125: \eqref{article-eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}, verifies the exact-rank partition
0126: and \eqref{article-eq:squarefree-blms-pigeonhole} on every squarefree layer, checks
0127: the refined upper bound \eqref{eq:refined-private-coordinate-upper-bound},
0128: checks the fibotomic identities \eqref{article-eq:fibotomic-binet-error} and
0129: \eqref{article-eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}, the entropy inequality
0130: \eqref{article-eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy}, the exact-rank congruence candidate bound,
0131: and the available cases of \eqref{eq:jarden-exact-rank-consequence}, and
0132: records the running ratio against the support-entropy scale
0133: $(\log2)\omega(n)^2/4$. For the rank-pure results, it directly enumerates all
0134: minimal covers for $k\le4$, checks the Hearne--Wagner and connected-component
0135: counts, verifies the M\"obius exact-rank-prime formula on every support, and
0136: tests every canonical rank-pure product against the independently computed
0137: $\mathcal M_n$. This covers all $208$ layers $3\le n\le210$, including exact
0138: realization of every minimal cover on all $104$ odd layers. It reports $59/59$
0139: set equalities for both original comparisons and no finite-bound or rank-pure
0140: failures. On the same $208$ layers it computes the exact total and connected
0141: support spectra from the rank-support hypergraphs and checks both cases of
0142: Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-support-spectra}, as well as the rank-jump product
0143: formula for the extremal slice. The exact output is
0144: \path{artifacts/finite_verification.txt}. The exact factorizations used for
0145: $2\le n\le210$ are recorded in
0146: \path{artifacts/fibonacci_factorizations_2_210.tsv}; the verifier checks
0147: every row by multiplication. The Python and SymPy versions, commands, file
0148: inventory, and verification scope are in \path{artifacts/REPRODUCE.md}, and
0149: \path{artifacts/SHA256SUMS} authenticates the supplied files. These finite
0150: checks do not provide distributional control of $R(n)$.
0151: In particular, they do not prove the asymptotic hypotheses \textup{(H2)} or
0152: \textup{(BW)}.

0001: \section{Finite verification for the three-coordinate table}
0002: \label{app:three-coordinate-checklist}
0003: 
0004: \begin{proposition}[Reader's checklist for the three-coordinate table]
0005: \label{prop:three-coordinate-table-checklist}
0006: Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,
0007: \ell_2,\ell_3\}$.  The following finite procedure returns exactly
0008: $\mathcal M_n$.
0009: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
0010: \item For every nonempty $J\subseteq[3]$, compute the exact-rank window
0011: $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ and the rank classes
0012: $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ for $d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ by
0013: Lemma~\ref{article-lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}. This gives every prime
0014: slot $P_J(n)$.
0015: \item For each coordinate $i$, compute the single possible ladder candidate
0016: $\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ from
0017: Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}, then retain it in
0018: $L_{i,J}(n)$ exactly for those $J$ for which its rank divides $n$ and has
0019: full-coordinate set $J$.
0020: \item For each coordinate permutation of each of the eight rows in
0021: Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}, replace the displayed slots
0022: by the finite sets found in (i) and (ii), with
0023: $S_i(n)=P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n)$.
0024: \item Keep precisely those row fillings whose selected prime powers have
0025: distinct underlying primes, equivalently those satisfying the Hall
0026: inequalities in Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection}; multiply the selected
0027: prime powers and insert the product into a set, thereby removing repetitions
0028: caused by stabilizers and coordinate permutations.
0029: \end{enumerate}
0030: The products retained in (iv) are exactly the minimal generators listed in
0031: Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.  In particular, the
0032: table is a closed finite classification for fixed $n$, not an interface to an
0033: additional infinite search.
0034: \end{proposition}
0035: 
0036: \begin{proof}
0037: Step (i) is precisely the prime-slot identity in
0038: Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}; the M\"obius formula
0039: there is Lemma~\ref{article-lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}.  Step (ii) is the
0040: ladder-slot identity in the same proposition, which says that every
0041: $L_{i,J}(n)$ is empty or consists of the displayed single candidate.  Step
0042: (iii) is only the coordinate-labelling convention of
0043: Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness}.  By that theorem, after the
0044: slots of a labelled row are replaced by their finite admissible sets, a row
0045: realizes a minimal generator if and only if the slot-selection test in step
0046: (iv) succeeds; Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} is exactly the stated
0047: Hall criterion for distinct underlying primes.  The one-factor rows
0048: $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_3$ are the rank-jump generators with full
0049: three-coordinate support.  Conversely, every minimal generator with
0050: three-coordinate support has, by
0051: Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-realization}, one fixed labelled
0052: coordinate permutation of one of the eight row types and therefore appears in
0053: this procedure. The labelled rank-jump factor set is unique, whereas the
0054: unlabelled row is an $S_3$-orbit; the set insertion in step (iv) prevents the
0055: raw permuted enumeration from asserting stronger uniqueness.
0056: \end{proof}
0057: 
0058: \begin{example}[Applying the checklist at $n=42$]
0059: \label{ex:n42-three-coordinate-checklist}
0060: Let $n=42=2\cdot3\cdot7$ and label the coordinates by
0061: $(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)=(2,3,7)$.  The prime factors of
0062: \[
0063: F_{42}=2^3\cdot13\cdot29\cdot211\cdot421
0064: \]
0065: have ranks
0066: \[
0067: \alpha(2)=3,
0068: \alpha(4)=6,
0069: \alpha(13)=7,
0070: \alpha(29)=14,
0071: \alpha(421)=21,
0072: \alpha(211)=42.
0073: \]
0074: Thus $\Atom(42)=\{211\}$. The exact-rank windows used below are
0075: $P_{12}(42)=\varnothing$, $P_{13}(42)=\{29\}$,
0076: $P_{23}(42)=\{421\}$, and $P_{123}(42)=\{211\}$.  Singleton slots are
0077: $S_1(42)=\varnothing$, $S_2(42)=\{2\}$, and $S_3(42)=\{13\}$.  The proper
0078: ladder slots relevant here are
0079: $L_{1,12}(42)=\{4\}$, $L_{1,123}(42)=\varnothing$,
0080: $L_{2,J}(42)=\varnothing$, and $L_{3,J}(42)=\varnothing$.
0081: 
0082: The table then gives the following non-rank-jump generators.  The row
0083: $\Gamma_4$ with the permuted slots $P_{13}$ and $P_{23}$ gives
0084: $29\cdot421=12209$.  The row $\Gamma_5$ gives
0085: $4\cdot421=1684$ from $L_{1,12}$ and $P_{23}$, while the analogous
0086: coordinate permutation with an exact-rank $P_{13}$ partner is not a row of type
0087: $\Gamma_5$ for this ladder orientation.  The row $\Gamma_7$ gives
0088: $2\cdot29=58$ from $S_2$ and $P_{13}$ after relabeling.  The row $\Gamma_8$
0089: gives $13\cdot4=52$ from $S_3$ and the permuted ladder slot $L_{1,12}$.
0090: All other rows fail because one of the required slots is empty.  Hence
0091: \[
0092: \mathcal M_{42}=\{52,58,211,1684,12209\}.
0093: \]
0094: The example illustrates the theorem's reading rule: every success or failure
0095: is decided by a finite slot list and a coprimeness check.
0096: \end{example}

-\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}
-%% ====================================================================
-
-For an integer $q\ge1$, the \emph{rank of apparition} (or \emph{order of
-appearance}) $\alpha(q)$ is the least positive index $r$ such that $q\mid
-F_r$, where $F_0=0$ and $F_1=1$.  The existence of this index is recalled in
-Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-rank}.  We use the conventions $\alpha(1)=1$ and
-$D_1=\operatorname{Div}(F_1)=\{1\}$.  For $n\ge2$, write
-\[
- D_n:=\operatorname{Div}(F_n),\qquad
- B_n:=\{q\in D_n:\alpha(q)=n\},\qquad
- \mathcal M_n:=\min_{\mid} B_n .
-\]
-The rank divisibility criterion gives $B_n=\alpha^{-1}(n)$. Thus $B_n$ is
-the ordinary level set, or exact preimage, of $n$ under the rank map,
-equivalently the set
-of moduli that first divide a Fibonacci number at index $n$, and
-$\mathcal M_n$ is obtained by the generic poset operation of taking its
-divisibility-minimal elements.
-The boundary layer is empty: $B_2=\mathcal M_2=\varnothing$.  Throughout,
-$\log$ is natural, $\mathcal P(n)$ is the set of prime divisors of $n$,
-$\omega(n)=\#\mathcal P(n)$, and $\Omega(n)$ counts prime factors with
-multiplicity.
-
-\subsection*{Prior work and novelty boundary}
-
-The cardinality of $B_n$ is contained in Stroi\'nski's general
-$\alpha$-contraction formalism \cite{Stroinski2016AlphaContraction}; classical
-M\"obius identities for Fibonacci divisibility appear in
-\cite{Halton1966DivisibilityFibonacci,FultonMorris1969ArithmeticalFunctions}.
-For primes, nearby arithmetic-distribution results are due to Kiss. His 1987
-paper connects an almost-all upper hypothesis for greatest primitive divisors
-to Wieferich-type divisors \cite{Kiss1987WieferichLucas}; his 1988 work treats
-primitive divisors and accumulated primitive parts
-\cite{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}, while his paper on ranks of apparition of
-primes in Lucas sequences bounds averages of $\alpha(p)/p$
-\cite{Kiss1989RankApparition}.  These results, and Stroi\'nski's cumulative
-bound for primes with bounded rank, do not give upper-distribution estimates
-for the growing exact fibers
-\[
- \Pi_\alpha(d):=\{p\text{ prime}:\alpha(p)=d\},\qquad
- a(d):=\#\Pi_\alpha(d).
-\]
-The distinction between cumulative rank estimates and the individual
-multiplicities $a(d)$ is decisive below.
-
-The nearest structural predecessor is Wagner's theory of minimal
-multiplicative covers of an integer \cite{Wagner1978MultiplicativeCovers}.
-Wagner studies divisor tuples $(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$ with lcm $n$ such that the
-lcm becomes smaller when any one component is deleted, and presents them as
-the multiplicative generalization of the minimal covers of finite sets studied
-by Hearne--Wagner \cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}. Proposition~
-\ref{prop:wagner-comparison} proves the exact comparison. When all rank-jump factors are
-prime, $d^-(p)=1$ and our witness condition is Wagner's condition after
-forgetting tuple order. A ladder jump has nontrivial $d^-(p^e)$, so deletion
-is replaced by lowering one label. The contributions here are this
-Fibonacci-decorated predecessor version of standard join irredundance, its
-correspondence with
-$\mathcal M_n$, the canonical squarefree slice, and the exact arithmetic
-weights. The classical minimal-cover skeleton itself is not new.
-
-Other nearby work studies different aspects of the order-of-appearance map.
-Luca and Pomerance study its local behavior under additive shifts
-\cite{LucaPomerance2014LocalBehavior}; Trojovsk\'a and
-FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga study periodic points and dynamics
-\cite{Trojovska2020PeriodicPoints,
-FitzGibbonsJavaheriMillerVerga2025Dynamics}; and Sanna gives distribution
-theorems for rank divisibility and, under GRH, fixed indices of appearance
-\cite{Sanna2022RankDivisibility,Sanna2024IndexAppearance}. Cera Da
-Concei\c c\~ao subsequently gives explicit densities for fixed rank
-divisibility for all Lucas sequences and all fixed divisors
-\cite{CeraDaConceicao2026PrimeDensities}. Rank divisibility
-$d\mid\alpha(p)$ does not isolate $\alpha(p)=d$, and the fixed-index theorem
-does not provide the growing exact-fiber uniformity required here.
-
-FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga ask whether, for each $k\geq1$, there
-are infinitely many relatively prime integers of fixed-point order $k$, and
-conjecture that the basin of each fixed point $x>5$ contains infinitely many
-relatively prime integers.  Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays} constructs
-infinite prime inverse rays.  Corollaries~\ref{cor:prime-fixed-order} and
-\ref{cor:prime-basins} answer both questions in the stronger prime form.  The
-argument is a direct application of exact-rank prime existence and does not
-use the weighted-cover theory.
-
-The structural starting points of this paper are classical:
-\[
- q\mid F_m\Longleftrightarrow\alpha(q)\mid m,\qquad
- \gcd(F_r,F_s)=F_{\gcd(r,s)},
-\]
-and
-\[
- \alpha(\operatorname{lcm}(u,v))
- =\operatorname{lcm}(\alpha(u),\alpha(v)).
-\]
-See \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm,Vinson1963RankApparition}; Luca--Tron record
-the last identity for Fibonacci numbers \cite{LucaTron2015SelfFibonacciDivisors},
-and Renault proves it for the more general $(a,b)$-Fibonacci sequence
-\cite{Renault2013PeriodRankOrder}. Exact-rank prime existence is supplied by
-Carmichael and Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier
-\cite{Carmichael1913PrimitiveDivisors,
-BiluHanrotVoutier2001PrimitiveDivisorsLucas}.  The upper-set identity,
-coordinatewise lcm test, prime-power lifting formulas, and private-coordinate
-injection are consequences of these inputs.  We record them as lemmas and do
-not claim them as independent arithmetic advances.
-
-\subsection*{The reduction to a weighted arithmetic problem}
-
-For a prime power $\theta=p^e$, call $\theta$ rank-jump when lowering it to
-$p^{e-1}$ lowers its rank.  Relative to $n$, its rank has a full-coordinate
-support $T_n(\theta)$ and an essential support $E_n(\theta)$, the coordinates
-lost on lowering.  An $n$-witness cover is a pairwise coprime collection of
-rank-jump prime powers whose full supports cover $\mathcal P(n)$ and in which
-each factor has an
-essential coordinate absent from all other full supports.
-
-\begin{previewtheorem}[Witness-cover classification]
-Multiplication is a bijection from $n$-witness covers to $\mathcal M_n$.
-Consequently every $m\in\mathcal M_n$ has a unique rank-jump factorization and
-\[
- \omega(m)\le\omega(n).
-\]
-\end{previewtheorem}
-
-This is Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification}.  Its uniqueness is the usual
-unique factorization in $\mathbb Z$; the nontrivial content is the admissibility
-test identifying which prime-power factor sets occur. The classification turns the
-counting problem into a minimal-cover problem, but it does not erase the
-number of primes available at each exact rank.  The following result gives a
-necessary weighted obstruction on a positive-density family.
-
-\begin{previewtheorem}[Weighted odd-layer obstruction]
-Let $n\ge3$ be odd, set $V=\mathcal P(n)$, and for
-$\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V$ put
-$n_S=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n)}$.  If
-$\operatorname{MinCov}(V)$ denotes the irredundant covers of $V$ by nonempty
-subsets, then
-\[
- \sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
- \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}a(n_S)
- \le\#\mathcal M_n.
-\]
-\end{previewtheorem}
-
-The general rank-pure embedding is
-Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-pure-universality}, and the displayed obstruction is
-Corollary~\ref{cor:odd-weighted-cover-obstruction}.  The sum is the exact
-cardinality of an explicit rank-pure sector. Corollary~
-\ref{cor:rank-pure-minimal-transversals} encodes it as the minimal-transversal
-count of a canonical coordinate hypergraph, and the associated split graph is
-the standard split-incidence encoding. No theorem about arbitrary
-transversals or split graphs is claimed. More arithmetically, on every
-squarefree index Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} identifies
-that sector with the divisibility-minimal squarefree part of
-$\alpha^{-1}(n)$. Thus the weighted cover polynomial counts standard
-transversal objects and a standard slice of the exact fiber, not merely an
-auxiliary family. Any upper equivalent for
-$\#\mathcal M_n$ must control it. It need not exhaust the full fiber:
-$\alpha(13)=7$ and $\alpha(13^2)=91$, so the odd squarefree layer $91$ already
-has the ladder generator $169$ outside the rank-pure sector.
-
-Let $C_k$ be the number of irredundant covers of a labelled $k$-set.
-Hearne--Wagner give its exact enumeration
-\cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}. Lemma~
-\ref{lem:labelled-minimal-cover-comparison} compares that labelled formula
-directly with the labelled central sum in the split-graph asymptotics of
-Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka, giving
-\[
- \log C_k=\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+O(k)
-\]
-\cite{BenderRichmondWormald1985ChordalSplit,Troyka2019SplitGraphs}. This count
-does not use Royle's correspondence between unlabelled isomorphism types. For odd
-$n$, define the normalized weighted excess
-\[
- \mathcal W(n):=\frac1{C_{\omega(n)}}
- \sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(\mathcal P(n))}
- \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}a(n_S).
-\]
-Then the rank-pure sector satisfies
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-weighted-lower-bound}
- \log\#\mathcal M_n
- \ge\frac{\log2}{4}\omega(n)^2+\log\mathcal W(n)+O(\omega(n)).
-\end{equation}
-
-Since odd integers have positive density and
-$\omega(n)\sim\log\log n$ for almost all of them, the proposed tier-up theorem
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:target-normal-order}
- \log\#\mathcal M_n\sim
- \frac{\log2}{4}(\log\log n)^2
- \qquad\text{for almost all }n
-\end{equation}
-requires
-\[
- \log\mathcal W(n)=o((\log\log n)^2)
-\]
-outside an $o(x)$ exceptional set of odd $n\le x$.  No result
-located in the arXiv, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, or zbMATH searches proves
-this weighted exact-rank dispersion estimate.  The available primitive-divisor
-theorems give existence, while the nearest distribution theorems control
-cumulative ranks, rank divisibility, the size of one primitive divisor, or a
-fixed index of appearance.  None controls the simultaneous weights
-$a(n_S)$ over the divisor family of a typical $n$.
-
-\subsection*{Unconditional bounds and the failed step}
-
-For a general $n$, let $R(n)$ be the largest number of rank-jump prime powers
-having one fixed essential/full support pair.  Private-coordinate encoding and
-the rank-pure construction give, for $k=\omega(n)\ge3$,
-\[
- (2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}-1)^{\lceil k/2\rceil}
- \le\#\mathcal M_n
- \le\sum_{s=1}^k\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}.
-\]
-Hence
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-entropy-bounds}
- \frac{\log2}{4}k^2-O(1)
- \le\log\#\mathcal M_n
- \le\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+k\log R(n)+O(k).
-\end{equation}
-The lower estimate already gives the target constant after the
-Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order theorem.  The upper estimate proves
-\eqref{eq:target-normal-order} if $\log R(n)=o(\omega(n))$ almost everywhere,
-but that maximum condition is only sufficient.  The weighted-cover condition
-above is necessary; it is not sufficient because the complementary ladder and
-non-rank-pure sectors also require an upper bound.
-
-We do prove two arithmetic estimates toward this interface.  First, collecting
-several exact ranks into a common support window contributes only
-$O(x\log\log x)$ to the relevant weighted mean, so the unresolved mean term is
-a visible single-rank maximum. Second, the standard Fibonacci cyclotomic, or
-fibotomic, factorization and the
-congruences $p\equiv\pm1\pmod d$ for $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$ give
-\[
- a(d)\le
- \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
- \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(d)}{\log d}.
-\]
-These are Theorems~\ref{thm:mean-rank-window-deaggregation} and
-\ref{thm:fibotomic-rank-entropy}.  The pointwise estimate is far too large to
-bound $\log\mathcal W(n)$ at the scale required above, and the cumulative
-estimates do not localize to the exact ranks $n_S$. This is the precise step
-at which the unconditional proof of \eqref{eq:target-normal-order} stops.
-It does, however, have a separate standard-object consequence. The classical
-primitive-part theorem retains the multiplicities discarded by the radical
-bound. Theorem~\ref{thm:large-primitive-wieferich-alternative} combines that
-input with the exact-rank count to prove that, at every sufficiently large
-rank, either a primitive divisor is at least $n^{2-\varepsilon}$ or a repeated
-primitive divisor is a Wall--Sun--Sun prime. Under Wall's conjecture this
-gives $P_{\rm prim}(F_n)\geq n^{2-o(1)}$.
-Proposition~\ref{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction} makes one limitation
-exact: among positive weight profiles with a fixed total mass, concentrating
-all excess mass on the full support minimizes the weighted cover sum. Hence
-even a lower bound of the conjectural size for
-$\omega(F_n)=\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)$ does not, by itself, force weighted-cover
-dispersion. No Fibonacci realization of the abstract extremizer is claimed.
-
-\subsection*{Organization}
-
-Section~\ref{sec:prelim} records the classical rank and primitive-divisor
-inputs. Section~\ref{sec:upper-fibers} gives the Wagner comparison and proves
-the witness-cover classification. Section~\ref{sec:prime-power-realization}
-proves the prime-power lifting, prime--ladder dichotomy, and unique ladder-slot
-formula. Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} develops the canonical squarefree slice,
-its weighted count, the labelled cover asymptotic, and worked examples.
-Section~\ref{sec:growth} proves the rank-window, fibotomic, support-entropy,
-and large-primitive-divisor bounds. Section~\ref{sec:inverse-dynamics} gives the short inverse-ray
-application, and the final section states the remaining arithmetic
-interfaces. The submitted supplement contains the connected-block
-factorization, exact support spectra, complete classifications for
-$\omega(n)\le4$, secondary asymptotics, and finite checks, all with numbered
-cross-references.

-\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}
-%% ====================================================================
-
-For an integer $q\ge1$, the \emph{rank of apparition} (or \emph{order of
-appearance}) $\alpha(q)$ is the least positive index $r$ such that $q\mid
-F_r$, where $F_0=0$ and $F_1=1$.  The existence of this index is recalled in
-Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-rank}.  We use the conventions $\alpha(1)=1$ and
-$D_1=\operatorname{Div}(F_1)=\{1\}$.  For $n\ge2$, write
-\[
- D_n:=\operatorname{Div}(F_n),\qquad
- B_n:=\{q\in D_n:\alpha(q)=n\},\qquad
- \mathcal M_n:=\min_{\mid} B_n .
-\]
-The rank divisibility criterion gives $B_n=\alpha^{-1}(n)$. Thus $B_n$ is
-the ordinary level set, or exact preimage, of $n$ under the rank map,
-equivalently the set
-of moduli that first divide a Fibonacci number at index $n$, and
-$\mathcal M_n$ is obtained by the generic poset operation of taking its
-divisibility-minimal elements.
-The boundary layer is empty: $B_2=\mathcal M_2=\varnothing$.  Throughout,
-$\log$ is natural, $\mathcal P(n)$ is the set of prime divisors of $n$,
-$\omega(n)=\#\mathcal P(n)$, and $\Omega(n)$ counts prime factors with
-multiplicity.
-
-\subsection*{Prior work and novelty boundary}
-
-The cardinality of $B_n$ is contained in Stroi\'nski's general
-$\alpha$-contraction formalism \cite{Stroinski2016AlphaContraction}; classical
-M\"obius identities for Fibonacci divisibility appear in
-\cite{Halton1966DivisibilityFibonacci,FultonMorris1969ArithmeticalFunctions}.
-For primes, nearby arithmetic-distribution results are due to Kiss. His 1987
-paper connects an almost-all upper hypothesis for greatest primitive divisors
-to Wieferich-type divisors \cite{Kiss1987WieferichLucas}; his 1988 work treats
-primitive divisors and accumulated primitive parts
-\cite{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}, while his paper on ranks of apparition of
-primes in Lucas sequences bounds averages of $\alpha(p)/p$
-\cite{Kiss1989RankApparition}.  These results, and Stroi\'nski's cumulative
-bound for primes with bounded rank, do not give upper-distribution estimates
-for the growing exact fibers
-\[
- \Pi_\alpha(d):=\{p\text{ prime}:\alpha(p)=d\},\qquad
- a(d):=\#\Pi_\alpha(d).
-\]
-The distinction between cumulative rank estimates and the individual
-multiplicities $a(d)$ is decisive below.
-
-The nearest structural predecessor is Wagner's theory of minimal
-multiplicative covers of an integer \cite{Wagner1978MultiplicativeCovers}.
-Wagner studies divisor tuples $(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$ with lcm $n$ such that the
-lcm becomes smaller when any one component is deleted, and presents them as
-the multiplicative generalization of the minimal covers of finite sets studied
-by Hearne--Wagner \cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}. Proposition~
-\ref{prop:wagner-comparison} proves the exact comparison. When all rank-jump factors are
-prime, $d^-(p)=1$ and our witness condition is Wagner's condition after
-forgetting tuple order. A ladder jump has nontrivial $d^-(p^e)$, so deletion
-is replaced by lowering one label. The contributions here are this
-Fibonacci-decorated predecessor version of standard join irredundance, its
-correspondence with
-$\mathcal M_n$, the canonical squarefree slice, and the exact arithmetic
-weights. The classical minimal-cover skeleton itself is not new.
-
-Other nearby work studies different aspects of the order-of-appearance map.
-Luca and Pomerance study its local behavior under additive shifts
-\cite{LucaPomerance2014LocalBehavior}; Trojovsk\'a and
-FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga study periodic points and dynamics
-\cite{Trojovska2020PeriodicPoints,
-FitzGibbonsJavaheriMillerVerga2025Dynamics}; and Sanna gives distribution
-theorems for rank divisibility and, under GRH, fixed indices of appearance
-\cite{Sanna2022RankDivisibility,Sanna2024IndexAppearance}. Cera Da
-Concei\c c\~ao subsequently gives explicit densities for fixed rank
-divisibility for all Lucas sequences and all fixed divisors
-\cite{CeraDaConceicao2026PrimeDensities}. Rank divisibility
-$d\mid\alpha(p)$ does not isolate $\alpha(p)=d$, and the fixed-index theorem
-does not provide the growing exact-fiber uniformity required here.
-
-FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga ask whether, for each $k\geq1$, there
-are infinitely many relatively prime integers of fixed-point order $k$, and
-conjecture that the basin of each fixed point $x>5$ contains infinitely many
-relatively prime integers.  Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays} constructs
-infinite prime inverse rays.  Corollaries~\ref{cor:prime-fixed-order} and
-\ref{cor:prime-basins} answer both questions in the stronger prime form.  The
-argument is a direct application of exact-rank prime existence and does not
-use the weighted-cover theory.
-
-The structural starting points of this paper are classical:
-\[
- q\mid F_m\Longleftrightarrow\alpha(q)\mid m,\qquad
- \gcd(F_r,F_s)=F_{\gcd(r,s)},
-\]
-and
-\[
- \alpha(\operatorname{lcm}(u,v))
- =\operatorname{lcm}(\alpha(u),\alpha(v)).
-\]
-See \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm,Vinson1963RankApparition}; Luca--Tron record
-the last identity for Fibonacci numbers \cite{LucaTron2015SelfFibonacciDivisors},
-and Renault proves it for the more general $(a,b)$-Fibonacci sequence
-\cite{Renault2013PeriodRankOrder}. Exact-rank prime existence is supplied by
-Carmichael and Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier
-\cite{Carmichael1913PrimitiveDivisors,
-BiluHanrotVoutier2001PrimitiveDivisorsLucas}.  The upper-set identity,
-coordinatewise lcm test, prime-power lifting formulas, and private-coordinate
-injection are consequences of these inputs.  We record them as lemmas and do
-not claim them as independent arithmetic advances.
-
-\subsection*{The reduction to a weighted arithmetic problem}
-
-For a prime power $\theta=p^e$, call $\theta$ rank-jump when lowering it to
-$p^{e-1}$ lowers its rank.  Relative to $n$, its rank has a full-coordinate
-support $T_n(\theta)$ and an essential support $E_n(\theta)$, the coordinates
-lost on lowering.  An $n$-witness cover is a pairwise coprime collection of
-rank-jump prime powers whose full supports cover $\mathcal P(n)$ and in which
-each factor has an
-essential coordinate absent from all other full supports.
-
-\begin{previewtheorem}[Witness-cover classification]
-Multiplication is a bijection from $n$-witness covers to $\mathcal M_n$.
-Consequently every $m\in\mathcal M_n$ has a unique rank-jump factorization and
-\[
- \omega(m)\le\omega(n).
-\]
-\end{previewtheorem}
-
-This is Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification}.  Its uniqueness is the usual
-unique factorization in $\mathbb Z$; the nontrivial content is the admissibility
-test identifying which prime-power factor sets occur. The classification turns the
-counting problem into a minimal-cover problem, but it does not erase the
-number of primes available at each exact rank.  The following result gives a
-necessary weighted obstruction on a positive-density family.
-
-\begin{previewtheorem}[Weighted odd-layer obstruction]
-Let $n\ge3$ be odd, set $V=\mathcal P(n)$, and for
-$\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V$ put
-$n_S=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n)}$.  If
-$\operatorname{MinCov}(V)$ denotes the irredundant covers of $V$ by nonempty
-subsets, then
-\[
- \sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
- \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}a(n_S)
- \le\#\mathcal M_n.
-\]
-\end{previewtheorem}
-
-The general rank-pure embedding is
-Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-pure-universality}, and the displayed obstruction is
-Corollary~\ref{cor:odd-weighted-cover-obstruction}.  The sum is the exact
-cardinality of an explicit rank-pure sector. Corollary~
-\ref{cor:rank-pure-minimal-transversals} encodes it as the minimal-transversal
-count of a canonical coordinate hypergraph, and the associated split graph is
-the standard split-incidence encoding. No theorem about arbitrary
-transversals or split graphs is claimed. More arithmetically, on every
-squarefree index Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} identifies
-that sector with the divisibility-minimal squarefree part of
-$\alpha^{-1}(n)$. Thus the weighted cover polynomial counts standard
-transversal objects and a standard slice of the exact fiber, not merely an
-auxiliary family. Any upper equivalent for
-$\#\mathcal M_n$ must control it. It need not exhaust the full fiber:
-$\alpha(13)=7$ and $\alpha(13^2)=91$, so the odd squarefree layer $91$ already
-has the ladder generator $169$ outside the rank-pure sector.
-
-Let $C_k$ be the number of irredundant covers of a labelled $k$-set.
-Hearne--Wagner give its exact enumeration
-\cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}. Lemma~
-\ref{lem:labelled-minimal-cover-comparison} compares that labelled formula
-directly with the labelled central sum in the split-graph asymptotics of
-Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka, giving
-\[
- \log C_k=\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+O(k)
-\]
-\cite{BenderRichmondWormald1985ChordalSplit,Troyka2019SplitGraphs}. This count
-does not use Royle's correspondence between unlabelled isomorphism types. For odd
-$n$, define the normalized weighted excess
-\[
- \mathcal W(n):=\frac1{C_{\omega(n)}}
- \sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(\mathcal P(n))}
- \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}a(n_S).
-\]
-Then the rank-pure sector satisfies
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-weighted-lower-bound}
- \log\#\mathcal M_n
- \ge\frac{\log2}{4}\omega(n)^2+\log\mathcal W(n)+O(\omega(n)).
-\end{equation}
-
-Since odd integers have positive density and
-$\omega(n)\sim\log\log n$ for almost all of them, the proposed tier-up theorem
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:target-normal-order}
- \log\#\mathcal M_n\sim
- \frac{\log2}{4}(\log\log n)^2
- \qquad\text{for almost all }n
-\end{equation}
-requires
-\[
- \log\mathcal W(n)=o((\log\log n)^2)
-\]
-outside an $o(x)$ exceptional set of odd $n\le x$.  No result
-located in the arXiv, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, or zbMATH searches proves
-this weighted exact-rank dispersion estimate.  The available primitive-divisor
-theorems give existence, while the nearest distribution theorems control
-cumulative ranks, rank divisibility, the size of one primitive divisor, or a
-fixed index of appearance.  None controls the simultaneous weights
-$a(n_S)$ over the divisor family of a typical $n$.

-\subsection*{Unconditional bounds and the failed step}
-
-For a general $n$, let $R(n)$ be the largest number of rank-jump prime powers
-having one fixed essential/full support pair.  Private-coordinate encoding and
-the rank-pure construction give, for $k=\omega(n)\ge3$,
-\[
- (2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}-1)^{\lceil k/2\rceil}
- \le\#\mathcal M_n
- \le\sum_{s=1}^k\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}.
-\]
-Hence
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-entropy-bounds}
- \frac{\log2}{4}k^2-O(1)
- \le\log\#\mathcal M_n
- \le\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+k\log R(n)+O(k).
-\end{equation}
-The lower estimate already gives the target constant after the
-Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order theorem.  The upper estimate proves
-\eqref{eq:target-normal-order} if $\log R(n)=o(\omega(n))$ almost everywhere,
-but that maximum condition is only sufficient.  The weighted-cover condition
-above is necessary; it is not sufficient because the complementary ladder and
-non-rank-pure sectors also require an upper bound.
-
-We do prove two arithmetic estimates toward this interface.  First, collecting
-several exact ranks into a common support window contributes only
-$O(x\log\log x)$ to the relevant weighted mean, so the unresolved mean term is
-a visible single-rank maximum. Second, the standard Fibonacci cyclotomic, or
-fibotomic, factorization and the

-\[
- a(d)\le
- \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
- \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(d)}{\log d}.
-\]
-These are Theorems~\ref{thm:mean-rank-window-deaggregation} and
-\ref{thm:fibotomic-rank-entropy}.  The pointwise estimate is far too large to
-bound $\log\mathcal W(n)$ at the scale required above, and the cumulative
-estimates do not localize to the exact ranks $n_S$. This is the precise step
-at which the unconditional proof of \eqref{eq:target-normal-order} stops.
-It does, however, have a separate standard-object consequence. The classical
-primitive-part theorem retains the multiplicities discarded by the radical
-bound. Theorem~\ref{thm:large-primitive-wieferich-alternative} combines that
-input with the exact-rank count to prove that, at every sufficiently large
-rank, either a primitive divisor is at least $n^{2-\varepsilon}$ or a repeated
-primitive divisor is a Wall--Sun--Sun prime. Under Wall's conjecture this
-gives $P_{\rm prim}(F_n)\geq n^{2-o(1)}$.
-Proposition~\ref{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction} makes one limitation

-all excess mass on the full support minimizes the weighted cover sum. Hence
-even a lower bound of the conjectural size for
-$\omega(F_n)=\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)$ does not, by itself, force weighted-cover
-dispersion. No Fibonacci realization of the abstract extremizer is claimed.

+\begin{theorem}[Support bound]
+\label{thm:minimal-generator-growth}

-\subsection*{Organization}
+Wagner's minimal multiplicative covers
+\cite{Wagner1978MultiplicativeCovers} supply the classical prime-jump
+skeleton: deleting one lcm label must lower the lcm. Fibonacci prime-power
+lifting adds the predecessor $d^-(\theta)$, so a ladder label must be lowered
+rather than deleted. Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} identifies
+exactly which such covers are the minimal rank fibers.

+The arithmetic realization uses the classical existence of an exact-rank

+exactly which such covers are the minimal rank fibers.
