-\section{Four-coordinate witness kernels}\label{sec:four-coordinate-kernels}
-
-The general enumeration of irredundant covers of finite sets is classical
-\cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}.  Here the relevant objects carry the
-additional Fibonacci essential/full-support decoration.  The classification
-below concerns this decorated structure and its arithmetic realization; the
-generic cover enumeration and Hall's theorem are used as inputs.
-
-Throughout this section assume
-\[
- \mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3,\ell_4\},\qquad
- a_i=\nu_{\ell_i}(n),\qquad V=[4].
-\]
-For nonempty $J\subseteq V$ and $i\in J$, write
-\[
- P_J:=(J,J),\qquad L_{i\mid J}:=(\{i\},J),
- \qquad S_i:=(\{i\},\{i\}).
-\]
-Thus $P_J$ denotes a prime slot, $L_{i\mid J}$ a proper ladder slot when
-$\#J>1$, and $S_i$ the undifferentiated singleton slot, which may be filled by
-either a prime or a ladder jump.  Braces and commas in subscripts are
-suppressed when no ambiguity can arise.
-
-For arithmetic filling, attach to these symbols the already defined rank-jump
-slot sets
-\[
- \mathfrak C(P_J)=\{p\in\mathcal A_{J,J}(n):p\text{ is prime}\},
- \qquad
- \mathfrak C(L_{i\mid J})=
- \{p^e\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},J}(n):e>1\},
-\]
-and
-\[
- \mathfrak C(S_i)=\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n).
-\]
-The exact-rank window, M\"obius count, and unique ladder-candidate formulas
-for these sets are those of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}; its proof is
-coordinatewise and the same formulas are read here with $[3]$ replaced by
-$V$.  We use these previously established formulas without claiming a new
-arithmetic result.

-\begin{theorem}[Complete four-coordinate kernel classification]
-\label{thm:four-coordinate-kernel-classification}
-Let
-\[
- \Delta=\{(I_1,J_1),\ldots,(I_r,J_r)\}
-\]
-be a collection of nonempty pairs satisfying
-\[
- I_j\subseteq J_j\subseteq V,\qquad
- I_j=J_j\ \text{or}\ \#I_j=1,
-\]
-\[
- \bigcup_{j=1}^rJ_j=V,
- \qquad
- I_j\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne j}J_h\ne\varnothing
- \quad(1\le j\le r).
-\]
-Up to coordinate permutation and reordering of slots, $\Delta$ belongs to
-exactly one of the twenty-four rows in
-Tables~\ref{tab:four-coordinate-connected-kernels} and
-\ref{tab:four-coordinate-disconnected-kernels}.  The first thirteen rows are
-exactly those for which the hypergraph with edges $J_1,\ldots,J_r$ is
-connected.  There are $243$ labelled kernels in total, of which $133$ have
-connected full-support hypergraph and $110$ do not.
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-For every slot choose a private coordinate
-$x_j\in I_j\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne j}J_h$.  These coordinates are distinct,
-so $r\le4$.  Suppose first that the $J$-hypergraph is connected.  If $r=1$,
-coverage gives $J_1=V$, and the prime--ladder alternative gives $K_1$ or
-$K_2$.  If $r=2$, set

- \quad C=J_2\setminus J_1.

-partition $V$.  Up to interchanging the two slots, their cardinalities are

-\begin{proposition}[Strict separation of the two support notions]
-\label{prop:four-coordinate-support-separation}
-There exist four-coordinate minimal generators whose positive-support
-hypergraph is connected although their full-support hypergraph is not.  More
-precisely, for
-\[
- n=3^2\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11=3465,
- \qquad
- m=17\cdot61\cdot421\cdot19801=8644661177,
-\]
-one has $m\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$, while the hypergraph with edges
-$T_n(\theta)$ for the four rank-jump factors of $m$ is disconnected.
-\end{proposition}

-\begin{proof}
-The four primes have exact ranks
-\[
- \alpha(17)=9,\qquad \alpha(61)=15,\qquad
- \alpha(421)=21,\qquad \alpha(19801)=33.
-\]
-Indeed,
-\[
- F_9=2\cdot17,\quad F_{15}=2\cdot5\cdot61,\quad
- F_{21}=2\cdot13\cdot421,\quad
- F_{33}=2\cdot89\cdot19801,
-\]
-and none of the displayed primes divides the Fibonacci number at a proper
-divisor of its displayed index.  With coordinates ordered as $(3,5,7,11)$,
-their full supports are
-\[
- \{1\},\quad\{2\},\quad\{3\},\quad\{4\}.
-\]
-They cover $V$ irredundantly.  Equivalently, the lcm of the four ranks is
-$3465$, whereas deleting them in the displayed order gives the four lcms
-\[
- 1155,\qquad693,\qquad495,\qquad315,
-\]
-all strictly smaller than $n$.  The minimal-lcm criterion therefore gives
-$m\in\mathcal M_n$.
-
-On the other hand, the positive supports of the four ranks are
-\[
- \{1\},\quad\{1,2\},\quad\{1,3\},\quad\{1,4\}.
-\]
-They form a connected star, so Definition~\ref{article-def:support-hypergraph}
-gives $m\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$.  The four singleton full supports
-are disconnected, proving the strict separation.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Exact arithmetic realization in four coordinates]
-\label{thm:four-coordinate-arithmetic-realization}
-Let $\mathcal O_4$ be the twenty-four orbit representatives in
-Tables~\ref{tab:four-coordinate-connected-kernels} and
-\ref{tab:four-coordinate-disconnected-kernels}.  Fix
-$\rho\in\mathcal O_4$ and a labelled coordinate permutation of $\rho$, and
-let $X_\rho$ be its slot set.  Replace each slot $x$ by its finite candidate
-set $C_x=\mathfrak C(x)$ defined above.
-Then the row has a coprime filling if and only if
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:four-hall}
- \#\bigcup_{x\in Y}\nu(C_x)\ge\#Y
- \qquad(Y\subseteq X_\rho),
-\end{equation}
-where $\nu(C_x)$ is the set of underlying primes of the prime powers in
-$C_x$.  The set $\mathcal M_n$ consists exactly of the distinct products
-obtained from all such fillings of all labelled rows.
-
-For a candidate rank-jump factor $\theta$, put
-\[
- K_n(\theta)=\{i:\nu_{\ell_i}(\alpha(\theta))>0\},
- \qquad
- C_{x,K}=\{\theta\in C_x:K_n(\theta)=K\}.
-\]
-Then $\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$ consists exactly of the products obtained
-from profiles $(K_x)_{x\in X_\rho}$ for which the hypergraph
-$(V,\{K_x:x\in X_\rho\})$ is connected and
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:four-profile-hall}
- \#\bigcup_{x\in Y}\nu(C_{x,K_x})\ge\#Y
- \qquad(Y\subseteq X_\rho).
-\end{equation}
-For the rows $K_1,\ldots,K_{13}$ the connectivity condition is automatic.
-For $D_1,\ldots,D_5$ it is equivalent to intersection of the two positive
-supports.  For $D_6,D_7,D_8$ it is equivalent to the singleton component's
-positive support meeting the union of the other two.  For $D_9,D_{10}$ the
-three positive supports must have connected intersection graph, and for
-$D_{11}$ the four positive supports must form a connected hypergraph; in the
-last case \eqref{eq:four-profile-hall} comprises all fifteen nonempty slot
-subsets.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} identifies elements of
-$\mathcal M_n$ with pairwise coprime jumpic witness covers.  The
-prime--ladder alternative identifies the labelled essential/full-support
-kernel of any such cover with one of the twenty-four rows in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-kernel-classification}, and the established
-rank-jump slot formulas give every candidate for every slot.
-For prime powers, pairwise coprimeness is exactly distinctness of underlying
-primes.  Hall's theorem \cite[Chapter~2]{LovaszPlummer1986MatchingTheory}
-therefore gives \eqref{eq:four-hall}.  Conversely, a Hall filling has the
-coverage and private-coordinate properties encoded by its row, hence is a
-witness cover and produces an element of $\mathcal M_n$.  Unique
-factorization recovers its labelled rank-jump factor set; repetitions caused by
-row stabilizers are removed by taking distinct products.
-
-The definition of $\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$ uses the positive supports
-$K_n(\theta)$, not the full supports $T_n(\theta)$.  After fixing a positive
-support profile, the only remaining compatibility condition is again
-distinctness of underlying primes, so Hall's theorem gives
-\eqref{eq:four-profile-hall}.  Taking the union over precisely the connected
-profiles proves the asserted formula.  Since $T_n(\theta)\subseteq
-K_n(\theta)$, every profile over a $K$-row is connected.  The stated tests for
-the $D$-rows follow directly from their component structures in the second
-table.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:four-coordinate-minimal-classification}
-The one-, two-, and three-coordinate classifications together with
-Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-arithmetic-realization} give a finite exact
-classification of $\mathcal M_n$ and $\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$ whenever
-$\omega(n)\le4$.  Combined with
-Theorem~\ref{thm:mingenerator-connected-factorization}, the same data give the
-existing partition normal form for every four-coordinate minimal generator.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Only the case $\omega(n)=4$ is new.  Theorem
-\ref{thm:four-coordinate-arithmetic-realization} classifies that case
-directly.  The connected-factorization theorem supplies the equivalent
-normal form obtained by multiplying the connected factors associated with a
-set partition of $\mathcal P(n)$.
-\end{proof}

-\subsection*{Organization}
+Wagner's minimal multiplicative covers
+\cite{Wagner1978MultiplicativeCovers} supply the classical prime-jump
+skeleton: deleting one lcm label must lower the lcm. Fibonacci prime-power
+lifting adds the predecessor $d^-(\theta)$, so a ladder label must be lowered
+rather than deleted. Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} identifies
+exactly which such covers are the minimal rank fibers.
 
-Section~\ref{sec:prelim} records the classical rank and primitive-divisor
-inputs. Section~\ref{sec:upper-fibers} gives the Wagner comparison and proves
-the witness-cover classification. Section~\ref{sec:prime-power-realization}
-proves the prime-power lifting, prime--ladder dichotomy, and unique ladder-slot
-formula. Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} develops the canonical squarefree slice,
-its weighted count, the labelled cover asymptotic, and worked examples.
-Section~\ref{sec:growth} proves the rank-window, fibotomic, support-entropy,
-and large-primitive-divisor bounds. Section~\ref{sec:inverse-dynamics} gives the short inverse-ray
-application, and the final section states the remaining arithmetic
-interfaces. The submitted supplement contains the connected-block
-factorization, exact support spectra, complete classifications for
-$\omega(n)\le4$, secondary asymptotics, and finite checks, all with numbered
-cross-references.
+The arithmetic realization uses the classical existence of an exact-rank
+prime for every rank $n\geq3$ except $6$ and $12$, following Carmichael and
+Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier
+\cite{Carmichael1913PrimitiveDivisors,BiluHanrotVoutier2001PrimitiveDivisorsLucas}.
+The multiplicities $a(d)$ retain information not supplied by existence alone;
+they become the weights in Theorem~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}.

-\[
- \prod_{d\mid n}F_d^{\mu(n/d)}=\Psi_n(1)

-\begin{theorem}[Large primitive divisor--Fibonacci--Wieferich alternative]
-\label{thm:large-primitive-wieferich-alternative}
-Let $F_0=0$ and $F_1=1$.  Call a prime $p$ a primitive prime divisor of
-$F_n$ when
-\[
- p\mid F_n\qquad\text{and}\qquad p\nmid 5F_1F_2\cdots F_{n-1}.
-\]
-For every real $\varepsilon>0$, there is an integer
-$N_\varepsilon\geq13$ such that, for every $n\geq N_\varepsilon$, at least
-one of the following holds:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
-\item $F_n$ has a primitive prime divisor $p\geq n^{2-\varepsilon}$;
-\item $F_n$ has a primitive prime divisor $q$ such that $q^2\mid F_n$.
-\end{enumerate}
-In the second alternative, $z(q)=n$ and $q$ is a Wall--Sun--Sun,
-equivalently Fibonacci--Wieferich, prime.
-
-Consequently, if no Wall--Sun--Sun primes exist and
-$P_{\rm prim}(F_n)$ denotes the largest primitive prime divisor of $F_n$,
-then
-\[
- \liminf_{n\to\infty}
- \frac{\log P_{\rm prim}(F_n)}{\log n}\geq2.
-\]
-Equivalently, $P_{\rm prim}(F_n)\geq n^{2-o(1)}$.
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-Fix $n\geq13$ and suppose alternative \textup{(ii)} fails.  Every primitive
-prime then occurs in $F_n$ to exponent one.  The classical primitive-divisor
-theorem gives at least one such prime, and hence
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:primitive-part-max-bound}
- \log U_n^{\rm prim}
- \leq a(n)\log P_{\rm prim}(F_n).
-\end{equation}
-For $n\geq13$, the exact-rank primes counted by $a(n)$ are precisely the

-\[

-Here $O(\log n)=o(\phi_{\rm E}(n))$ follows from the standard lower bound

-The first alternative therefore holds for all sufficiently large $n$, with

-\begin{remark}[Comparison with known large-divisor results]
-\label{rem:large-primitive-comparison}
-Stewart proved the unconditional lower bound
-$n\exp(\log n/(104\log\log n))$ for the greatest prime factor of the relevant
-Lucas cyclotomic factor, beyond an effective sequence-dependent threshold
-\cite[Theorem~1]{Stewart2013DivisorsLucasLehmer}.  Hong gives an explicit
-Fibonacci formulation: for each fixed positive integer $\kappa$, every
-sufficiently large $F_n$ has a primitive divisor outside
-$n\pm1,\ldots,\kappa n\pm1$, and hence one at least
-$(\kappa+1)n-1$ \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Hong2025BigPrimitiveDivisors}.
-The exponent $2-o(1)$ above is much stronger, but only after excluding the
-lifting anomaly.
-
-In Kiss's 1988 chapter, Theorem~2 fixes a nondegenerate Lucas sequence and a
-real $0<\lambda<1$, and proves that a positive proportion of the indices
-$n\leq x$ have a primitive prime-power factor of $R_n$ exceeding
-$n^{2-\lambda}$, for all sufficiently large $x$
-\cite[Theorem~2]{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}.  This is a positive-density
-result for the full prime power, not a pointwise lower bound for its base
-prime; indeed, Kiss notes that it does not decide whether the primes or the
-exponents are large.  By contrast, the theorem above treats every
-sufficiently large rank and separates the base-prime size from multiplicity
-at that same rank: failure of the large-base-prime alternative yields a
-repeated primitive prime of exact rank $n$, hence a Wall--Sun--Sun prime.
-Kiss's theorem gives neither that exact-rank alternative nor the all-indices
-conditional liminf displayed above.
-
-Kiss proved an earlier, different bridge to Wieferich-type primes: if, for a
-fixed $0<\delta<1$, the greatest primitive divisor of a Lucas term is below
-$n^{1+\delta}$ for almost all indices, then a positive-density set of indices
-has a term divisible by a Wieferich-type prime
-\cite{Kiss1987WieferichLucas}.  That result is neither pointwise nor an
-exact-rank alternative.  The theorem above does not resolve Wall's question;
-it says that failure of a near-quadratic primitive divisor cannot occur in an
-ordinary rank-lifting layer, but forces a Fibonacci--Wieferich anomaly at that
-exact rank.
-\end{remark}

-$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_r\}$ with the factors ordered so that
-$(E_n(\theta_j),T_n(\theta_j))=(I_j,J_j)$. By definition
-$\theta_j\in\mathcal A_{I_j,J_j}(n)$, and pairwise coprimeness is part of
-Definition~\ref{article-def:witness-cover}. Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families}
-places each such factor in the corresponding prime or ladder family, and
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests} translates those
-families into the displayed rank-window and ladder-candidate conditions. Thus
-the arithmetic selection test succeeds.
-
-Conversely, assume that the arithmetic selection test succeeds. By
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}, each selected
-prime power lies in the required prime or ladder family, and
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families} gives
-$\theta_j\in\mathcal A_{I_j,J_j}(n)$. Distinct underlying primes are exactly
-pairwise coprimeness for prime powers. Because the fixed row is an abstract
-witness type, the sets $J_j$ cover $[3]$, and for every $j$ one has
-$I_j\nsubseteq\bigcup_{h\ne j}J_h$. Translating back to $T_n$ and $E_n$, the
-set $\Theta=\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_r\}$ satisfies the coverage and
-irredundance conditions in Definition~\ref{article-def:witness-cover}; coprimeness
-gives the remaining condition. Hence $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover, so
-Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} gives
-$m=\prod_j\theta_j\in\mathcal M_n$ with the prescribed row type.
-
-The factorization of $m$ into maximal prime powers is unique, so it recovers
-the displayed labelled rank-jump factor set uniquely. A raw enumeration over all
-coordinate permutations may nevertheless repeat a labelled row or a product
-when a $\Gamma_i$ has a nontrivial stabilizer. Accordingly, unlabelled shapes
-are identified only at the level of $S_3$-orbits, and all enumerated products
-are deduplicated. The final exclusion of $\Gamma_2$ is
-Lemma~\ref{lem:fibonacci-three-coordinate-types}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Three-coordinate realization]\label{lem:three-coordinate-realization}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$. After the labelled coordinate
-supports $E_n,T_n\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$ are fixed, every element of
-$\mathcal M_n$ arises from exactly one nonempty arithmetic selection in the
-rank windows $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ and the explicit ladder candidates
-$\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ belonging to one fixed labelled coordinate permutation of
-one of the eight admissible types in
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness}; the selected prime powers
-must have distinct underlying primes. The unlabelled $\Gamma$-rows are only
-representatives modulo coordinate relabeling.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-This is Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} together with
-Lemmas~\ref{lem:fibonacci-three-coordinate-types} and
-\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness}.
-\end{proof}
-
-The finite slot-selection algorithm behind Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}
-is recorded in Appendix~\ref{app:three-coordinate-checklist}; it is used below
-only to justify that the displayed table is an effective closed classification.
-
-\begin{theorem}[Complete low-support classification: eight support-three families]
-\label{thm:low-support-classification-package}
-Let $n\ge2$.  The minimal generators $\mathcal M_n$ are classified for
-$\omega(n)\le3$ as follows.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item If $\omega(n)=1$, then $\mathcal M_n=\Atom(n)$.
-\item If $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2\}$, then $\mathcal M_n$ is the
- disjoint union of $\Atom(n)$ and the products
- $\theta_1\theta_2$ with
- $\theta_i\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n)$ and
- $\gcd(\theta_1,\theta_2)=1$.
-\item If $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$, then $\mathcal M_n$ is the
- set of distinct products admitted by Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification},
- after applying all coordinate permutations and the finite slot-selection
- criterion of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection}.  Equivalently, for each
- permuted row one chooses one prime power from each displayed slot set, with
- distinct underlying primes. Every such product occurs. Each element of
- $\mathcal M_n$ has a unique labelled support set $\mathsf T(m)$, while its
- unlabelled $\Gamma_i$ is determined only up to the $S_3$-orbit; a product
- produced more than once by the raw permuted enumeration is retained once.
-\end{enumerate}
-For the three-coordinate rows,
-$P_J(n)$ denotes the exact-rank prime slot, $L_{i,J}(n)$ the ladder slot with
-essential coordinate $i$ and full support $J$, and
-$S_i(n)=P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n)$ the singleton slot.  Each slot is the
-following explicit finite set:
-\[
-\begin{aligned}
-\mathfrak C(P_J)&:=\bigcup_{d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d),\\
-\mathfrak C(L_{i,J})&:=\{\lambda\in\mathcal L_i^*(n):\alpha(\lambda)\mid n,
-\ \{k:\nu_{\ell_k}(\alpha(\lambda))=\nu_{\ell_k}(n)\}=J\},\\
-\mathfrak C(S_i)&:=\mathfrak C(P_{\{i\}})\cup \mathfrak C(L_{i,\{i\}}).
-\end{aligned}
-\]
-Here $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ is the finite exact-rank window and
-$\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ is the empty-or-singleton ladder candidate set of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}. A row succeeds
-exactly when its displayed finite slot sets admit a filling by distinct
-underlying primes, equivalently when the Hall test of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} holds.  The displayed rows are
-representatives modulo relabeling of the coordinates $1,2,3$.
-Equivalently, writing $[3]=\{1,2,3\}$, suppressing braces in prime-slot
-subscripts, and letting $(i,j,k)$ range over ordered triples of distinct
-coordinates, the eight orbit representatives are
-\[
-P_{[3]},\quad L_{i,[3]},\quad P_{i,j}P_{j,k},\quad
-L_{i,\{i,j\}}P_{j,k},\quad
-L_{i,\{i,j\}}L_{k,\{j,k\}},\quad S_iP_{j,k},
-\quad S_iL_{j,\{j,k\}},\quad S_iS_jS_k,
-\]
-respectively for $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4,\Gamma_5,\Gamma_6,\Gamma_7,
-\Gamma_8,\Gamma_9$.
-Let $\mathcal G_n$ denote the finite set displayed in (i), (ii), or (iii), with
-the convention $\mathcal G_2=\varnothing$.  Then, for every $n\ge2$ with
-$\omega(n)\le3$,
-\[
-\mathcal G_n=\mathcal M_n,
-\]
-and the displayed list is a finite minimal-generator classification. The
-table should be read in three passes.  First choose one of the eight
-unlabelled support skeletons and then apply an arbitrary permutation of the
-coordinate labels $1,2,3$.  Next replace every displayed slot by its explicit
-finite candidate set $\mathfrak C(\cdot)$, so prime slots are tested through
-the rank windows $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ and ladder slots through the candidate
-sets $\mathcal L_i^*(n)$. Finally apply the distinct-prime Hall test and insert
-the resulting products into a set: a row
-contributes exactly the products obtained by choosing one prime power from each
-of its candidate slots with no underlying prime repeated.  The lemmas preceding
-the theorem prove that these three finite steps are equivalent to the abstract
-witness-cover conditions, so the table is not an additional heuristic case
-split but the effective normal form for all support-three minimal generators.
-
-\begin{table}[ht]
-\centering
-\small
-\caption{Complete three-coordinate classification. Each displayed row is a
-representative modulo relabeling of the three coordinates; all coordinate
-permutations of the row are included in the classification.}
-\label{tab:three-coordinate-classification}
-\begin{tabular}{p{0.10\linewidth}p{0.29\linewidth}p{0.49\linewidth}}
-\toprule
-Type & support-three family & finite slot test\\
-\midrule
-$\Gamma_1$ & $P_{123}(n)$ & $\mathfrak C(P_{123})\ne\varnothing$\\

-$\Gamma_5$ & $L_{1,12}(n),\ P_{23}(n)$ & $\mathfrak C(L_{1,12})\ne\varnothing$ and $\mathfrak C(P_{23})$ contains a prime different from the ladder prime\\

-$\Gamma_8$ & $S_1(n),\ L_{2,23}(n)$ & $\mathfrak C(L_{2,23})\ne\varnothing$ and $\mathfrak C(S_1)$ contains a rank-jump factor with a different underlying prime\\
-$\Gamma_9$ & $S_1(n),\ S_2(n),\ S_3(n)$ & the three finite singleton sets satisfy the Hall distinct-prime inequalities\\
-\bottomrule

-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The one-coordinate assertion is Corollary~\ref{cor:one-support-complete-classification}.
-The two-coordinate assertion is Corollary~\ref{cor:two-support-complete-classification}.
-Assume now that $\omega(n)=3$. Lemma~\ref{lem:fibonacci-three-coordinate-types}
-reduces every witness cover to the eight listed abstract types and excludes
-$\Gamma_2$. Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families} translates
-an abstract slot $(I,J)$ into exactly one of the displayed prime, ladder,
-or singleton families: nonsingleton slots with $I=J$ are $P_J(n)$, proper
-ladder slots $I=\{i\}\subsetneq J$ are $L_{i,J}(n)$, and singleton slots are
-$S_i(n)=P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n)$. Substituting these translations into
-the eight admissible abstract types of Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}
-gives precisely the rows of Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}.
-The same substitution, with braces suppressed in prime-slot subscripts,
-gives the displayed canonical-family list: the first two rows are the full
-prime and full ladder families, the next three are the two-slot overlapping
-families, the next two attach a singleton slot to a nonsingleton slot, and the
-last row is the three-singleton family.
-
-It remains only to identify the tests in the last column. For prime slots,
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests} gives
-$P_J(n)=\bigcup_{d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d)$ and, after deleting
-previously used underlying primes, the stated finite multiplicity criterion.
-For ladder slots, the same proposition gives the displayed singleton-candidate
-formula for $L_{i,J}(n)$. Pairwise coprimeness of the chosen prime powers is
-exactly the distinct-underlying-prime condition because all slots are filled by
-prime powers. Hence the table's row test is the arithmetic selection test of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness}. That theorem also gives the
-converse construction and uniqueness, up to reordering slots with identical
-labelled data, while Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} identifies the
-resulting products with the elements of $\mathcal M_n$.
-
-Thus the displayed support-dependent set $\mathcal G_n$ equals
-$\mathcal M_n$ in all cases $\omega(n)\le3$, including the boundary convention
-$\mathcal G_2=\varnothing=\mathcal M_2$.  In the three-coordinate case the
-finiteness of the prime and ladder slot sets and the exact slot enumeration
-are supplied by Proposition~\ref{prop:three-coordinate-table-checklist}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Support-three obstruction certificates]
-\label{cor:support-three-obstruction-certificates}
-Assume $\omega(n)=3$ and let a proposed support-three minimal-generator shape be
-specified by an irredundant finite list of rank-jump slots whose full-support sets
-cover the labelled coordinates $\{1,2,3\}$.  Exactly one of the following
-alternatives occurs.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
-\item The shape is the excluded skeleton $\Gamma_2$, equivalently it requires an
-rank-jump factor with $1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta)=3$; then no Fibonacci minimal
-generator has that shape.
-\item After relabeling it is one of the eight rows in
-Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}.  The row contributes exactly
-the products obtained from the finite candidate sets
-$\mathfrak C(P_J)$, $\mathfrak C(L_{i,J})$, and $\mathfrak C(S_i)$ by choosing
-one prime power in each row slot with distinct underlying primes.
-\item The row is one of the eight admissible skeletons but the finite
-distinct-prime Hall inequalities of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} fail;
-then the row contributes no element of $\mathcal M_n$.
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus every failure in support three has a certificate of one of two kinds: the
-single structural Fibonacci obstruction $\Gamma_2$, or a finite Hall deficiency
-inside an otherwise admissible slot row.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}, every irredundant three-coordinate
-witness skeleton is one of $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_9$. The prime--ladder
-dichotomy, Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, excludes precisely the
-case in which a rank-jump factor has a proper nonsingleton essential set inside a larger
-full-support set; among the nine skeletons this is exactly $\Gamma_2$, proving
-(a).
-
-For every remaining skeleton, Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families}
-translates each abstract slot into one of the prime slots $P_J(n)$, ladder
-slots $L_{i,J}(n)$, or singleton slots $S_i(n)$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}
-identifies these as the finite candidate sets displayed in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.  A selected row therefore
-forms a witness cover exactly when its chosen prime powers are pairwise
-coprime, and for prime powers this is exactly distinctness of underlying primes.
-Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} is precisely the Hall criterion for such a
-selection.  If the criterion holds, Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification}
-turns the selected witness cover into the corresponding element of
-$\mathcal M_n$; if it fails, no coprime filling of that row exists.  These are
-(b) and (c), and the alternatives exhaust all support-three possibilities.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Low-support rank level sets and counting]
-\label{cor:low-support-normal-form}
-\label{cor:low-support-birth-layer-package}
-\label{prop:low-support-cardinality-formula}
-Let $n\ge2$ with $\omega(n)\le3$, and let $\mathcal G_n$ be the finite
-minimal-generator set described in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.  Then $\mathcal G_n$ is
-the canonical antichain of minimal elements of $B_n$, and for every $q\in D_n$,
-\[
-q\in B_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\text{there exists }g\in\mathcal G_n\text{ with }g\mid q.
-\]
-Equivalently,
-\[
-B_n=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal G_n}\{q\in D_n:\ g\mid q\},
-\]
-where the union is taken inside the divisor lattice $D_n$ and is not asserted
-to be disjoint.  The rank-level-set cardinality is the closed finite formula
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-support-cardinality-formula}
-A(n)=
-\sum_{\varnothing\ne\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal G_n}
-(-1)^{|\mathcal S|+1}
-\tau\left(\frac{F_n}{\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)}\right),
-\end{equation}
-with the convention that the empty sum is $0$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package} gives
-$\mathcal G_n=\mathcal M_n$ for $\omega(n)\le3$, including the boundary
-convention $\mathcal G_2=\varnothing=\mathcal M_2$. Minimal elements of an
-upper set are pairwise incomparable, so $\mathcal G_n$ is an antichain in
-$D_n$.  The upper-fiber identity, Lemma~\ref{article-thm:upper-fiber}, gives for every
-$n\ge2$ the principal-upper-ideal decomposition
-\[
-B_n=\bigcup_{m\in\mathcal M_n}\{q\in D_n:m\mid q\}.
-\]
-Replacing $\mathcal M_n$ by $\mathcal G_n$ gives the displayed union and the
-membership criterion.  The minimal elements of this union are exactly the
-generators in $\mathcal G_n$, because no two elements of $\mathcal G_n$ are
-comparable.
-
-It remains to count the union.  If $\mathcal G_n=\varnothing$, then
-$B_n=\varnothing$, so $A(n)=0$ and the empty-sum convention gives
-\eqref{eq:low-support-cardinality-formula}.  Otherwise, for $g\in\mathcal G_n$
-put $U_g:=\{q\in D_n:g\mid q\}$.  For a nonempty subset
-$\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal G_n$, a divisor $q$ of $F_n$ lies in
-$\bigcap_{g\in\mathcal S}U_g$ if and only if
-$\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)$ divides $q$.  Since every $g\in\mathcal G_n$ divides
-$F_n$, this least common multiple also divides $F_n$, and division by it gives a
-bijection
-\[
-\bigcap_{g\in\mathcal S}U_g
-\longleftrightarrow
-\operatorname{Div}\left(F_n/\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)\right).
-\]
-Hence
-\[
-\#\bigcap_{g\in\mathcal S}U_g=
-\tau\left(\frac{F_n}{\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)}\right).
-\]
-Ordinary finite inclusion--exclusion applied to
-$B_n=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal G_n}U_g$ proves
-\eqref{eq:low-support-cardinality-formula}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Prime-only three-coordinate skeleton]
-\label{cor:primitive-three-skeleton}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$ and that
-$n_S:=\prod_{i\in S}\ell_i^{\nu_{\ell_i}(n)}$ satisfies
-$n_S\ge 3$ and $n_S\notin\{6,12\}$ for every nonempty
-$S\subseteq[3]$. Then the four prime-only three-coordinate
-types $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_4$, $\Gamma_7$, and $\Gamma_9$ are realized in
-$\mathcal M_n$. More precisely, after choosing exact-rank primes
-$\pi_S$ with $\alpha(\pi_S)=n_S$, the following minimal generators realize
-these types:
-\[
-\pi_{123},\qquad
-\pi_{12}\pi_{23},\qquad
-\pi_1\pi_{23},\qquad
-\pi_1\pi_2\pi_3 .
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The hypothesis and Theorem~\ref{article-thm:primitive-divisors} provide the indicated
-exact-rank primes. An exact-rank prime for $n_S$ is a prime jump with
-$E_n(\pi_S)=T_n(\pi_S)=S$. The four displayed collections of coordinate
-sets are precisely the prime-only types $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_4$,
-$\Gamma_7$, and $\Gamma_9$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}, and
-the chosen primes are pairwise distinct. The
-pairwise-coprime selection criterion of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness} therefore gives the four
-minimal generators.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}\label{rem:wss}
-The only Wall--Sun--Sun input needed here is local.  By
-Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}, for $p\neq 2,5$ one has
-$\alpha(p^2)=\alpha(p)$ if and only if $\nu_p(F_{\alpha(p)})\ge 2$, the
-Wall--Sun--Sun condition for $p$ \cite{SunSun1992FibonacciFLT}.  Thus the
-condition merely determines whether the first odd-prime ladder step is delayed;
-we do not use any distributional assertion about such primes.
-\end{remark}

-\section{Low-support classifications}\label{sec:low-support}
-%% ====================================================================
-
-We now introduce the Fibonacci-specific arithmetic input. The structural
-results of Section~\ref{article-sec:upper-fibers} did not use the formulas below.

-\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
-\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
-Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
-$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
-\[
-\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
-\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
-\]
-\[
-\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
-\]
-and, for $p\ne2,5$,
-\[
-\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
-\]
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
-\[
-p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
-\]
-\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
-\[
-F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
-\]
-gives
-\[
-z_p\mid p-\left(\frac5p\right),
-\]
-so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
-\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the modern
-treatment of Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that
-when $z_p\mid r$,
-\[
-\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
-\]
-Writing $r=z_pu$ and using $p\nmid z_p$ yields
-\[
-\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u).
-\]
-Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
-$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
-$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$. This proves the formula for $p\ne2,5$ without an
-implicit assumption on $z_p$.
-
-For the exceptional primes, the cited formulas specialize to
-\[
-\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
-\qquad
-\nu_2(F_r)=
-\begin{cases}
-0, & 3\nmid r,\\
-1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
-3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
-\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
-\end{cases}
-\]
-The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices with
-valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for $e\ge4$ the
-least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:rank-jump-classification}
-The rank-jump prime powers are exactly the following:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
-$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not a rank-jump factor.
-\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
-\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
-$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
-$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
-$1<e\le h_p$ is rank-jump.
-\end{enumerate}
-Consequently every rank-jump factor is either a prime jump $p\in\Atom(\alpha(p))$ or a
-ladder jump $p^e$ with $e>1$. Every ladder jump changes only the $p$-adic
-coordinate of its apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
-$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. Hence $2$ and $4$ are rank-jump,
-$8$ is not, and each $2^e$ with $e\ge4$ is rank-jump. For $p=5$, every step is
-rank-jump. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
-gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. This proves the list. At every
-ladder step, $d(\theta)/d^-(\theta)$ is a power of the same prime $p$, which
-proves the final assertion.
-\end{proof}
-
-This section keeps the low-support classification in the main theorem stream
-while treating the slot mechanics as proof support. The principal conclusion is
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}: for support three there
-are exactly eight admissible families, and every remaining decision is a finite
-slot-filling test.  The arithmetic tests for filling those slots are stated here;
-the reader-facing checklist and the worked $n=42$ verification are collected in
-Appendix~\ref{app:three-coordinate-checklist}.
-
-\begin{lemma}[Prime--ladder alternative]\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
-Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
-\[
-E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
-\]
-If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or a singleton, and any
-coordinate in $E_n(\theta)$ is the prime coordinate $p$. In particular no
-Fibonacci rank-jump factor has
-\[
-1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate of
-$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering $\theta$; hence
-$E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$.
-
-Assume $e>1$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:rank-jump-classification}, $\theta$ is a
-ladder jump. The prime-power formulas in
-Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} show that
-$d(\theta)$ and $d^-(\theta)$ differ only in the $p$-adic coordinate of the
-apparition index: this is explicit for $p=2$ and $p=5$, and for
-$p\ne2,5$ it follows from
-$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at the rank-jump ladder levels. Therefore the only
-full coordinate that can be lost when
-passing from $d(\theta)$ to $d^-(\theta)$ is the coordinate $p$ itself.
-Thus $E_n(\theta)$ is empty or $\{p\}$.
-
-The final assertion follows because either $E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$ in
-the prime jump case or $\#E_n(\theta)\le1$ in the ladder case.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Private-coordinate injection]\label{thm:extremal-coordinate-separation}
-Let $\Theta$ be an $n$-witness cover. For each
-$\theta\in\Theta$ one may choose a coordinate
-\[
-\ell(\theta)\in
-E_n(\theta)\setminus\bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta,\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta),
-\]
-and the chosen coordinates are distinct. If
-$|\Theta|=\omega(n)$, then after relabeling the elements of $\Theta$ by
-the coordinates of $\mathcal P(n)$ one has
-\[
-T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}\qquad(\ell\in\mathcal P(n)).
-\]
-In particular, when $\omega(n)=2$, every two-element $n$-witness cover has
-one rank-jump factor supported on the first coordinate and one rank-jump factor supported on the
-second.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The existence of $\ell(\theta)$ is exactly the irredundance condition in
-Definition~\ref{article-def:witness-cover}. If
-$\ell(\theta)=\ell(\eta)$ with $\theta\ne\eta$, then
-$\ell(\theta)\in T_n(\eta)$ because
-$E_n(\eta)\subseteq T_n(\eta)$, contradicting the choice of
-$\ell(\theta)$. Hence the chosen coordinates are distinct.
-
-If $|\Theta|=\omega(n)$, the injection
-$\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a bijection from $\Theta$ to
-$\mathcal P(n)$. The coordinate $\ell(\theta)$ is not in
-$T_n(\eta)$ for any $\eta\ne\theta$. Since the $T_n(\eta)$ cover
-$\mathcal P(n)$, every coordinate other than $\ell(\theta)$ is the private
-coordinate of some other rank-jump factor and therefore is not in $T_n(\theta)$. Thus
-$T_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}$ for every $\theta$, which gives the stated
-separation after relabeling.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[One-coordinate classification]
-\label{cor:one-support-complete-classification}
-If $\omega(n)=1$, then
-\[
-\mathcal M_n=\Atom(n).
-\]
-With the convention of Definition~\ref{article-def:birth-layer}, the exceptional
-case $n=2$ gives $\mathcal M_2=\varnothing=\Atom(2)$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ and let $\Theta$ be the corresponding $n$-witness
-cover from Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification}. By
-Corollary~\ref{article-cor:support-bound}, $\#\Theta\le\omega(n)=1$. Since the
-$T_n$-sets of a witness cover must cover $\mathcal P(n)$, the cover has one
-rank-jump factor, say $\Theta=\{\theta\}$. The coverage condition forces
-$T_n(\theta)=\mathcal P(n)$, and because $d(\theta)\mid n$ this is
-equivalent to $d(\theta)=n$. Hence $\theta\in\Atom(n)$ and
-$m=\theta$.
-
-Conversely, if $\theta\in\Atom(n)$ and $n\ne2$, then
-$d(\theta)=n$, so $T_n(\theta)=\mathcal P(n)$. Since
-$d^-(\theta)<d(\theta)=n$ and $\mathcal P(n)$ has one element, the unique
-prime coordinate of $n$ lies in $E_n(\theta)$. Thus $\{\theta\}$ is an
-$n$-witness cover, and Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} gives
-$\theta\in\mathcal M_n$. For $n=2$, Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}
-and Corollary~\ref{cor:rank-jump-classification} show that no prime power has
-rank $2$, while Definition~\ref{article-def:birth-layer} gives
-$\mathcal M_2=\varnothing$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Two-coordinate classification]
-\label{cor:two-support-complete-classification}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2\}$ and identify
-$\{\ell_1,\ell_2\}$ with $\{1,2\}$ in the notation
-$\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ from Definition~\ref{article-def:rank-jump-families}. Also put
-\[
-\mathcal P_i(n):=\{\theta\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n):
-\theta\text{ is a prime jump}\},
-\qquad
-\mathcal L_i(n):=\{\theta\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n):
-\theta\text{ is a ladder jump}\}.
-\]
-Then $\mathcal M_n$ is the disjoint union of the following two families:
-\[
-\Atom(n)
-\]
-and
-\[
-\{\theta_1\theta_2:\ \theta_i\in
-\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n)=\mathcal P_i(n)\cup\mathcal L_i(n),\
-\gcd(\theta_1,\theta_2)=1\}.
-\]
-Equivalently, every non-rank-jump minimal generator is obtained by choosing,
-for each coordinate, one prime or ladder jump whose rank first jumps on that
-coordinate, with the two chosen prime powers coprime.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$, and write its witness cover as $\Theta$. If
-$\#\Theta=1$, then its sole rank-jump factor has rank $n$, so $m\in\Atom(n)$.
-
-Assume $\#\Theta>1$. By Corollary~\ref{article-cor:support-bound},
-$\#\Theta\le2$, hence $\#\Theta=2$. The second assertion of
-Lemma~\ref{thm:extremal-coordinate-separation} says, after relabeling the
-two factors, that one rank-jump factor has full support $\{1\}$ and the other has full
-support $\{2\}$. Since each rank-jump factor in a witness cover has a nonempty essential
-coordinate not supplied by the other rank-jump factor, the first has
-$E_n=T_n=\{1\}$ and the second has $E_n=T_n=\{2\}$. Thus the two rank-jump factors lie in
-the displayed families, and pairwise coprimeness is part of the witness-cover
-definition. Corollary~\ref{cor:rank-jump-classification} gives the stated
-prime-or-ladder decomposition of each one-coordinate family.
-
-Conversely, a single rank-jump factor in $\Atom(n)$ is an $n$-witness cover by itself,
-because lowering it lowers its rank. If
-$\theta_i\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n)$ are coprime, then their
-$T$-sets cover $\{1,2\}$ and each rank-jump factor has its own essential coordinate.
-Therefore $\{\theta_1,\theta_2\}$ is an $n$-witness cover, and
-Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} gives
-$\theta_1\theta_2\in\mathcal M_n$. The two displayed families are disjoint
-because their elements have respectively one and two prime-power factors.
-\end{proof}
-
-We now classify the three-support case. The abstract $\Gamma_i$ record only
-the pairs $(E_n(\theta),T_n(\theta))$ up to coordinate relabeling. The lemmas
-below exclude the one shape incompatible with Fibonacci prime-power arithmetic,
-identify finite exact-rank and ladder slots for the remaining shapes, and apply
-the distinct-underlying-prime selection criterion.
-
-\begin{lemma}[Abstract three-coordinate skeletons]\label{lem:abstract-three-types}
-Let $X=\{1,2,3\}$. Consider finite collections
-\[
-\Delta=\{(I_1,J_1),\dots,(I_r,J_r)\},\qquad
-\varnothing\ne I_a\subseteq J_a\subseteq X,
-\]
-up to permutation of $X$ and reordering of the pairs, subject to
-\[
-\bigcup_a J_a=X,\qquad
-I_a\nsubseteq\bigcup_{b\ne a}J_b\quad(1\le a\le r).
-\]
-Then $r\le3$, and every such abstract three-coordinate witness type is
-equivalent to exactly one of the following nine labelled types:
-\[
-\begin{array}{ll}
-\Gamma_1:\ \{(123,123)\},&
-\Gamma_2:\ \{(12,123)\},\\
-\Gamma_3:\ \{(1,123)\},&
-\Gamma_4:\ \{(12,12),(23,23)\},\\
-\Gamma_5:\ \{(1,12),(23,23)\},&
-\Gamma_6:\ \{(1,12),(3,23)\},\\
-\Gamma_7:\ \{(1,1),(23,23)\},&
-\Gamma_8:\ \{(1,1),(2,23)\},\\
-\Gamma_9:\ \{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\}.
-\end{array}
-\]
-Here, for instance, $123$ denotes $\{1,2,3\}$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For each pair choose
-$x_a\in I_a\setminus\bigcup_{b\ne a}J_b$. Then $x_a\in J_a$ and the
-$x_a$ are distinct, so $r\le\#X=3$.
-
-If $r=1$, then $J_1=X$. Up to relabeling, $I_1$ has size $3$, $2$, or $1$,
-giving $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_2$, and $\Gamma_3$.
-
-If $r=2$, neither $J_1$ nor $J_2$ is contained in the other, because each
-has a private coordinate outside the other. Thus the unordered pair
-$(J_1,J_2)$ is, up to relabeling, either $(12,23)$ or $(1,23)$. In the
-overlapping case $(12,23)$, the first private coordinate is $1$ and the
-second is $3$. Hence, again up to reversing the two pairs, the possible
-essential sets are $(12,23)$, $(1,23)$, or $(1,3)$, giving
-$\Gamma_4$, $\Gamma_5$, and $\Gamma_6$. In the disjoint case $(1,23)$, the
-first essential set must be $1$, while the second is either $23$ or a
-singleton; these are $\Gamma_7$ and $\Gamma_8$.
-
-If $r=3$, the three chosen private coordinates exhaust $X$. Since each
-coordinate is absent from the two $J$-sets to which it is not assigned, no
-$J_a$ can contain any coordinate other than its own private coordinate.
-Thus the only possibility is
-$\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\}$, namely $\Gamma_9$.
-The cases are mutually exclusive by $r$, by the intersection pattern of the
-$J$-sets, and by the sizes of the $I$-sets after those data are fixed.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Fibonacci three-coordinate types]\label{lem:fibonacci-three-coordinate-types}
-Assume $\omega(n)=3$. Every $n$-witness cover has one of the abstract types
-\[
-\Gamma_1,\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4,\Gamma_5,\Gamma_6,\Gamma_7,\Gamma_8,\Gamma_9,
-\]
-and no $n$-witness cover has type $\Gamma_2$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $\Theta$ be an $n$-witness cover. The collection of pairs
-\[
-\{(E_n(\theta),T_n(\theta)):\theta\in\Theta\}
-\]
-satisfies the abstract hypotheses of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}; coverage and irredundance are exactly
-the last two conditions in Definition~\ref{article-def:witness-cover}. Hence its
-type is one of $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_9$.
-
-By Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, a Fibonacci rank-jump factor has either
-$E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$, in the prime jump case, or
-$E_n(\theta)$ empty or a singleton, in the ladder case. In a witness cover
-$E_n(\theta)$ cannot be empty. Therefore no rank-jump factor can have
-$1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta)$. The only abstract type in the displayed
-list requiring such a rank-jump factor is $\Gamma_2$, represented by $(12,123)$, so
-$\Gamma_2$ is excluded.
-
-This proves the asserted containment in the eight displayed types and the
-exclusion of $\Gamma_2$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Prime and ladder jump families in three coordinates]
-\label{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$ and identify subsets of
-$[3]=\{1,2,3\}$ with the corresponding coordinate subsets of
-$\mathcal P(n)$. For nonempty $J\subseteq[3]$ define the prime jump family
-\[
-P_J(n):=\{\theta\in\mathcal A_{J,J}(n):\theta\text{ is a prime}\},
-\]
-and, for $i\in J$, define the ladder family
-\[
-L_{i,J}(n):=\{\theta\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},J}(n):
-\theta=p^e\text{ with }e>1\}.
-\]
-Then, for every nonempty $I\subseteq J\subseteq[3]$,
-\[
-\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)=
-\begin{cases}
-P_J(n), & I=J,\ \#J>1,\\[1mm]
-P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n), & I=J=\{i\},\\[1mm]
-L_{i,J}(n), & I=\{i\}\subsetneq J,\\[1mm]
-\varnothing, & \text{otherwise.}
-\end{cases}
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $\theta\in\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$. By definition, $\theta$ is a rank-jump factor with
-$E_n(\theta)=I$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$. If $\theta=p$ is a prime jump, then
-$d^-(\theta)=1$, so every full coordinate is lost after lowering; hence
-$E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$ and $\theta\in P_J(n)$. Conversely, every
-$\theta\in P_J(n)$ has $(E_n(\theta),T_n(\theta))=(J,J)$ by definition.
-
-Now suppose $\theta=p^e$ with $e>1$. The prime--ladder alternative
-(Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}) gives that $E_n(\theta)$ is
-either empty or a singleton. Since $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is defined only for
-nonempty $I$, any such rank-jump factor in it has $I=\{i\}$ for some $i\in J$, and it
-lies in $L_{i,J}(n)$. Conversely, every member of $L_{i,J}(n)$ is a ladder
-rank-jump factor with $(E_n(\theta),T_n(\theta))=(\{i\},J)$ by definition.
-
-Combining the prime jump case with the ladder case gives the four displayed
-alternatives. If $\#I>1$ and $I\ne J$, the prime jump case is impossible
-because prime jumps have $I=J$, while the ladder case is impossible
-because ladder jumps have singleton essential support. Hence the remaining
-families are empty.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Finite slot-selection test]
-\label{lem:finite-slot-selection}
-Let $X$ be a set of at most three labelled slots.  For each $x\in X$, let
-$C_x$ be a finite set of admissible prime powers.  Define
-\[
- \nu(C_x):=\{p:\ p\text{ is the underlying prime of some }p^e\in C_x\}.
-\]
-There are choices $\theta_x\in C_x$ whose underlying primes are pairwise
-distinct if and only if, for every $Y\subseteq X$,
-\[
-\#\bigcup_{y\in Y}\nu(C_y)\ge \#Y .
-\]
-Consequently, in the three-coordinate classification below, a row is decided
-by the finite bipartite graph whose left vertices are the row slots and whose
-right vertices are the admissible underlying primes supplied by the exact-rank
-rank windows and the explicit ladder candidates.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Apply Hall's marriage theorem to the finite family of underlying-prime sets
-$N_x:=\nu(C_x)$, with the slots as the left vertex class
-\cite[Chapter~2]{LovaszPlummer1986MatchingTheory}. Its neighborhood condition
-is exactly the displayed inequality, and a matching saturating all slots is
-equivalent to choosing representatives with distinct underlying primes.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Arithmetic tests for the three-coordinate rank-jump factor families]
-\label{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$, and write
-$a_i:=\nu_{\ell_i}(n)$. For nonempty $J\subseteq[3]$ put
-\[
-\mathcal R_J(n):=\{d\mid n:\ \{k:\nu_{\ell_k}(d)=a_k\}=J\},
-\qquad
-\mathcal R_J^\circ(n):=\mathcal R_J(n)\setminus\{1,2,6,12\}.
-\]
-Use the rank classes $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ from
-Lemma~\ref{article-lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}.
-Then
-\[
-P_J(n)=\bigcup_{d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d),
-\]
-where a prime $p$ is identified with the prime jump $p$. In particular
-$P_J(n)\ne\varnothing$ if and only if $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)\ne\varnothing$.
-More generally, after forbidding a finite set $S$ of primes,
-$P_J(n)\setminus S\ne\varnothing$ if and only if there exists
-$d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ such that
-\[
-\#\Pi_\alpha(d)>
-\#\{p\in S:\alpha(p)=d\},
-\qquad
-\#\Pi_\alpha(d)=\sum_{c\mid d}\mu(d/c)\,\omega(F_c).
-\]
-
-For the ladder families, define a candidate set $\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ as follows.
-If $\ell_i\notin\{2,5\}$, write
-$z_i:=\alpha(\ell_i)$, $h_i:=\nu_{\ell_i}(F_{z_i})$, and
-$s_i:=\nu_{\ell_i}(z_i)$. Then
-\[
-\mathcal L_i^*(n):=
-\begin{cases}
-\{4\}, & \ell_i=2,\ a_i=1,\\
-\{2^{a_i+2}\}, & \ell_i=2,\ a_i\ge2,\\
-\{5^{a_i}\}, & \ell_i=5,\ a_i\ge2,\\
-\varnothing, & \ell_i=5,\ a_i=1,\\
-\{\ell_i^{h_i+a_i-s_i}\}, &
-   \ell_i\notin\{2,5\}\text{ and }a_i>s_i,\\
-\varnothing, &
-   \ell_i\notin\{2,5\}\text{ and }a_i\le s_i .
-\end{cases}
-\]
-For each $i\in J$,
-\[
-L_{i,J}(n)=
-\{\lambda\in\mathcal L_i^*(n):\alpha(\lambda)\mid n,\ 
-\{k:\nu_{\ell_k}(\alpha(\lambda))=a_k\}=J\}.
-\]
-Thus every ladder family $L_{i,J}(n)$ is empty or consists of the single
-displayed prime power.  Hence every labelled three-coordinate slot has an
-explicit finite admissible set: a prime slot is the finite disjoint union
-of the rank classes $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ with
-$d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$, and a ladder slot is decided by the displayed
-single candidate.  Pairwise-coprime filling of any row is therefore exactly
-the finite slot-selection test of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection}; the
-exact-rank prime multiplicities are
-$\#\Pi_\alpha(d)=\sum_{c\mid d}\mu(d/c)\omega(F_c)$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $p\in P_J(n)$ and put $d=\alpha(p)$. Since $p$ is a prime jump,
-$E_n(p)=T_n(p)$, and the condition $T_n(p)=J$ says exactly that
-$d\in\mathcal R_J(n)$. No prime has rank $1$ or $2$, because
-$F_1=F_2=1$. Also no prime has rank $6$ or $12$: the prime divisors of
-$F_6=8$ and $F_{12}=144$ are $2$ and $3$, with
-$\alpha(2)=3$ and $\alpha(3)=4$. Hence $d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$.
-Conversely, if $d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ and $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then
-$d\mid n$ and the full-coordinate set of $d$ is $J$; since $p$ is a prime jump,
-$p\in P_J(n)$. This proves the displayed identity for $P_J(n)$.
-
-The nonemptiness equivalence is precisely where the Fibonacci primitive-divisor
-theorem enters. If $P_J(n)$ is nonempty, the identity just proved gives a rank
-$d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$. Conversely, if
-$\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ is nonempty and $d$ is any element of it, then by
-definition $d\mid n$ and $d\notin\{1,2,6,12\}$. The only possible
-exact-rank obstructions are exactly $1,2,6,12$: ranks $1$ and $2$ occur for
-no prime, ranks $6$ and $12$ occur for no prime as checked above, and
-Theorem~\ref{article-thm:primitive-divisors} supplies a prime $p$ with
-$\alpha(p)=d$ for every remaining $d\ge3$. Thus
-$\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is nonempty for every $d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$, and
-$P_J(n)$ is nonempty exactly when $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ is nonempty. The
-version with a forbidden finite set $S$ is the same rank-by-rank argument after
-removing the primes of $S$: some rank $d$ remains fillable exactly when the
-number of available primes in $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ exceeds the number of forbidden
-primes of that rank. The formula for $\#\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is
-Lemma~\ref{article-lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}.
-
-It remains to identify the ladder families. Let
-$\theta=p^e\in L_{i,J}(n)$. By
-Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, the essential coordinate of a
-ladder jump is the prime coordinate $p$ itself; hence $p=\ell_i$. The
-prime-power formulas in Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave
-only one possible exponent once the $\ell_i$-adic coordinate of
-$\alpha(p^e)$ is required to equal $a_i$. If $\ell_i=2$, the rank-jump ladder
-levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and $2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$;
-therefore the candidate is $4$ when $a_i=1$ and $2^{a_i+2}$ when $a_i\ge2$.
-If $\ell_i=5$, the rank is $5^e$, so a nonprime ladder jump with full
-$5$-coordinate $a_i$ exists only for $a_i\ge2$, and then it is $5^{a_i}$.
-Finally suppose $\ell_i\notin\{2,5\}$. At rank-jump ladder levels,
-\[
-\alpha(\ell_i^e)=\ell_i^{e-h_i}z_i\qquad(e>h_i),
-\]
-so the full-coordinate equation
-$\nu_{\ell_i}(\alpha(\ell_i^e))=a_i$ forces
-$e=h_i+a_i-s_i$, and this is a rank-jump ladder exponent precisely when
-$a_i>s_i$.
-
-Thus every member of $L_{i,J}(n)$ lies in $\mathcal L_i^*(n)$. The remaining
-conditions for membership in $L_{i,J}(n)$ are exactly that its rank divide
-$n$ and that its full-coordinate set be $J$. Conversely, if
-$\lambda\in\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ satisfies those two displayed conditions, the
-same prime-power formulas show that $\lambda$ is a rank-jump ladder. Lowering
-$\lambda$ reduces only the $\ell_i$-coordinate of its rank, so
-$E_n(\lambda)=\{i\}$ and $T_n(\lambda)=J$. Hence
-$\lambda\in L_{i,J}(n)$.
-The displayed exact-rank windows and ladder candidate sets also exhaust the
-exceptional cases: $2$ and $5$ are handled by their separate ladder lines,
-the ranks $1,2,6,12$ are removed from exact-rank windows, and any
-Wall--Sun--Sun plateau for $p\ne2,5$ is already absorbed in the parameter
-$h_i=\nu_{\ell_i}(F_{z_i})$ before the single possible exponent
-$h_i+a_i-s_i$ is formed.
-\end{proof}

-Table~\ref{tab:birth-layer-data-generated} displays the rank level set cardinality $A(n)$
-and the number of minimal generators $\#\mathcal M_n$ for $2\le n\le 30$,
-computed by exhaustive enumeration. The table is illustrative only: the
-unconditional inequalities in Theorem~\ref{article-thm:minimal-generator-growth} do
-not rely on this finite sample. Several features visible in the
-data agree with the structural results of the preceding sections.
-First, $\#\mathcal M_n=1$ whenever $\omega(n)=1$ and
-$n\notin\{19,25,27\}$; the exceptions arise from composite Fibonacci numbers
-with multiple rank-jump families at the same prime-power index.
-Second, the jump at $n=12$ ($A(12)=10$, $\#\mathcal M_{12}=3$) and at $n=24$
-($A(24)=55$, $\#\mathcal M_{24}=4$) reflects the interaction of the
-exceptional prime $2$ with the layers having no exact-rank prime at indices
-$6$ and $12$.

-types $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_4$, $\Gamma_5$, $\Gamma_7$, and $\Gamma_8$.
-The remaining admissible shapes $\Gamma_3$, $\Gamma_6$, and $\Gamma_9$ are
-not realized at $n=30$. This exact five-type assertion, including the three
-nonrealization proofs, is Proposition~\ref{prop:n30-five-type-classification};
-it is not inferred from the table.
-
-The table was produced by the finite divisor/rank computation in the next
-proposition, applied exhaustively for $2\le n\le30$.  The manuscript source
-includes the short script that performs this enumeration and the generated
-table file input below; these files are supplementary to the mathematical
-criterion rather than part of the theorem stream. For the classical
-factorization literature, see the tables of Brillhart--Montgomery--Silverman
-\cite{BrillhartMontgomerySilverman1988Tables}.

-\begin{proposition}[Finite divisor/rank verification with supplied factorization]
-\label{prop:effective-birth-layer-computation}
-Let $n\ge2$ and suppose the integer factorization of $F_n$ is known. Then
-$B_n$, $A(n)$, and $\mathcal M_n$ are recovered exactly by the following finite
-divisor/rank test.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
-\item Enumerate the divisor set $D_n=\operatorname{Div}(F_n)$ from the
- factorization of $F_n$.
-\item Enumerate the divisor set $\operatorname{Div}(n)$. For each
- $q\in D_n$, compute
- \[
- \alpha_n(q):=\min\{d\mid n:q\mid F_d\}.
- \]
-\item Set $B_n=\{q\in D_n:q\ge2,\ \alpha_n(q)=n\}$ and
- $A(n)=\#B_n$.
-\item Sort $B_n$ by divisibility-compatible order, for instance by size, and
- retain exactly those $m\in B_n$ for which no previously retained element
- divides $m$; the retained set is $\mathcal M_n$.
-\end{enumerate}
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Since every $q\in D_n$ divides $F_n$, Proposition~\ref{article-prop:rank-basics}
-shows that $q\mid F_d$ for some $d$ if and only if $\alpha(q)\mid d$. In
-particular $q\mid F_n$ implies $\alpha(q)\mid n$, so the least positive index
-at which $q$ appears is exactly
-\[
-\alpha(q)=\min\{d\mid n:q\mid F_d\}=\alpha_n(q).
-\]
-Hence the test in step (c) gives precisely the definition
-$B_n=\{q\in D_n:\alpha(q)=n\}$, with the harmless exclusion of $q=1$ already
-consistent with the convention $\alpha(1)=1$ and $n\ge2$. Counting this set
-gives $A(n)$.
-
-It remains to justify step (d). The set $B_n$ is finite. If its elements are
-processed in increasing size, then every proper divisor of the current element
-has already been processed. We claim inductively that every discarded element
-has a retained minimal divisor. The claim is vacuous before the first element.
-If the current element is discarded, it has a previously retained divisor by
-the algorithm, so the claim holds for it; if it is retained, it is its own
-retained divisor. Thus every earlier divisor, retained or discarded, has a
-retained divisor below it. Consequently the current element is retained if and
-only if no smaller element of $B_n$ divides it, which is exactly minimality in
-the divisibility poset. The retained set is therefore $\mathcal M_n$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{remark}[Reproducibility scope]
-The preceding proposition is used only to document the finite verification
-interface for the table, not as a complexity theorem.  After the factorization
-of $F_n$ has been supplied, the displayed loops involve only the finite divisor
-sets of $F_n$ and $n$, ordinary divisibility tests $q\mid F_d$, and divisor
-comparisons inside $B_n$.  The manuscript makes no bit-complexity assertion and
-does not include the cost of factoring $F_n$ in the numerical evidence.
-\end{remark}

+\section{Finite enumeration}\label{sec:numerical}
+
+Table~\ref{tab:birth-layer-data-generated} gives $\#B_n$ and
+$\#\mathcal M_n$ for $2\leq n\leq30$. It is obtained by the exact finite
+procedure below. In particular, the row $n=15$ recovers the two generators
+$10$ and $61$ used in the article.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Finite divisor/rank verification]
+\label{prop:effective-birth-layer-computation}
+Let $n\geq2$ and suppose the integer factorization of $F_n$ is known. Then
+$B_n$, $\#B_n$, and $\mathcal M_n$ are recovered exactly as follows.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
+\item Enumerate $D_n=\operatorname{Div}(F_n)$ and $\operatorname{Div}(n)$.
+\item For each $q\in D_n$, compute
+\[
+ \alpha_n(q)=\min\{d\mid n:q\mid F_d\}.
+\]
+\item Set $B_n=\{q\in D_n:q\geq2,\ \alpha_n(q)=n\}$.
+\item Process $B_n$ in increasing order and retain $m$ precisely when no
+previously retained element divides $m$; the retained set is $\mathcal M_n$.
+\end{enumerate}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $q\mid F_n$, Proposition~\ref{article-prop:rank-basics} gives
+$\alpha(q)\mid n$ and
+\[
+ \alpha(q)=\min\{d\mid n:q\mid F_d\}=\alpha_n(q).
+\]
+Thus (c) recovers the exact fiber. For (d), every proper divisor of the current
+element has already been processed. Inductively, every discarded element has
+a retained divisor, so the current element is retained exactly when no
+smaller member of $B_n$ divides it.
+\end{proof}
+

+independent constructions of the finite fibers. Direct divisor/rank
+enumeration and the upper-fiber witness construction agree as sets through

+strict ladder example at $n=91$ through $n=210$. These calculations are

-\begin{lemma}[Finite rank of apparition]\label{lem:finite-rank}
-For every integer $q\ge1$, the rank of apparition $\alpha(q)$ is finite.  More
-precisely, $\alpha(1)=1$, and for every $q\ge2$ there is a positive integer
-$r$ such that $q\mid F_r$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The case $q=1$ is the stated convention.  Let $q\ge2$.  Work modulo $q$ with
-the Fibonacci state vector $(F_m,F_{m+1})$.  The transition
-\[
-(x,y)\longmapsto (y,x+y)
-\]
-has inverse $(x,y)\mapsto (y-x,x)$ modulo $q$, so it is a permutation of the
-finite set $(\ZZ/q\ZZ)^2$.  Therefore the orbit of the initial state $(0,1)$
-is periodic and returns to $(0,1)$ after some positive number $r$ of steps.
-Thus $(F_r,F_{r+1})\equiv(0,1)\pmod q$, in particular $q\mid F_r$.  The
-least such positive $r$ exists by well ordering.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rank-basics}
-Let $q,u,v\ge1$ and let $a,b,m\ge1$. Then:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item $q\mid F_m$ if and only if $\alpha(q)\mid m$.
-\item $\gcd(F_a,F_b)=F_{\gcd(a,b)}$.
-\item $\alpha(\lcmop(u,v))=\lcmop(\alpha(u),\alpha(v))$.
-\end{enumerate}
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The divisibility criterion and the strong-divisibility identity are classical;
-we use them in the forms proved by Wall \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm} and
-Vinson \cite{Vinson1963RankApparition}. The convention $\alpha(1)=1$ makes
-the assertion for $q=1$ immediate.

-\begin{theorem}[Prime inverse rays]\label{thm:prime-inverse-rays}
-Let $y\geq7$ be an integer with $y\neq12$.  There are pairwise distinct
-primes $p_1,p_2,\ldots$ such that, on putting $p_0=y$,
-\[
- \alpha(p_r)=p_{r-1}\qquad(r\geq1).
-\]
-The primes can be chosen so that
-\[
- p_r<E_r(y)\qquad(r\geq1).
-\]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors} gives an exact-rank prime $p_1$ with
-$\alpha(p_1)=y$.  Since $y\geq7$, this prime is not $2$, $3$, or $5$, and
-hence $p_1\geq7$.  Inductively, if $p_r\geq7$ is chosen, then
-$p_r\notin\{6,12\}$, so the same theorem supplies a prime $p_{r+1}$ with
-$\alpha(p_{r+1})=p_r$.  This constructs the ray indefinitely.
-
-No $p_r$ equals $5$: for $r=1$ this follows from $\alpha(p_1)=y\neq5$, and
-for $r>1$ the equality $p_r=5$ would propagate backwards under $\alpha$ to
-$p_1=5$.  If two primes in the ray were equal, that repeated prime would be
-periodic under $\alpha$.  The absence of cycles of length greater than one
-would make it a fixed prime, whereas the fixed-point classification shows
-that the only fixed prime is $5$.  Thus the $p_r$ are pairwise distinct.
-
-Finally, $\alpha(p_r)=p_{r-1}$ implies $p_r\mid F_{p_{r-1}}$.  Since
-$F_d<\varphi^d$ for $d\geq1$, we have
-\[
- p_r\leq F_{p_{r-1}}<\varphi^{p_{r-1}}.
-\]
-Induction on $r$ now gives $p_r<E_r(y)$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Primes in every nontrivial fixed-point basin]
-\label{cor:prime-basins}
-For every fixed point $x>5$, the basin $\Omega_x$ contains infinitely many
-primes.  More precisely, put
-\[
- y_x=\begin{cases}7,&x=12,\\ x,&x\neq12.\end{cases}
-\]
-Then, for every $X>0$,
-\[
- \#\{p\leq X:p\text{ prime},\ p\in\Omega_x\}
- \geq \max\bigl(\{r\geq1:E_r(y_x)\leq X\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).
-\]
-In particular, the lower bound is $\log^*X-O_x(1)$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $x\neq12$, then $x\geq7$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays}
-applied with $y=x$ gives distinct primes whose forward orbits reach $x$.
-For the exceptional fixed point $12$, use
-\[
- \alpha(7)=8,\qquad \alpha(8)=6,\qquad \alpha(6)=12
-\]
-and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays} above $y=7$.  In either case,
-the bound $p_r<E_r(y_x)$ gives the displayed counting estimate.  The
-iterated-logarithm form follows by inverting the fixed-base exponential
-recursion; changing the initial value changes the inverse height by
-$O_x(1)$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Primes of every positive fixed-point order]
-\label{cor:prime-fixed-order}
-For every $k\geq1$, the class $\Lambda_k$ contains infinitely many primes.
-More precisely, for every $X>0$,
-\[
- \#\{p\leq X:p\text{ prime},\ h(p)=k\}
- \geq
- \#\{b\geq1:E_k(12\cdot5^b)\leq X\}.
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Fix $b\geq1$ and put $p_{0,b}=12\cdot5^b$.  Repeating the construction in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays} for $k$ steps gives primes
-$p_{1,b},\ldots,p_{k,b}$ such that
-\[
- \alpha(p_{j,b})=p_{j-1,b}\quad(1\leq j\leq k),
- \qquad p_{k,b}<E_k(12\cdot5^b).
-\]
-The points $p_{1,b},\ldots,p_{k,b}$ are not fixed, so
-$h(p_{k,b})=k$.  If $b\neq b'$, then $p_{k,b}\neq p_{k,b'}$, since applying
-$\alpha^{\circ k}$ would otherwise give
-$12\cdot5^b=12\cdot5^{b'}$.  The asserted bound and infinitude follow.
-\end{proof}
-
-FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga asked whether every $\Lambda_k$ with
-$k\geq1$ contains infinitely many relatively prime integers, and conjectured
-that every $\Omega_x$ with fixed $x>5$ does so
-\cite{FitzGibbonsJavaheriMillerVerga2025Dynamics}. As a direct corollary of
-classical exact-rank prime existence, Corollaries~
-\ref{cor:prime-fixed-order} and \ref{cor:prime-basins} answer both questions
-affirmatively in the stronger prime form. The only input needed is the
-classical exact-rank existence recorded in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors}; the witness-cover and rank-pure
-machinery developed earlier is not used in their proofs.

+\section{Quantitative bounds}\label{sec:growth}
+
+For $n\geq3$, define the rank-window multiplicity precisely by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-window-multiplicity}
+ R(n):=\max\!\left\{1,
+ \max_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}
+ \#\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-jump-family-ladder-slots} shows that this number is
+finite: prime-jump families are finite unions of exact-rank prime classes,
+and each ladder family contains at most one factor.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Deaggregation of a rank window]
+\label{lem:rank-window-deaggregation}
+For $d\mid n$, put
+\[
+ T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}
+\]
+and
+\[
+ A^*(n)=\max\!\left\{1,
+ \max_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)\ne\varnothing}}a(d)\right\}.
+\]
+If $n=\prod_\ell\ell^{e_\ell}$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}
+ 0\leq\log R(n)-\log A^*(n)
+ \leq\log2+\sum_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}\log e_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, let
+\[
+ W_J(n)=\{d\mid n:T_n(d)=J\}.
+\]
+Then $\#W_J(n)=\prod_{\ell\notin J}e_\ell$, and the prime jumps with
+$(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$ form the disjoint union of the classes
+$\Pi_\alpha(d)$ for $d\in W_J(n)$. All other nonempty families are ladder
+families of size at most one. Hence, with
+\[
+ P(n)=\max_{J\ne\varnothing}\sum_{d\in W_J(n)}a(d),
+\]
+we have $P(n)\leq R(n)\leq P(n)+1$. It follows that
+\[
+ A^*(n)\leq R(n)
+ \leq1+A^*(n)\prod_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}e_\ell,
+\]
+which gives \eqref{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:minimal-generator-growth}]
+For $n\geq3$, the strict increase of the Fibonacci sequence from index $2$
+onward gives $\alpha(F_n)=n$. Thus $B_n$ is a nonempty finite poset and
+$\mathcal M_n\ne\varnothing$.
+
+Assume $k\geq3$, order $\mathcal P(n)$, and put $r=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$.
+Choose an $r$-set
+$P\subseteq\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{2,3\}$ and put
+$Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. For each map
+\[
+ H:Q\longrightarrow2^P\setminus\{\varnothing\}
+\]
+and $i\in P$, define
+\[
+ T_i=\{i\}\cup\{q\in Q:i\in H(q)\}.
+\]
+The integer $n_{T_i}$ has a prime divisor outside $\{2,3\}$, so it is not
+$6$ or $12$. Choose an exact-rank prime $\pi_{T_i}$ of rank $n_{T_i}$ by
+Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors}. The supports $T_i$ cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and $i$ is private to $T_i$; hence the primes $\pi_{T_i}$
+form a witness cover. Different maps give different support families and,
+by unique factorization, different elements of $\mathcal M_n$. There are
+$(2^r-1)^{k-r}$ such maps, proving the lower bound.
+
+For the upper bound, let $\Theta$ be a witness cover with $s$ factors. Choose
+the least private coordinate $x_\theta$ of each $\theta\in\Theta$. These
+coordinates are distinct; write $P=\{x_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ and
+$Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. If $x_\theta=x$, then
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=\{x\}\cup U_\theta,\qquad U_\theta\subseteq Q.
+\]
+By Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, either
+$E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$ or $E_n(\theta)=\{x\}$. For fixed $x$ this gives
+at most $2R(n)2^{k-s}$ choices. Ignoring coverage and coprimeness only
+increases the count, so summing over the $\binom{k}{s}$ possible private sets
+and $1\leq s\leq k$ proves the upper bound in
+\eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}.
+
+Finally, $r(k-r)=\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor$ and
+$(k-r)\log(1-2^{-r})=O(1)$. For the upper bound use
+$s(k-s)\leq k^2/4$, $s\leq k$, and
+$\sum_s\binom{k}{s}\leq2^k$. Taking logarithms gives
+\eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}.
+\end{proof}
+
+The term $\omega(n)\log R(n)$ depends on the multiplicities $a(d)$ of
+individual exact ranks, as Lemma~\ref{lem:rank-window-deaggregation} makes
+explicit. Presently available existence and cumulative primitive-divisor
+estimates do not remove this term. Consequently
+\eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order} does not give an unconditional
+almost-all equivalent for $\log\#\mathcal M_n$; such a result would also have
+to control witness covers outside the rank-pure sector.

-\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
-\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
-Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
-$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
-\[
- Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
-              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
- \qquad A:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
-\]
-Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
- Z_V(w)\ge C_k+A-(2^k-1).
-\end{equation}
-This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
-\[
- w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
-\]
-If $k\ge3$, this is the only equality profile.
-
-Consequently, if $n\ge3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
- \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
- \ge C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
- \mathcal W(n)\ge
- 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
-\end{equation}
-Among all positive weight profiles with the same total
-$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact.  The
-extremizing profile is an abstract information-theoretic model; it is not
-asserted to be realized by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
-\[
- \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
- \ge1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
-\]
-Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when
-$S=V$, and otherwise use
-$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$.  Summing the preceding inequality
-over all minimal covers therefore gives
-\[
- Z_V(w)\ge C_k+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}x_S
- =C_k+A-(2^k-1).
-\]
-The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed
-full-support profile has weighted sum
-$C_k-1+w_V=C_k+A-(2^k-1)$, proving sharpness.
-
-Suppose $k\ge3$ and $S$ is proper and nonempty. If $|S|=1$, both the
-singleton partition of $V$ and $\{S,V\setminus S\}$ are minimal covers
-containing $S$. If $|S|\ge2$, choose $s\in S$ and $t\in V\setminus S$; in
-addition to the preceding singleton-complement cover, there is the minimal
-cover consisting of $S$, $\{s,t\}$, and the singletons
-$\{v\}$ for $v\in V\setminus(S\cup\{t\})$. Thus every proper $S$ occurs in
-at least two minimal covers. In the summed linear lower bound its coefficient
-is therefore at least two, so equality forces $x_S=0$ for every proper $S$.
-This proves the equality classification.

-to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of

- \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
- =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
-\]
-Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
-\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
-Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
-\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+If the displayed almost-all formula held, intersecting its validity set with
+the odd integers and the Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order set, then using

-\begin{theorem}[Mean rank-window deaggregation]
-\label{thm:mean-rank-window-deaggregation}
-Put
-\[
- a(d):=\#\Pi_\alpha(d),\qquad
- \mathcal D^+(n):=\{d\mid n:T_n(d)\ne\varnothing\},
-\]
-and
-\[
- A^*(n):=\max\left\{1,\max_{d\in\mathcal D^+(n)}a(d)\right\}.
-\]
-Then, as $x\to\infty$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:mean-window-deaggregation}
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log R(n)
- =\sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log A^*(n)
- +O(x\log\log x).
-\end{equation}
-Consequently the mean sparse-window hypothesis \textup{(H2)} is equivalent to
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:visible-single-rank-interface}
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)
- \log\max\left\{1,
- \max_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)\ne\varnothing}}
- \#\Pi_\alpha(d)\right\}
- =o\bigl(x(\log\log x)^2\bigr).
-\end{equation}
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, let
-\[
- W_J(n):=\{d\mid n:T_n(d)=J\}.
-\]
-If $n=\prod_\ell\ell^{e_\ell}$, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:support-window-size}
- \#W_J(n)=\prod_{\ell\notin J}e_\ell.
-\end{equation}
-The prime jumps in the family with essential and full supports $(J,J)$ form
-the finite disjoint union
-\[
- \coprod_{d\in W_J(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d),
-\]
-because a prime has a unique rank of apparition. By the prime--ladder
-alternative and the unique ladder-slot formula in
-Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy} and
-Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-jump-family-ladder-slots}, every remaining effective
-rank-jump family is a ladder family with singleton essential support and at most
-one rank-jump factor. Therefore, with
-\[
- P(n):=\max_{\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}
-       \sum_{d\in W_J(n)}a(d),
-\]
-one has
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-window-versus-R}
- P(n)\le R(n)\le P(n)+1.
-\end{equation}
-Every $d\in\mathcal D^+(n)$ belongs to one of the windows above. Hence
-\[
- A^*(n)\le R(n)
- \le1+A^*(n)\max_J\#W_J(n)
- \le1+A^*(n)\prod_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}e_\ell.
-\]
-Writing
-\[
- h(n):=\sum_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}\log e_\ell,
-\]
-and using $A^*(n)\ge1$ gives
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}
- 0\le\log R(n)-\log A^*(n)\le\log2+h(n).
-\end{equation}
-For each exponent $e\ge2$, $\log e\le\sum_{2\le j\le e}\log j$, so
-\[
- h(n)\le\sum_{\substack{p^j\mid n\\j\ge2}}\log j.
-\]
-The classical mean estimate \eqref{eq:mean-omega-input}, used uniformly with
-$\log\log(3y)$ in place of $\log\log y$ for small $y$, yields
-\begin{align*}
- \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)h(n)
- &\le\sum_{\substack{p^j\le x\\j\ge2}}\log j
-       \sum_{m\le x/p^j}\omega(p^jm)\\
- &\le\sum_{\substack{p^j\le x\\j\ge2}}\log j
-       \sum_{m\le x/p^j}(1+\omega(m))\\
- &\ll x\log\log x\sum_p\sum_{j\ge2}\frac{\log j}{p^j}
- \ll x\log\log x.
-\end{align*}
-The double series converges absolutely. Summing
-\eqref{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation} and using
-$\sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)\ll x\log\log x$ proves
-\eqref{eq:mean-window-deaggregation}; the stated equivalence follows because
-$x\log\log x=o(x(\log\log x)^2)$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Single-rank sufficient and necessary interfaces]
-\label{cor:single-rank-mean-interfaces}

-\begin{equation}\label{eq:single-rank-sufficient-condition}

-\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--

-\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
-definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
-Thus $\Psi_d(1)$ is the standard Fibonacci cyclotomic, or fibotomic,

-\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
-\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
-Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
-\[
- \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
-\]
-Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
- \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
- \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
-\end{equation}
-For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
-$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
-is $1$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The polynomial factorization
-\[
- F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
-\]
-and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
-functions give
-\[
- \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
-\]
-Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
-$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
-value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
-negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
-
-If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
-divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
-$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
-$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
-$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
-exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
-any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
-follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
-primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
-\end{proof}
