-\begin{lemma}[Finite rank of apparition]\label{lem:finite-rank}
-For every integer $q\ge1$, the rank of apparition $\alpha(q)$ is finite.  More
-precisely, $\alpha(1)=1$, and for every $q\ge2$ there is a positive integer
-$r$ such that $q\mid F_r$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The case $q=1$ is the stated convention.  Let $q\ge2$.  Work modulo $q$ with
-the Fibonacci state vector $(F_m,F_{m+1})$.  The transition
-\[
-(x,y)\longmapsto (y,x+y)
-\]
-has inverse $(x,y)\mapsto (y-x,x)$ modulo $q$, so it is a permutation of the
-finite set $(\ZZ/q\ZZ)^2$.  Therefore the orbit of the initial state $(0,1)$
-is periodic and returns to $(0,1)$ after some positive number $r$ of steps.
-Thus $(F_r,F_{r+1})\equiv(0,1)\pmod q$, in particular $q\mid F_r$.  The
-least such positive $r$ exists by well ordering.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rank-basics}
-Let $q,u,v\ge1$ and let $a,b,m\ge1$. Then:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item $q\mid F_m$ if and only if $\alpha(q)\mid m$.
-\item $\gcd(F_a,F_b)=F_{\gcd(a,b)}$.
-\item $\alpha(\lcmop(u,v))=\lcmop(\alpha(u),\alpha(v))$.
-\end{enumerate}
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The divisibility criterion and the strong-divisibility identity are classical;
-we use them in the forms proved by Wall \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm} and
-Vinson \cite{Vinson1963RankApparition}. The convention $\alpha(1)=1$ makes
-the assertion for $q=1$ immediate.

-\cite{LucaTron2015SelfFibonacciDivisors}; Renault gives the corresponding
-identity for the more general $(a,b)$-Fibonacci sequences
-\cite{Renault2013PeriodRankOrder}. For completeness, an integer $m$ is

+The finiteness of $\alpha(q)$ follows from the periodicity of the Fibonacci
+state vector modulo $q$; see, for example, Wall
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. We use the following standard facts.
+
+\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rank-basics}
+For positive integers $q,u,v,a,b,m$,
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $q\mid F_m$ if and only if $\alpha(q)\mid m$;
+\item $\gcd(F_a,F_b)=F_{\gcd(a,b)}$;
+\item $\alpha(\lcmop(u,v))=\lcmop(\alpha(u),\alpha(v))$.
+\end{enumerate}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The first two statements are classical
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm,Vinson1963RankApparition}. For the last, an integer
+$m$ is divisible by $\alpha(\lcmop(u,v))$ exactly when both $u$ and $v$
+divide $F_m$, hence exactly when both $\alpha(u)$ and $\alpha(v)$ divide $m$.
+The two sides therefore have the same positive multiples. This lcm identity
+also appears in \cite{LucaTron2015SelfFibonacciDivisors,Renault2013PeriodRankOrder}.
+\end{proof}
+
+We call $p$ an \emph{exact-rank prime of rank $d$} when $\alpha(p)=d$.
+The term \emph{primitive divisor of $F_d$} retains its standard meaning: a
+prime dividing $F_d$ but not $5F_1\cdots F_{d-1}$. Thus the exact-rank prime
+$5$ at rank $5$ is not primitive in this terminology.

+$\alpha(p_n)=n$.

+supplies a prime dividing $F_n$ and no earlier Fibonacci number, so its rank
+is $n$.
+\end{proof}

-\section{A prime inverse-ray application}\label{sec:inverse-dynamics}
-%% ====================================================================
-
-Write $\operatorname{Fix}(\alpha)$ for the fixed points of the rank map.  For
-$m\geq1$, define its \emph{fixed-point order} by
-\[
- h(m):=\min\{k\geq0:\alpha^{\circ k}(m)\in
- \operatorname{Fix}(\alpha)\},
- \qquad
- \Lambda_k:=\{m\geq1:h(m)=k\}.
-\]
-For $x\in\operatorname{Fix}(\alpha)$, define its basin by
-\[
- \Omega_x:=\{m\geq1:\alpha^{\circ j}(m)=x
- \text{ for some }j\geq0\}.
-\]
-These are the conventions of FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga
-\cite{FitzGibbonsJavaheriMillerVerga2025Dynamics}. The fixed-point
-classification is due to Marques \cite{Marques2012OrderAppearance}:
-\[
- \operatorname{Fix}(\alpha)=\{5^a:a\geq0\}
- \cup\{12\cdot5^a:a\geq0\}
-\]
-Luca--Tron proved that every orbit reaches one of these fixed points
-\cite{LucaTron2015SelfFibonacciDivisors}. In particular, the rank map has no
-cycles of length greater than one. FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga are
-cited below for their questions and terminology, not as the first source of
-these two imported theorems.
-
-No new prime-existence input is proved in this section. Every prime selected
-below comes directly from Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors}.
-
-Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$ and, for $t>0$, set
-\[
- E_0(t)=t,\qquad E_{r+1}(t)=\varphi^{E_r(t)}\quad(r\geq0).
-\]
-
-\begin{theorem}[Prime inverse rays]\label{thm:prime-inverse-rays}
-Let $y\geq7$ be an integer with $y\neq12$.  There are pairwise distinct
-primes $p_1,p_2,\ldots$ such that, on putting $p_0=y$,
-\[
- \alpha(p_r)=p_{r-1}\qquad(r\geq1).
-\]
-The primes can be chosen so that
-\[
- p_r<E_r(y)\qquad(r\geq1).
-\]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors} gives an exact-rank prime $p_1$ with
-$\alpha(p_1)=y$.  Since $y\geq7$, this prime is not $2$, $3$, or $5$, and
-hence $p_1\geq7$.  Inductively, if $p_r\geq7$ is chosen, then
-$p_r\notin\{6,12\}$, so the same theorem supplies a prime $p_{r+1}$ with
-$\alpha(p_{r+1})=p_r$.  This constructs the ray indefinitely.
-
-No $p_r$ equals $5$: for $r=1$ this follows from $\alpha(p_1)=y\neq5$, and
-for $r>1$ the equality $p_r=5$ would propagate backwards under $\alpha$ to
-$p_1=5$.  If two primes in the ray were equal, that repeated prime would be
-periodic under $\alpha$.  The absence of cycles of length greater than one
-would make it a fixed prime, whereas the fixed-point classification shows
-that the only fixed prime is $5$.  Thus the $p_r$ are pairwise distinct.
-
-Finally, $\alpha(p_r)=p_{r-1}$ implies $p_r\mid F_{p_{r-1}}$.  Since
-$F_d<\varphi^d$ for $d\geq1$, we have
-\[
- p_r\leq F_{p_{r-1}}<\varphi^{p_{r-1}}.
-\]
-Induction on $r$ now gives $p_r<E_r(y)$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Primes in every nontrivial fixed-point basin]
-\label{cor:prime-basins}
-For every fixed point $x>5$, the basin $\Omega_x$ contains infinitely many
-primes.  More precisely, put
-\[
- y_x=\begin{cases}7,&x=12,\\ x,&x\neq12.\end{cases}
-\]
-Then, for every $X>0$,
-\[
- \#\{p\leq X:p\text{ prime},\ p\in\Omega_x\}
- \geq \max\bigl(\{r\geq1:E_r(y_x)\leq X\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).
-\]
-In particular, the lower bound is $\log^*X-O_x(1)$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $x\neq12$, then $x\geq7$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays}
-applied with $y=x$ gives distinct primes whose forward orbits reach $x$.
-For the exceptional fixed point $12$, use
-\[
- \alpha(7)=8,\qquad \alpha(8)=6,\qquad \alpha(6)=12
-\]
-and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays} above $y=7$.  In either case,
-the bound $p_r<E_r(y_x)$ gives the displayed counting estimate.  The
-iterated-logarithm form follows by inverting the fixed-base exponential
-recursion; changing the initial value changes the inverse height by
-$O_x(1)$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Primes of every positive fixed-point order]
-\label{cor:prime-fixed-order}
-For every $k\geq1$, the class $\Lambda_k$ contains infinitely many primes.
-More precisely, for every $X>0$,
-\[
- \#\{p\leq X:p\text{ prime},\ h(p)=k\}
- \geq
- \#\{b\geq1:E_k(12\cdot5^b)\leq X\}.
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Fix $b\geq1$ and put $p_{0,b}=12\cdot5^b$.  Repeating the construction in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:prime-inverse-rays} for $k$ steps gives primes
-$p_{1,b},\ldots,p_{k,b}$ such that
-\[
- \alpha(p_{j,b})=p_{j-1,b}\quad(1\leq j\leq k),
- \qquad p_{k,b}<E_k(12\cdot5^b).
-\]
-The points $p_{1,b},\ldots,p_{k,b}$ are not fixed, so
-$h(p_{k,b})=k$.  If $b\neq b'$, then $p_{k,b}\neq p_{k,b'}$, since applying
-$\alpha^{\circ k}$ would otherwise give
-$12\cdot5^b=12\cdot5^{b'}$.  The asserted bound and infinitude follow.
-\end{proof}
-
-FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga asked whether every $\Lambda_k$ with
-$k\geq1$ contains infinitely many relatively prime integers, and conjectured
-that every $\Omega_x$ with fixed $x>5$ does so
-\cite{FitzGibbonsJavaheriMillerVerga2025Dynamics}. As a direct corollary of
-classical exact-rank prime existence, Corollaries~
-\ref{cor:prime-fixed-order} and \ref{cor:prime-basins} answer both questions
-affirmatively in the stronger prime form. The only input needed is the
-classical exact-rank existence recorded in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors}; the witness-cover and rank-pure
-machinery developed earlier is not used in their proofs.

+\section{Quantitative bounds}\label{sec:growth}
+
+For $n\geq3$, define the rank-window multiplicity precisely by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-window-multiplicity}
+ R(n):=\max\!\left\{1,
+ \max_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}
+ \#\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-jump-family-ladder-slots} shows that this number is
+finite: prime-jump families are finite unions of exact-rank prime classes,
+and each ladder family contains at most one factor.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Deaggregation of a rank window]
+\label{lem:rank-window-deaggregation}
+For $d\mid n$, put
+\[
+ T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}
+\]
+and
+\[
+ A^*(n)=\max\!\left\{1,
+ \max_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)\ne\varnothing}}a(d)\right\}.
+\]
+If $n=\prod_\ell\ell^{e_\ell}$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}
+ 0\leq\log R(n)-\log A^*(n)
+ \leq\log2+\sum_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}\log e_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, let
+\[
+ W_J(n)=\{d\mid n:T_n(d)=J\}.
+\]
+Then $\#W_J(n)=\prod_{\ell\notin J}e_\ell$, and the prime jumps with
+$(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$ form the disjoint union of the classes
+$\Pi_\alpha(d)$ for $d\in W_J(n)$. All other nonempty families are ladder
+families of size at most one. Hence, with
+\[
+ P(n)=\max_{J\ne\varnothing}\sum_{d\in W_J(n)}a(d),
+\]
+we have $P(n)\leq R(n)\leq P(n)+1$. It follows that
+\[
+ A^*(n)\leq R(n)
+ \leq1+A^*(n)\prod_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}e_\ell,
+\]
+which gives \eqref{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:minimal-generator-growth}]
+For $n\geq3$, the strict increase of the Fibonacci sequence from index $2$
+onward gives $\alpha(F_n)=n$. Thus $B_n$ is a nonempty finite poset and
+$\mathcal M_n\ne\varnothing$.
+
+Assume $k\geq3$, order $\mathcal P(n)$, and put $r=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$.
+Choose an $r$-set
+$P\subseteq\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{2,3\}$ and put
+$Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. For each map
+\[
+ H:Q\longrightarrow2^P\setminus\{\varnothing\}
+\]
+and $i\in P$, define
+\[
+ T_i=\{i\}\cup\{q\in Q:i\in H(q)\}.
+\]
+The integer $n_{T_i}$ has a prime divisor outside $\{2,3\}$, so it is not
+$6$ or $12$. Choose an exact-rank prime $\pi_{T_i}$ of rank $n_{T_i}$ by
+Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors}. The supports $T_i$ cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and $i$ is private to $T_i$; hence the primes $\pi_{T_i}$
+form a witness cover. Different maps give different support families and,
+by unique factorization, different elements of $\mathcal M_n$. There are
+$(2^r-1)^{k-r}$ such maps, proving the lower bound.
+
+For the upper bound, let $\Theta$ be a witness cover with $s$ factors. Choose
+the least private coordinate $x_\theta$ of each $\theta\in\Theta$. These
+coordinates are distinct; write $P=\{x_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ and
+$Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. If $x_\theta=x$, then
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=\{x\}\cup U_\theta,\qquad U_\theta\subseteq Q.
+\]
+By Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, either
+$E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$ or $E_n(\theta)=\{x\}$. For fixed $x$ this gives
+at most $2R(n)2^{k-s}$ choices. Ignoring coverage and coprimeness only
+increases the count, so summing over the $\binom{k}{s}$ possible private sets
+and $1\leq s\leq k$ proves the upper bound in
+\eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}.
+
+Finally, $r(k-r)=\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor$ and
+$(k-r)\log(1-2^{-r})=O(1)$. For the upper bound use
+$s(k-s)\leq k^2/4$, $s\leq k$, and
+$\sum_s\binom{k}{s}\leq2^k$. Taking logarithms gives
+\eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}.
+\end{proof}
+
+The term $\omega(n)\log R(n)$ depends on the multiplicities $a(d)$ of
+individual exact ranks, as Lemma~\ref{lem:rank-window-deaggregation} makes
+explicit. Presently available existence and cumulative primitive-divisor
+estimates do not remove this term. Consequently
+\eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order} does not give an unconditional
+almost-all equivalent for $\log\#\mathcal M_n$; such a result would also have
+to control witness covers outside the rank-pure sector.

-\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
-\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
-Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
-$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
-\[
- Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}

-\]

-\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}

-\end{equation}
-This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
-\[

-Among all positive weight profiles with the same total

-\begin{proof}
-Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,

-Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when

-\[

-The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed

-addition to the preceding singleton-complement cover, there is the minimal
-cover consisting of $S$, $\{s,t\}$, and the singletons
-$\{v\}$ for $v\in V\setminus(S\cup\{t\})$. Thus every proper $S$ occurs in
-at least two minimal covers. In the summed linear lower bound its coefficient
-is therefore at least two, so equality forces $x_S=0$ for every proper $S$.
-This proves the equality classification.
-
-For odd squarefree $n$, the nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond
-to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of
-$F_n$, and $a(1)=0$, so
-\[
- \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
- =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
-\]
-Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
-\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
-Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
-\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+If the displayed almost-all formula held, intersecting its validity set with
+the odd integers and the Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order set, then using
+$\#\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}\le\#\mathcal M_n$, would force
+\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-dispersion-interface}.
 \end{proof}

-\section{Support entropy and the unresolved arithmetic multiplicity}
-\label{sec:growth}
-%% ====================================================================
-
-Write $\Omega(N)=\sum_p\nu_p(N)$ for the number of prime factors of $N$
-counted with multiplicity. Set $R(2)=1$, consistently with
-$\mathcal M_2=\varnothing$. For $n\ge3$ define the maximal rank-window
-multiplicity
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-window-multiplicity}
- R(n):=\max\!\left\{1,
- \max_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}
-       \#\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)\right\}.
-\end{equation}
-By the prime--ladder alternative, the nonsingleton families counted here are the
-exact-rank windows $P_J(n)$, whereas every ladder family contributes at most
-one rank-jump factor. Thus $R(n)$ records the maximal rank-jump-family multiplicity retained
-by the counting bounds below. It is an exact parameter for those bounds, but
-it is not asserted to be an information-theoretically complete invariant of
-the arithmetic outside the support combinatorics.
-
-We first remove the contribution caused solely by collecting several exact
-rank classes in one support window. For $d\mid n$, write
-\[
- T_n(d):=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
- \nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}.
-\]
-
-\begin{theorem}[Mean rank-window deaggregation]
-\label{thm:mean-rank-window-deaggregation}
-Put
-\[
- a(d):=\#\Pi_\alpha(d),\qquad
- \mathcal D^+(n):=\{d\mid n:T_n(d)\ne\varnothing\},
-\]
-and
-\[
- A^*(n):=\max\left\{1,\max_{d\in\mathcal D^+(n)}a(d)\right\}.
-\]
-Then, as $x\to\infty$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:mean-window-deaggregation}
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log R(n)
- =\sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log A^*(n)
- +O(x\log\log x).
-\end{equation}
-Consequently the mean sparse-window hypothesis \textup{(H2)} is equivalent to
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:visible-single-rank-interface}
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)
- \log\max\left\{1,
- \max_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)\ne\varnothing}}
- \#\Pi_\alpha(d)\right\}
- =o\bigl(x(\log\log x)^2\bigr).
-\end{equation}
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, let
-\[
- W_J(n):=\{d\mid n:T_n(d)=J\}.
-\]
-If $n=\prod_\ell\ell^{e_\ell}$, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:support-window-size}
- \#W_J(n)=\prod_{\ell\notin J}e_\ell.
-\end{equation}
-The prime jumps in the family with essential and full supports $(J,J)$ form
-the finite disjoint union
-\[
- \coprod_{d\in W_J(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d),
-\]
-because a prime has a unique rank of apparition. By the prime--ladder
-alternative and the unique ladder-slot formula in
-Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy} and
-Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-jump-family-ladder-slots}, every remaining effective
-rank-jump family is a ladder family with singleton essential support and at most
-one rank-jump factor. Therefore, with
-\[
- P(n):=\max_{\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}
-       \sum_{d\in W_J(n)}a(d),
-\]
-one has
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-window-versus-R}
- P(n)\le R(n)\le P(n)+1.
-\end{equation}
-Every $d\in\mathcal D^+(n)$ belongs to one of the windows above. Hence
-\[
- A^*(n)\le R(n)
- \le1+A^*(n)\max_J\#W_J(n)
- \le1+A^*(n)\prod_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}e_\ell.
-\]
-Writing
-\[
- h(n):=\sum_{\ell^{e_\ell}\parallel n}\log e_\ell,
-\]
-and using $A^*(n)\ge1$ gives
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation}
- 0\le\log R(n)-\log A^*(n)\le\log2+h(n).
-\end{equation}
-For each exponent $e\ge2$, $\log e\le\sum_{2\le j\le e}\log j$, so
-\[
- h(n)\le\sum_{\substack{p^j\mid n\\j\ge2}}\log j.
-\]
-The classical mean estimate \eqref{eq:mean-omega-input}, used uniformly with
-$\log\log(3y)$ in place of $\log\log y$ for small $y$, yields
-\begin{align*}
- \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)h(n)
- &\le\sum_{\substack{p^j\le x\\j\ge2}}\log j
-       \sum_{m\le x/p^j}\omega(p^jm)\\
- &\le\sum_{\substack{p^j\le x\\j\ge2}}\log j
-       \sum_{m\le x/p^j}(1+\omega(m))\\
- &\ll x\log\log x\sum_p\sum_{j\ge2}\frac{\log j}{p^j}
- \ll x\log\log x.
-\end{align*}
-The double series converges absolutely. Summing
-\eqref{eq:pointwise-window-deaggregation} and using
-$\sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)\ll x\log\log x$ proves
-\eqref{eq:mean-window-deaggregation}; the stated equivalence follows because
-$x\log\log x=o(x(\log\log x)^2)$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Single-rank sufficient and necessary interfaces]
-\label{cor:single-rank-mean-interfaces}
-A sufficient condition for \textup{(H2)} is
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:single-rank-sufficient-condition}
- \sum_{d\le x}
- \frac{(\omega(d)+\log\log x)\log\max\{1,a(d)\}}{d}
- =o\bigl((\log\log x)^2\bigr).
-\end{equation}
-Conversely, \textup{(H2)} implies the diagonal necessary condition
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:single-rank-necessary-condition}
- \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)\log\max\{1,a(n)\}
- =o\bigl(x(\log\log x)^2\bigr).
-\end{equation}
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Since
-\[
- \log A^*(n)\le\sum_{d\mid n}\log\max\{1,a(d)\},
-\]
-the substitution $n=dm$ and $\omega(dm)\le\omega(d)+\omega(m)$ gives
-\[
- \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)\log A^*(n)
- \ll x\sum_{d\le x}
- \frac{(\omega(d)+\log\log x)\log\max\{1,a(d)\}}{d}.
-\]
-Thus \eqref{eq:single-rank-sufficient-condition} and
-Theorem~\ref{thm:mean-rank-window-deaggregation} imply \textup{(H2)}. For the
-necessary condition, $n\in\mathcal D^+(n)$, and hence
-$R(n)\ge A^*(n)\ge\max\{1,a(n)\}$; summation proves the claim.
-\end{proof}

-The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
-\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
-polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
-\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
-Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
-\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
-definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
-Thus $\Psi_d(1)$ is the standard Fibonacci cyclotomic, or fibotomic,
-integer; only the notation $\mathfrak F_d$ below is local to this paper.
-
-\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
-\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
-Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
-\[
- \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
-\]
-Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
- \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
- \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
-\end{equation}
-For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
-$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
-is $1$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The polynomial factorization
-\[
- F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
-\]
-and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
-functions give
-\[
- \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
-\]
-Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
-$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
-value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
-negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
-
-If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
-divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
-$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
-$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
-$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
-exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
-any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
-follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
-primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
-\label{thm:fibotomic-rank-entropy}
-Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, let $\phi_{\rm E}$ denote Euler's totient
-function, and, for $d\geq3$, put
-\[
- \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
-\]
-For $k\geq0$, set $m=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ and
-\[
- \mathcal H_d(k):=
- k\log\frac{2d}{3}+2\log(m!)+(k-2m)\log(m+1).
-\]
-There is an absolute constant $C_F$ such that, for every $d\geq3$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy}
- \mathcal H_d(a(d))\leq \phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi+C_F.
-\end{equation}
-More generally, every finitely supported family of nonnegative real numbers
-$(\lambda_d)_{d\geq3}$ satisfies
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-fibotomic-rank-entropy}
- \sum_{d\geq3}\lambda_d\mathcal H_d(a(d))
- \leq (\log\varphi)\sum_{d\geq3}\lambda_d\phi_{\rm E}(d)
-       +C_F\sum_{d\geq3}\lambda_d.
-\end{equation}
-Uniformly as $d\to\infty$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound}
- a(d)\leq
- \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
- \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(d)}{\log d}.
-\end{equation}
-Consequently, uniformly as $n\to\infty$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:visible-exact-rank-bound}
- A^*(n)\leq
- \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
- \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{\log n}.
-\end{equation}
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Binet's formula, in the form
-\[
- F_r=\frac{\varphi^r}{\sqrt5}
- \bigl(1-(-\varphi^{-2})^r\bigr),
-\]
-and the identities
-$\sum_{r\mid d}\mu(d/r)=0$ and
-$\sum_{r\mid d}r\mu(d/r)=\phi_{\rm E}(d)$ show that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-binet-error}
- \log\mathfrak F_d=\phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi+E_d,
- \qquad
- |E_d|\leq
- C_F:=\sum_{j\geq1}
- \left|\log\bigl(1-(-\varphi^{-2})^j\bigr)\right|.
-\end{equation}
-The series defining $C_F$ converges geometrically.
-
-Lemma~\ref{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical} gives the exact-rank radical
-divisibility with no cancellation ambiguity.
-For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, the classical rank congruence gives
-\[
- d=\alpha(p)\mid p-\left(\frac5p\right),
-\]
-see \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm,Vinson1963RankApparition}. Thus
-$p\equiv\pm1\pmod d$. The ranks $d=3,5$ have respectively the single
-exact-rank primes $2,5$ and satisfy the estimate directly; the layers
-$d=6,12$ are empty and also satisfy it. For every remaining $d$, write the
-exact-rank primes in increasing order as
-$p_1<\cdots<p_k$. There are at most two candidates in each pair of residue
-classes $jd\pm1$, whence
-\[
- p_i\geq d\left\lceil\frac i2\right\rceil-1
- \geq\frac{2d}{3}\left\lceil\frac i2\right\rceil.
-\]
-It follows that, with $m=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-congruence-product-bound}
- \prod_{i=1}^kp_i\geq
- \left(\frac{2d}{3}\right)^k(m!)^2(m+1)^{k-2m}.
-\end{equation}
-Combining \eqref{eq:fibotomic-binet-error}--
-\eqref{eq:rank-congruence-product-bound} and taking logarithms proves
-\eqref{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy}. Multiplication by $\lambda_d\geq0$ and
-finite summation proves \eqref{eq:weighted-fibotomic-rank-entropy}.
-
-Stirling's lower bound applied in \eqref{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy} gives,
-with an absolute implied constant,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-entropy-coarse}
- a(d)\bigl(\log d+\log\max\{1,a(d)\}-O(1)\bigr)
- \leq \phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi+O(1).
-\end{equation}
-Fix $\varepsilon>0$. If $a(d)\leq\phi_{\rm E}(d)/(\log d)^2$, then
-\eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} follows immediately. Otherwise the
-standard uniform lower bound
-$\phi_{\rm E}(d)\gg d/\log\log(3d)$
-\cite{HardyWright2008Introduction} implies
-\[
- \log a(d)=\log d+O(\log\log d)=\log d+o(\log d).
-\]
-Substitution in \eqref{eq:rank-entropy-coarse} yields, for all sufficiently
-large $d$ depending only on $\varepsilon$,
-$(2+o(1))a(d)\log d\leq\phi_{\rm E}(d)\log\varphi$, proving
-\eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} with its $o(1)$ uniform over every
-$d$ beyond that threshold.
-
-For \eqref{eq:visible-exact-rank-bound}, the case $A^*(n)=1$ follows from
-$\phi_{\rm E}(n)/\log n\to\infty$. Otherwise choose
-$d_n\in\mathcal D^+(n)$ with $A^*(n)=a(d_n)$. The preceding estimate has
-the coarse consequence $a(d)\ll d/\log(2d)$. If
-$d_n\leq n/(\log n)^3$, the lower bound for $\phi_{\rm E}(n)$ gives
-\[
- a(d_n)=o\left(\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{\log n}\right).
-\]
-If $d_n>n/(\log n)^3$, then
-$\log d_n=(1+o(1))\log n$ and, since $d_n\mid n$,
-$\phi_{\rm E}(d_n)\leq\phi_{\rm E}(n)$. Applying
-\eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} at $d_n$ completes the proof. The two
-cases use thresholds depending only on $\varepsilon$, so the final $o(1)$ is
-uniform over all $n$ beyond a common threshold.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Exact support spectra and the extremal slice]
-\label{thm:exact-support-spectra}
-Let $n\ge3$, write
-\[
- n=\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\ell^{a_\ell},
- \qquad k=\omega(n),
-\]
-and put
-\[
- \Sigma(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n\},\qquad
- \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n^{\rm conn}\}.
-\]
-For each $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$, define the singleton diagonal rank-jump family
-\[
- \mathcal A_\ell(n):=
- \mathcal A_{\{\ell\},\{\ell\}}(n).
-\]
-Then multiplication gives a bijection
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection}
- \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\mathcal A_\ell(n)
- \longrightarrow
- \{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\},
- \qquad (\theta_\ell)_\ell\longmapsto
- \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\theta_\ell.
-\end{equation}
-In particular,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-count}
- \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\}
- =\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\#\mathcal A_\ell(n).
-\end{equation}
-The complete support spectrum is
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}
- \Sigma(n)=
- \begin{cases}
-  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},&n\text{ is even and squarefree},\\
-  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
- \end{cases}
-\end{equation}
-For the connected spectrum, $\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=\{1\}$ when $k=1$.
-If $k\ge2$, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}
- \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=
- \begin{cases}
-  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},
-   &\begin{array}{l}
-     n\text{ is squarefree, or }n=12s\text{ with }s\text{ squarefree}\
-     \text{and }\gcd(s,6)=1,
-    \end{array}\\[2mm]
-  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
- \end{cases}
-\end{equation}
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-We first classify the extremal slice. Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ have
-$\omega(m)=k$, and let $\Theta(m)$ be its witness cover. For every
-$\theta\in\Theta(m)$, choose a private coordinate
-\[
- \ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
- \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta(m),\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta).
-\]
-The chosen coordinates are distinct, since a coordinate chosen for two rank-jump factors
-would lie in the full support of each and hence would not be private to either.
-There are $k$ rank-jump factors and $k$ coordinates, so $\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a
-bijection. If $q\ne\ell(\theta)$, then $q$ is private to another rank-jump factor and
-therefore cannot lie in $T_n(\theta)$. Hence
-\[
- T_n(\theta)=E_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}.
-\]
-Thus the inverse of \eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection} sends $m$
-to its uniquely labelled rank-jump factors in the families $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$.
-
-Conversely, choose $\theta_\ell\in\mathcal A_\ell(n)$ for every
-$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$.
-These rank-jump factors are pairwise coprime. Indeed, if
-$\theta_\ell=p^e$ and $\theta_q=p^f$ had the same underlying prime, then
-$e\ne f$ because the same rank-jump factor cannot lie in two differently labelled
-families. Say $e<f$. Then $p^e\mid p^{f-1}$ would give
-\[
- d(\theta_\ell)\mid d^-(\theta_q).
-\]
-Since $\ell$ occurs to its full $n$-adic exponent in $d(\theta_\ell)$, it
-would also occur fully in $d(\theta_q)$, contrary to
-$T_n(\theta_q)=\{q\}$ and $q\ne\ell$. The singleton full supports cover
-$\mathcal P(n)$, and the singleton essential supports are private. Hence the
-chosen rank-jump factors form an $n$-witness cover. The witness-cover theorem proves that
-their product belongs to $\mathcal M_n$ and has $k$ distinct prime factors.
-Uniqueness follows from unique factorization. This proves the bijection and
-\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count}.
-
-We next decide when the factors on the right of
-\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count} are nonzero. If $\ell$ is odd, or
-if $\ell=2$ and $a_2\ge2$, then the exact-rank existence theorem supplies a
-prime of rank $\ell^{a_\ell}$; this is an element of
-$\mathcal A_\ell(n)$. Suppose now that $a_2=1$. If $n$ is squarefree and
-$\theta\in\mathcal A_2(n)$, then $d(\theta)\mid n$ cannot contain an odd
-coordinate: every such coordinate would occur fully and would belong to
-$T_n(\theta)$. Thus $d(\theta)=2$, which is impossible because $F_2=1$ and
-$\Atom(2)=\varnothing$. Therefore the extremal slice is empty when $n$ is
-even and squarefree.
-
-If instead $a_2=1$ and $q^2\mid n$ for some odd prime $q$, take a rank-jump factor of
-rank $2q$. For $q=3$, the rank-jump factor $4\in\Atom(6)$ has, relative to $n$,
-$E_n(4)=T_n(4)=\{2\}$. For $q\ge5$, the rank $2q$ is nonexceptional, so an
-exact-rank prime exists and again has essential and full support $\{2\}$,
-because the $q$-coordinate is sub-full in $n$. Thus
-$\mathcal A_2(n)\ne\varnothing$. All other diagonal families were already
-seen to be nonempty, proving that the support value $k$ occurs exactly in the
-second case of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
-
-It remains to realize every smaller support size. Assume $k\ge2$ and
-$1\le r\le k-1$. Choose a partition $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P(n)$ into $r$
-nonempty blocks, with the additional condition that $\{2\}$ is not a block
-when $a_2=1$. Such a partition exists because $r<k$. For $C\in\Pi$, put
-$n_C=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{a_\ell}$ and choose
-$\theta_C\in\Atom(n_C)$. This is possible by exact-rank prime existence
-unless $n_C\in\{6,12\}$; in those two cases use respectively
-$4\in\Atom(6)$ and $16\in\Atom(12)$. The forbidden rank $2$ was excluded by
-the choice of $\Pi$. Strong divisibility makes the rank-jump factors belonging to
-disjoint blocks pairwise coprime. Their full supports are the blocks $C$, and
-each has a nonempty essential support because lowering it decreases its rank.
-They therefore form an $n$-witness cover. Its product has exactly $r$ prime
-factors, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
-
-The same idea gives all connected support sizes below $k$. Choose a hub
-$h\in\mathcal P(n)$, taking $h=3$ whenever
-$\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ and $n_{\{2,3\}}\in\{6,12\}$, and partition
-$\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{h\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.
-Use one rank-jump factor of exact rank $n_{\{h\}\cup P_i}$ for each $i$. The only
-exceptional support that can occur is $\{2,3\}$; use $4$ at rank $6$ or $16$
-at rank $12$. In both cases its essential support contains the private
-coordinate $2\in P_i$. Every nonexceptional rank-jump factor is a prime jump and has any
-coordinate of the nonempty set $P_i$ as a private coordinate. The rank-jump factors are
-pairwise coprime: their ranks are distinct, and the exceptional rank-jump factor has
-underlying prime $2$, whose rank $3$ is not one of the other multi-coordinate
-ranks. The resulting witness cover is connected because all its rank-support
-edges contain $h$. Thus
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}
- \{1,\ldots,k-1\}\subseteq\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)\qquad(k\ge2).
-\end{equation}
-
-We finally decide whether the endpoint $k$ can be connected. In an extremal
-witness cover, write $\theta_\ell$ for the rank-jump factor with
-$T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}$ and let
-$S_\ell=\operatorname{supp}_n(d(\theta_\ell))$ be its positive-coordinate
-rank support. If $q\in S_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}$, then
-\[
- 1\le\nu_q(d(\theta_\ell))<a_q,
-\]
-so necessarily $a_q\ge2$. If $n$ is squarefree, every $S_\ell$ is therefore
-the singleton $\{\ell\}$, and the rank-support hypergraph is disconnected
-when $k\ge2$.
-
-There is one further obstruction. Let $n=12s$ with $s$ squarefree and
-$\gcd(s,6)=1$. The only coordinate of exponent at least two is $2$. Hence an
-edge $S_3$ larger than $\{3\}$ would force $d(\theta_3)=6$. But
-$\Atom(6)=\{4\}$, and lowering $4$ gives rank $3$; relative to this $n$, the
-$3$-coordinate is not lost. Thus a rank-jump factor of rank $6$ with
-$T_n(\theta_3)=\{3\}$ has empty essential support and cannot occur in a
-witness cover. Consequently $S_3=\{3\}$. Since $a_3=1$, the coordinate $3$
-cannot occur sub-fully in any other $S_\ell$, so it is isolated and the
-extremal generator is disconnected.
-
-Conversely, suppose that $n$ is nonsquarefree and is not of the preceding
-form. Choose a coordinate $h$ with $a_h\ge2$. If possible take $h\ne2$. For
-each $\ell\ne h$, choose a rank-jump factor of rank
-\[
- d_\ell=\ell^{a_\ell}h,
-\]
-and choose an exact-rank prime of rank $h^{a_h}$ for the $h$-rank-jump factor. The ranks
-$d_\ell$ are nonexceptional except possibly when $h=3$ and $\ell=2$; use
-$4$ when $d_2=6$ and $16$ when $d_2=12$. These exceptional rank-jump factors have
-$E_n=T_n=\{2\}$ because the $3$-coordinate is sub-full. If the only possible
-hub is $h=2$, then either $3\nmid n$ or $a_2\ge3$. In the latter case, use
-$9\in\Atom(12)$ for the $3$-rank-jump factor; relative to $n$ it has
-$E_n(9)=T_n(9)=\{3\}$. Use exact-rank primes of rank
-$\ell^{a_\ell}2$ for the remaining nonhub coordinates. In every case we have
-chosen one rank-jump factor from each $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$, so the extremal-slice
-bijection makes their product a minimal generator. Its rank-support edges are
-$\{h\}$ and the pairs $\{h,\ell\}$, hence it is connected. Together with
-\eqref{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}, this proves
-\eqref{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound-sharp}
-For $n\ge3$, there exists $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with
-$\omega(m)=\omega(n)$ if and only if $n$ is not even and squarefree. In
-particular, equality occurs on every odd layer.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-This is the endpoint assertion in \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
-\end{proof}

+\section{Secondary counting bounds}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Coarse and mean bounds]\label{cor:secondary-bounds}
+For $n\geq3$, put $k=\omega(n)$ and $L(n)=\log\#\mathcal M_n$. Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}
+ \#\mathcal M_n
+ \leq\sum_{r=0}^k\binom{\Omega(F_n)}r
+ \leq n^k,
+\end{equation}
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:crude-maximal-order}
+ \limsup_{n\to\infty}
+ \frac{L(n)\log\log n}{(\log n)^2}\leq1,
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sperner-wigert-envelope}
+ L(n)\leq\log\tau(F_n)
+ \leq(\log2\,\log\varphi+o(1))\frac n{\log n},
+ \qquad \varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, as $x\to\infty$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}
+ \left(\frac{\log2}{4}+o(1)\right)x(\log\log x)^2
+ \leq\sum_{3\leq n\leq x}L(n)
+ \leq(1+o(1))x\log x\,\log\log x.
+\end{equation}
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Unique factorization injects $\mathcal M_n$ into the subsets of the
+$\Omega(F_n)$ prime powers dividing $F_n$. Theorem~
+\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} bounds the subset size by $k$,
+giving the first inequality in \eqref{eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}.
+Since $2^{\Omega(F_n)}\leq F_n<2^{n-1}$, we have
+$\Omega(F_n)\leq n-2$, and
+$\sum_{r=0}^k\binom Nr\leq(N+1)^k$ gives the second.
+
+The classical maximal order of $\omega(n)$
+\cite[Theorem~22.11]{HardyWright2008Introduction} applied to
+$L(n)\leq\omega(n)\log n$ proves
+\eqref{eq:crude-maximal-order}. Since $\mathcal M_n$ is an antichain in the
+divisor lattice of $F_n$, Wigert's theorem \cite{Wigert1907Divisors} gives
+\[
+ L(n)\leq\log\tau(F_n)
+ \leq(\log2+o(1))\frac{\log F_n}{\log\log F_n}.
+\]
+Binet's formula yields \eqref{eq:sperner-wigert-envelope}.
+
+For the mean upper bound, use
+\cite{HardyRamanujan1917NormalPrimeFactors} in the form
+\[
+ \sum_{n\leq x}\omega(n)=x\log\log x+O(x)
+\]
+and $L(n)\leq\omega(n)\log n$. For the lower bound, Tur\'an's second-moment
+form of the Hardy--Ramanujan theorem \cite{Turan1934HardyRamanujan} gives
+\[
+ \sum_{n\leq x}\omega(n)^2=(1+o(1))x(\log\log x)^2.
+\]
+The lower half of \eqref{article-eq:private-cover-entropy-order}, after
+enlarging its absolute constant for $\omega(n)<3$, completes the proof.
+\end{proof}
+
+For a labelled $k$-set $V$, let $C_k$ be the number of irredundant covers of
+$V$ by nonempty subsets.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data bound]
+\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
+Assign a real weight $w_S\geq1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$, and put
+\[
+ Z_V(w)=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
+              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
+ \qquad A=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
+ Z_V(w)\geq C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\end{equation}
+This is best possible for every $A\geq2^k-1$: equality is attained by
+\[
+ w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
+\]
+If $k\geq3$, this is the only equality profile.
+
+Consequently, if $n\geq3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
+ \geq C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
+ \mathcal W(n)\geq
+ 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
+\end{equation}
+Among positive weight profiles with the same total
+$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact. The
+extremizing profile is not asserted to occur among Fibonacci exact-rank
+multiplicities.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\geq0$. For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
+\[
+ \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
+ \geq1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
+\]
+Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ for
+$S=V$, and otherwise use
+$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$. Summation proves
+\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}. The only minimal cover containing
+$V$ is $\{V\}$, so the displayed profile attains equality.
+
+If $k\geq3$, every proper nonempty $S$ occurs in at least two minimal covers.
+For $|S|=1$, use the singleton partition and $\{S,V\setminus S\}$; for
+$|S|\geq2$, choose $s\in S$, $t\notin S$, and also use the cover consisting
+of $S$, $\{s,t\}$, and the remaining singletons. Equality therefore forces
+$x_S=0$ for every proper $S$.
+
+For odd squarefree $n$, nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond to
+divisors $d>1$ of $n$, and exact ranks partition the prime divisors of $F_n$:
+\[
+ \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)=\omega(F_n).
+\]
+Apply \eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, Theorem~
+\ref{article-cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}, and
+\eqref{article-eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Multiplicity-free support entropy with arithmetic remainder]
-\label{thm:minimal-generator-growth}
-For every integer $n\ge3$, put $k=\omega(n)$ and
-$L(n)=\log\#\mathcal M_n$. Then $\mathcal M_n$ is nonempty. If $k\ge3$ and
-$r=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}
- (2^r-1)^{k-r}
- \le \#\mathcal M_n
- \le \sum_{s=1}^{k}\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}.
-\end{equation}
-In particular, uniformly along every sequence for which $\omega(n)\to\infty$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}
- \frac{\log2}{4}\,\omega(n)^2-O(1)
- \le L(n)
- \le \frac{\log2}{4}\,\omega(n)^2
-      +\omega(n)\log R(n)+O(\omega(n)).
-\end{equation}
-No exact quadratic coefficient for the full quantity $L(n)$ is claimed.
-The coefficient $\log2/4$ is exact only for the multiplicity-free
-minimal-cover contribution: the lower construction embeds the unweighted
-cover count, and the private-coordinate encoding gives the same quadratic
-support term in the upper bound. The display is not an asymptotic formula for
-$L(n)$ unless $R(n)=\exp(o(\omega(n)))$; no such unconditional estimate for
-$R(n)$ is proved here. In particular, the displayed coefficient is not
-claimed to be optimal among all deductions from fibotomic or exact-rank
-arithmetic information.
-
-For comparison, the crude support-count estimate gives
-\begin{equation}
-\label{eq:finite-minimal-generator-bound}
- \#\mathcal M_n
- \le \sum_{r=0}^{k}\binom{\Omega(F_n)}{r}
- \le n^k.
-\end{equation}
-Combining only the last inequality with the classical maximal order of
-$\omega(n)$ gives the crude corollary
-\begin{equation}
-\label{eq:crude-maximal-order}
- \limsup_{n\to\infty}
- \frac{L(n)\log\log n}{(\log n)^2}\le1.
-\end{equation}
-This envelope has scale $(\log n)^2/\log\log n$, a factor $\log\log n$
-above the witness-cover entropy scale; it is not a consequence of
-\eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}.
-At the coarser divisor-lattice scale, the antichain property and Wigert's
-theorem give the Sperner-type envelope
-\begin{equation}
-\label{eq:sperner-wigert-envelope}
- L(n)\le\log\tau(F_n)
- \le (\log2\,\log\varphi+o(1))\frac{n}{\log n},
- \qquad \varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2};
-\end{equation}
-in fact \eqref{eq:crude-maximal-order} is stronger and implies
-$L(n)=o(n/\log n)$.
-
-Moreover, as $x\to\infty$,
-\begin{equation}
-\label{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}
- \left(\frac{\log2}{4}+o(1)\right)x(\log\log x)^2
- \le \sum_{3\le n\le x}L(n)
- \le (1+o(1))x\log x\,\log\log x.
-\end{equation}

-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-First, $F_n\in B_n$ for every $n\ge3$.  Indeed,
-$F_n\mid F_d$ implies $F_n\le F_d$, and strict increase of the Fibonacci
-sequence from index $2$ onward forces $d\ge n$; hence $\alpha(F_n)=n$.
-Because $B_n$ is a nonempty finite poset, it has a minimal element, so
-$\mathcal M_n\ne\varnothing$ and $L(n)$ is defined.
-
-We first prove the explicit finite private-cover bound in
-\eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}. Fix $k\ge3$, and give
-$\mathcal P(n)$ an arbitrary order. Put
-\[
- X=\mathcal P(n)\cap\{2,3\},\qquad r=\lfloor k/2\rfloor.
-\]
-Since $k-\#X\ge k-2\ge r$, choose an $r$-element set
-$P\subseteq\mathcal P(n)\setminus X$, and put
-$Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. For every map
-\[
- H:Q\longrightarrow 2^P\setminus\{\varnothing\}
-\]
-and every $i\in P$, define
-\[
- T_i=\{i\}\cup\{q\in Q:i\in H(q)\}.
-\]
-The index $n_{T_i}=\prod_{\ell\in T_i}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n)}$ has a prime
-divisor outside $\{2,3\}$, because $i\in P$. Hence $n_{T_i}\ge5$ and
-$n_{T_i}\notin\{6,12\}$. Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-divisors} supplies a
-prime $\pi_{T_i}$ with $\alpha(\pi_{T_i})=n_{T_i}$; fix one such prime for
-each support that occurs.
-
-The supports $T_i$ cover $\mathcal P(n)$ because $H(q)$ is nonempty for every
-$q\in Q$. Moreover, $i$ belongs to $T_i$ and to no $T_j$ with $j\ne i$.
-Each $\pi_{T_i}$ is a prime jump, so
-$E_n(\pi_{T_i})=T_n(\pi_{T_i})=T_i$. Thus
-$\{\pi_{T_i}:i\in P\}$ is an $n$-witness cover. Distinct supports have
-distinct ranks and therefore distinct underlying primes. If two maps $H$
-differ, then their support families differ, since the edge containing the
-private coordinate $i$ identifies $T_i$; unique factorization then gives
-different minimal generators. There are
-$(2^r-1)^{\#Q}=(2^r-1)^{k-r}$ maps $H$, proving the lower bound in
-\eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}.
-
-For the upper bound, let $\Theta$ be an $n$-witness cover with $s$ rank-jump factors. For
-each $\theta\in\Theta$, choose the least coordinate
-\[
- x_\theta\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
- \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta\setminus\{\theta\}}T_n(\eta).
-\]
-These private coordinates are distinct; write
-$P=\{x_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ and
-$Q=\mathcal P(n)\setminus P$. If $x_\theta=x$, then
-\[
- T_n(\theta)=\{x\}\cup U_\theta,\qquad U_\theta\subseteq Q,
-\]
-because every other member of $P$ is private to another rank-jump factor. By the
-prime--ladder alternative in Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, either
-$E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta)$ or $E_n(\theta)=\{x\}$. Hence there are at most two
-support-pair alternatives, and the definition
-\eqref{eq:rank-window-multiplicity} allows at most $R(n)$ rank-jump factors for each.
-Thus, once $P$ is fixed, the rank-jump factor indexed by each
-$x\in P$ has at most $2R(n)2^{k-s}$ choices. Ignoring coverage and
-coprimeness only enlarges the count, so summing over the
-$\binom{k}{s}$ possible sets $P$ and over $1\le s\le k$ proves the upper
-bound in \eqref{eq:private-cover-finite-bounds}.
-
-Now $r(k-r)=\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor$ and
-$(k-r)\log(1-2^{-r})=O(1)$. Hence the logarithm of the lower bound is
-$(\log2)k^2/4+O(1)$. For the upper bound, use
-$s(k-s)\le k^2/4$, $s\le k$, and
-$\sum_s\binom{k}{s}\le2^k$ to obtain
-\[
- \log\sum_{s=1}^{k}\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}
- \le\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+k\log R(n)+O(k).
-\]
-This proves \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}.
-
-Let
-\[
- \mathcal Q_n=\{p^e:p\mid F_n,\ 1\le e\le\nu_p(F_n)\}.
-\]
-This set has cardinality $\Omega(F_n)$.  By unique factorization, the map
-\[
- m\longmapsto\{p^{\nu_p(m)}:p\mid m\}
-\]
-is injective from $\mathcal M_n$ into the subsets of $\mathcal Q_n$.
-Corollary~\ref{cor:support-bound} says that every image has at most

-
-Since every prime factor of $F_n$ is at least $2$,

-\[
- \sum_{r=0}^k\binom Nr\le(N+1)^k.
-\]
-Taking $N=\Omega(F_n)$ gives the second inequality in

-now combines with $L(n)\le\omega(n)\log n$ to prove
-\eqref{eq:crude-maximal-order}. This argument uses only the crude estimate
-$\#\mathcal M_n\le n^{\omega(n)}$, not the witness-cover entropy bound. On
-the other hand,
-$\mathcal M_n$ is an antichain in the divisor lattice of $F_n$, so
-\[
- \#\mathcal M_n\le\widthop(\operatorname{Div}(F_n))\le\tau(F_n).
-\]
-Wigert's maximal-order theorem \cite{Wigert1907Divisors} states that
-\[
- \log\tau(N)\le(\log2+o(1))\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}.
-\]
-Binet's formula gives $\log F_n=n\log\varphi+O(1)$ and
-$\log\log F_n=\log n+O(1)$, yielding
-\eqref{eq:sperner-wigert-envelope}.  Finally,
-$(\log n)^2/\log\log n=o(n/\log n)$, so

-For the mean upper bound, use the classical mean-value estimate

-\begin{equation}

- \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)=x\log\log x+O(x),
-\end{equation}
-together with $L(n)\le\omega(n)\log n$.  Uniformly for $n\le x$,

-\[
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}L(n)
- \le\log x\sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)

-\]
-
-Tur\'an's second-moment form of the Hardy--Ramanujan theorem

-\end{equation}
-After enlarging the absolute constant in the lower half of

-Summation and \eqref{eq:omega-second-moment} prove the lower half of

-\begin{definition}[Sufficient maximum-window hypothesis H1]
-\label{hyp:normal-window}
-For every $\varepsilon>0$,
-\[
- \#\{n\le x:\log R(n)>\varepsilon\omega(n)\}=o(x).
-\tag{H1}
-\]
-\end{definition}

-\begin{definition}[Sufficient maximum-window hypothesis H2]
-\label{hyp:mean-window}
-One has
-\[
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log R(n)
- =o\bigl(x(\log\log x)^2\bigr).
-\tag{H2}

-\begin{proposition}[Conditional obstruction from Fibonacci prime divisors]
-\label{prop:blms-obstructs-mean-window}
-Assume Conjecture~5.1 of Bugeaud--Luca--Mignotte--Siksek
-\cite{BugeaudLucaMignotteSiksek2005FewPrimeDivisors}, namely that
-$\omega(F_n)\gg\log n$ for composite $n$. Then, for every fixed
-$\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<1-\log2$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:blms-normal-window-obstruction}
- \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac1x
- \#\{n\le x:\log R(n)>\varepsilon\omega(n)\}
- \ge\frac6{\pi^2},
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:blms-mean-window-obstruction}
- \liminf_{x\to\infty}
- \frac{\sum_{3\le n\le x}\omega(n)\log R(n)}
- {x(\log\log x)^2}
- \ge\frac6{\pi^2}(1-\log2)>0.
-\end{equation}
-In particular, under that published conjecture, both sufficient
-maximum-window hypotheses \textup{(H1)} and \textup{(H2)} are false.
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $n$ be squarefree and put $k=\omega(n)$. The exact-rank partition of the
-prime divisors of $F_n$ gives
-\[
- \omega(F_n)=\sum_{d\mid n}a(d).
-\]
-For squarefree $n$, every nonempty support $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ has the
-single rank $d=\prod_{\ell\in J}\ell$ in its window. Since $a(1)=0$, the
-pigeonhole principle and \eqref{eq:prime-window-versus-R} give
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-blms-pigeonhole}
- R(n)\ge\max_{d\mid n}a(d)
- \ge\frac{\omega(F_n)}{2^k-1}.
-\end{equation}
-Under the stated conjecture, for every sufficiently large squarefree composite
-$n$,
-\[
- \log R(n)\ge\log\log n-k\log2+O(1).
-\]
-The Hardy--Ramanujan theorem has an exceptional set of $o(x)$ integers, so on
-all but $o(x)$ squarefree integers one has
-$k=(1+o(1))\log\log n$. Consequently
-\[
- \omega(n)\log R(n)
- \ge(1-\log2+o(1))(\log\log n)^2
-\]
-on this set. Squarefree integers have density $6/\pi^2$, and squarefree prime
-indices have density zero. Moreover,
-\[
- \frac{\log R(n)}{\omega(n)}\ge1-\log2+o(1)
-\]
-on the same set. This proves
-\eqref{eq:blms-normal-window-obstruction}; summation over squarefree composite
-indices proves \eqref{eq:blms-mean-window-obstruction}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Purely conditional consequences of H1 and H2]
-\label{cor:conditional-orders}
-Assuming hypothesis \textup{(H1)} in Definition~\ref{hyp:normal-window},
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:conditional-normal-order}
- L(n)\sim\frac{\log2}{4}(\log\log n)^2
- \quad\text{for almost all }n.
-\end{equation}
-Assuming hypothesis \textup{(H2)} in Definition~\ref{hyp:mean-window},
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:conditional-mean-order}
- \sum_{3\le n\le x}L(n)
- \sim\frac{\log2}{4}x(\log\log x)^2.
-\end{equation}
-These are implications only: neither conclusion is unconditional, and no
-positive arithmetic evidence for either sufficient hypothesis is presently
-known. Proposition~\ref{prop:blms-obstructs-mean-window} shows that the
-published Bugeaud--Luca--Mignotte--Siksek conjecture predicts that both
-hypotheses fail.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For the first assertion, intersect the density-one set in
-Definition~\ref{hyp:normal-window} with the Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order set.
-Then the error $\omega(n)\log R(n)+O(\omega(n))$ in
-\eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order} is $o(\omega(n)^2)$. For the second,
-sum the upper bound in \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order}, use
-Definition~\ref{hyp:mean-window}, \eqref{eq:omega-second-moment}, and
-$\sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)=O(x\log\log x)$, and compare with the unconditional
-lower mean bound \eqref{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Exact residual arithmetic interface]
-\label{rem:exact-average-open-interface}
-Supplementary Corollary~\ref{supp-cor:theta-refined-connected-entropy} and
-Theorem~\ref{thm:minimal-generator-growth} determine the contribution of the
-multiplicity-free minimal-cover model used here: $\log2/4$ is its exact
-quadratic coefficient, the fixed-choice rank-pure sector supplies its
-theta-refined lower terms, and the private-coordinate upper bound retains the
-term $\omega(n)\log R(n)$. Proposition~
-\ref{prop:rank-jump-family-ladder-slots} gives the rank-window description for
-every support size:
-prime jump families are finite disjoint unions of the rank
-classes $\Pi_\alpha(d)$, while ladder families are singletons. Thus
-Hypotheses \textup{(H1)} and \textup{(H2)} in Definitions~
-\ref{hyp:normal-window} and \ref{hyp:mean-window} ask precisely for sufficient
-upper distributional control of
-exact-rank prime multiplicities in those rank windows.
-
-The pointwise estimate \eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} proves only the
-consequence obtained by combining the fibotomic size identity with the
-divisibility of the exact-rank radical and the congruences
-$p\equiv\pm1\pmod d$. Supplementary Remark~
-\ref{supp-rem:cumulative-rank-estimates-insufficient} shows that even its
-Euler-factor scale does not by itself imply either maximum-window hypothesis. The
-manuscript does not prove that these inputs exhaust the information available
-from fibotomic arithmetic, or that
-\eqref{eq:fibotomic-rank-entropy} is optimal within any information class. Such
-an optimality theorem would require, at minimum, a precise axiom class of
-admissible information and a realizable extremal model satisfying those
-axioms. Neither is supplied here. Whether stronger unconditional dispersion or
-concentration consequences follow from fibotomic arithmetic is therefore an
-open interface.
-
-The closest distribution theorems do not close this interface.  In the
-notation of a nondegenerate Lucas sequence $U$ with nonsquare discriminant
-$\Delta$ and squarefree discriminant part $\Delta_0$, Sanna's Theorem~1.1
-\cite{Sanna2022RankDivisibility} gives, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula
-for
-\[
- \#\{p\le x:d\mid\rho_U(p)\}
-\]
-when $d$ is odd, with $3\nmid d$ if $\Delta_0=-3$, and
-$x>\exp(Be^{8\omega(d)}d^8)$.  The condition counted is
-$d\mid\rho_U(p)$, not the exact-rank condition $\rho_U(p)=d$; for example,
-$3\mid\alpha(17)=9$ although $\alpha(17)\ne3$.  Sanna's Theorem~1.1 on the
-index of appearance \cite{Sanna2024IndexAppearance} instead assumes GRH and,
-for a fixed positive integer $t$, counts primes having
-$\iota_U(p)=t$ uniformly for $x>t^3$. Cera Da Concei\c c\~ao removes the
-restrictions in the fixed rank-divisibility density problem and gives
-explicit densities for all Lucas sequences and fixed $d$
-\cite{CeraDaConceicao2026PrimeDensities}; the condition remains
-$d\mid\rho_U(p)$ and still does not isolate a growing exact fiber. In the
-Fibonacci case,
-$\alpha(p)=d$ and $\iota_F(p)=t$ imply
-\[
- p=td+\left(\frac5p\right)=td\pm1.
-\]
-Taking $x$ on the scale of this candidate prime restricts that theorem to
-$t^2\ll d$, and its cumulative fixed-index count still does not isolate the
-single rank $d$. Thus none of these results controls the growing exact fibers
-$\Pi_\alpha(d)$ required in \eqref{eq:visible-single-rank-interface}.
-
-The primitive-divisor theorems of Carmichael and Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier give
-existence in the Fibonacci setting. Granville proves an odd-multiplicity
-primitive-factor theorem for a class of second-order Lucas recurrences with
-$c\equiv2\pmod4$ and explicitly leaves the odd-$b,c$ case, including the
-Fibonacci recurrence $b=c=1$, outside that theorem
-\cite{Granville2012PrimitivePrimeFactors}. Thus it is a neighboring
-Lucas-sequence result, not a Fibonacci multiplicity input here. Kiss treats
-related Lucas-sequence primitive-divisor questions
-\cite{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}. Hong proves that, for each fixed positive
-integer $\kappa$ and all sufficiently large $n$ with an explicit threshold,
-$F_n$ has a primitive divisor at least $(\kappa+1)n-1$
-\cite{Hong2025BigPrimitiveDivisors}. These results concern existence, parity of
-one primitive factor's multiplicity in the stated Lucas class, or the size of
-one Fibonacci primitive divisor; they do not provide the required average
-dispersion or critical concentration estimates for Fibonacci exact-rank prime
-multiplicities in visible divisor windows. The
-Hardy--Ramanujan and
-Tur\'an theorems control the additive function $\omega(n)$ but not the prime
-factorization of $F_d$ across exact apparition ranks. Likewise, the
-Erd\H{o}s--Wintner theorem \cite{ErdosWintner1939Additive} concerns limiting
-distributions of additive arithmetic functions, whereas $L(n)$ and $R(n)$
-are not additive. No implication from RH or ERH to either rank-window
-conjecture is presently known. Accordingly, the normal and mean equivalents
-\eqref{eq:conditional-normal-order} and
-\eqref{eq:conditional-mean-order} are conditional; the unconditional
-statements are \eqref{eq:private-cover-entropy-order} and
-\eqref{eq:mean-logarithmic-growth}, together with the stronger connected lower
-bound in Supplementary Corollary~
-\ref{supp-cor:theta-refined-connected-entropy}.
-None of these estimates implies that the disconnected part of $\mathcal M_n$
-is negligible; the strictly stronger blockwise hypothesis needed for that
-conclusion is isolated in Supplementary Theorem~
-\ref{supp-thm:blockwise-connected-dominance}.
-\end{remark}

-\begin{proposition}[Exact support-three realization at $n=30$]

-\subsection*{Substructures of nonexceptional rank level sets}
-
-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:canonical-principal-interval}
-Let $n\ge3$, $n\notin\{6,12\}$, and choose an exact-rank prime $\pi_n$ with
-$\alpha(\pi_n)=n$. Then the principal interval
-\[
-[\pi_n,F_n]_{D_n}:=\{q\in D_n:\ \pi_n\mid q\}
-\]
-is contained in $B_n$. In particular $B_n$ contains a divisor-lattice
-interval naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Div}(F_n/\pi_n)$. This
-interval is natural after choosing $\pi_n$; no choice-free canonical interval
-is asserted.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By Theorem~\ref{article-thm:primitive-divisors}, there is a prime
-$\pi_n$ with $\alpha(\pi_n)=n$. Thus $\pi_n\in B_n$. Since
-Lemma~\ref{article-thm:upper-fiber} says that $B_n$ is an upper set in $D_n$,
-every divisor $q$ of $F_n$ with $\pi_n\mid q$ also lies in $B_n$. Division by
-$\pi_n$ gives an order-preserving bijection from this interval to
-$\operatorname{Div}(F_n/\pi_n)$, with inverse $d\mapsto \pi_n d$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:boolean-skeleton}
-Let $n\ge3$, $n\notin\{6,12\}$, and put
-\[
-\mathcal D_n^*:=\{d:\ d\mid n,\ 3\le d<n,\ d\notin\{6,12\}\}.
-\]
-For each $d\in\mathcal D_n^*$ choose an exact-rank prime
-$\pi_d$ with $\alpha(\pi_d)=d$, and choose an exact-rank prime
-$\pi_n$ with $\alpha(\pi_n)=n$. Then
-\[
-S\longmapsto \pi_n\prod_{d\in S}\pi_d
-\qquad(S\subseteq\mathcal D_n^*)
-\]
-embeds the Boolean lattice $2^{\mathcal D_n^*}$ into $B_n$. Hence
-$B_n$ contains a Boolean subposet of rank
-\[
-|\mathcal D_n^*|\ge \tau(n)-5.
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The exact-rank primes exist by Theorem~\ref{article-thm:primitive-divisors}. They
-are distinct, because distinct ranks of apparition cannot belong to the
-same prime. For every $d\mid n$, $\pi_d\mid F_d\mid F_n$, so the displayed
-products divide $F_n$. They all also divide a multiple of $\pi_n$ inside
-$D_n$, and Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-principal-interval} puts every such
-multiple in $B_n$.
-
-Since the primes $\pi_d$ are distinct, divisibility among the displayed
-products is exactly inclusion among the subsets $S$. Thus the map is a
-Boolean-lattice embedding. Among the $\tau(n)$ divisors of $n$, the only
-divisors excluded from $\mathcal D_n^*$ are contained in
-$\{1,2,6,12,n\}$, so $|\mathcal D_n^*|\ge\tau(n)-5$.
-\end{proof}

-\label{sec:supp-witness-consequences}

-\begin{corollary}[Finite Fibonacci support grammar]
-\label{cor:finite-witness-cover-types}
-Fix $k\ge1$. Up to relabeling of the $k$ prime coordinates of $n$, only
-finitely many witness-cover support types can occur for minimal generators
-$m\in\mathcal M_n$ with $\omega(n)=k$. Put
-\[
-\mathcal P_k:=\{(I,J):\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq[k],\
- I=J\text{ or }|I|=1\},
-\qquad
-N'_k:=\#\mathcal P_k=(2^k-1)+k(2^{k-1}-1).
-\]
-Every minimal generator determines a unique labelled support set
-\[
-\mathsf T(m):=\{(E_n(\theta),T_n(\theta)):\theta\in\Theta(m)\}
- \subseteq\mathcal P_k,
-\]
-with $1\le|\mathsf T(m)|\le k$, satisfying coverage and irredundance:
-\[
-\bigcup_{(I,J)\in\mathsf T(m)}J=[k],\qquad
-I\nsubseteq\bigcup_{(I',J')\in\mathsf T(m)\setminus\{(I,J)\}}J'.
-\]
-Consequently the number of possible labelled support types is at most
-\[
-\sum_{r=1}^k\binom{N'_k}{r}.
-\]
-The converse is not asserted: arithmetic realization additionally requires
-nonempty rank-jump factor families and representatives with distinct underlying primes.
-Unlabelled types are $S_k$-orbits of the labelled support sets. For $k=3$, the
-realization layer is the support-three slot test of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness} and
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification}, every $m\in\mathcal M_n$ is the
-product attached to a unique witness cover $\Theta(m)$, and
-Corollary~\ref{article-cor:support-bound} gives $\#\Theta(m)\le k$. Irredundance makes
-each $E_n(\theta)$ nonempty. After labeling $\mathcal P(n)$ by $[k]$, the
-prime--ladder alternative in Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy} shows
-that each rank-jump factor contributes a pair in $\mathcal P_k$: a prime jump has $I=J$,
-whereas a ladder jump with nonempty essential support has $|I|=1$.
-
-Two distinct rank-jump factors cannot contribute the same pair $(I,J)$, since then the
-essential support of either would be contained in the full support of the
-other. Hence $\mathsf T(m)$ is a genuine set and is uniquely determined by
-the labelled prime-power factorization. There are $2^k-1$ diagonal pairs and,
-for each singleton $I=\{i\}$, there are $2^{k-1}-1$ proper supersets
-$J\supsetneq I$, proving the formula for $N'_k$. Coverage and irredundance are
-exactly the two displayed conditions. Counting nonempty subsets of
-$\mathcal P_k$ of size at most $k$ proves the bound. Passing to unlabelled
-types amounts to taking $S_k$-orbits. The rank-jump factor-family nonemptiness and
-coprimeness requirements explain why the converse need not hold.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Best possible support budget]
-\label{cor:support-budget-best-possible}
-Let $g:\NN\to\NN$ be any function such that
-\[
-\omega(m)\le g(\omega(n))
-\]
-for every $n\ge2$ and every $m\in\mathcal M_n$. Then $g(k)\ge k$ for every
-$k\ge1$. Equivalently, Corollary~\ref{article-cor:support-bound} is sharp as a
-uniform bound depending only on the number of prime coordinates of $n$.
-Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-support-spectra} gives the exact layer-by-layer
-equality criterion and the complete support spectrum.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Fix $k\ge1$ and choose any product $n$ of $k$ distinct odd primes; for
-example, take the product of the first $k$ odd primes. Then $n$ is odd,
-$n\ge3$, and $\omega(n)=k$. Corollary~\ref{cor:support-bound-sharp} gives an
-element $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with $\omega(m)=\omega(n)=k$. Applying the assumed
-uniform inequality to this pair gives $k=\omega(m)\le g(k)$. Since $k$ was
-arbitrary, no uniform support budget smaller than $\omega(n)$ can hold.
-\end{proof}

-\section{Finite verification for the three-coordinate table}
-\label{app:three-coordinate-checklist}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Reader's checklist for the three-coordinate table]
-\label{prop:three-coordinate-table-checklist}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,
-\ell_2,\ell_3\}$.  The following finite procedure returns exactly
-$\mathcal M_n$.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item For every nonempty $J\subseteq[3]$, compute the exact-rank window
-$\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ and the rank classes
-$\Pi_\alpha(d)$ for $d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ by
-Lemma~\ref{article-lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}. This gives every prime
-slot $P_J(n)$.
-\item For each coordinate $i$, compute the single possible ladder candidate
-$\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ from
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}, then retain it in
-$L_{i,J}(n)$ exactly for those $J$ for which its rank divides $n$ and has
-full-coordinate set $J$.
-\item For each coordinate permutation of each of the eight rows in
-Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}, replace the displayed slots
-by the finite sets found in (i) and (ii), with
-$S_i(n)=P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n)$.
-\item Keep precisely those row fillings whose selected prime powers have
-distinct underlying primes, equivalently those satisfying the Hall
-inequalities in Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection}; multiply the selected
-prime powers and insert the product into a set, thereby removing repetitions
-caused by stabilizers and coordinate permutations.
-\end{enumerate}
-The products retained in (iv) are exactly the minimal generators listed in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.  In particular, the
-table is a closed finite classification for fixed $n$, not an interface to an
-additional infinite search.
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Step (i) is precisely the prime-slot identity in
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}; the M\"obius formula
-there is Lemma~\ref{article-lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}.  Step (ii) is the
-ladder-slot identity in the same proposition, which says that every
-$L_{i,J}(n)$ is empty or consists of the displayed single candidate.  Step
-(iii) is only the coordinate-labelling convention of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness}.  By that theorem, after the
-slots of a labelled row are replaced by their finite admissible sets, a row
-realizes a minimal generator if and only if the slot-selection test in step
-(iv) succeeds; Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} is exactly the stated
-Hall criterion for distinct underlying primes.  The one-factor rows
-$\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_3$ are the rank-jump generators with full
-three-coordinate support.  Conversely, every minimal generator with
-three-coordinate support has, by
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-realization}, one fixed labelled
-coordinate permutation of one of the eight row types and therefore appears in
-this procedure. The labelled rank-jump factor set is unique, whereas the
-unlabelled row is an $S_3$-orbit; the set insertion in step (iv) prevents the
-raw permuted enumeration from asserting stronger uniqueness.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{example}[Applying the checklist at $n=42$]
-\label{ex:n42-three-coordinate-checklist}
-Let $n=42=2\cdot3\cdot7$ and label the coordinates by
-$(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)=(2,3,7)$.  The prime factors of
-\[
-F_{42}=2^3\cdot13\cdot29\cdot211\cdot421
-\]
-have ranks
-\[
-\alpha(2)=3,
-\alpha(4)=6,
-\alpha(13)=7,
-\alpha(29)=14,
-\alpha(421)=21,
-\alpha(211)=42.
-\]
-Thus $\Atom(42)=\{211\}$. The exact-rank windows used below are
-$P_{12}(42)=\varnothing$, $P_{13}(42)=\{29\}$,
-$P_{23}(42)=\{421\}$, and $P_{123}(42)=\{211\}$.  Singleton slots are
-$S_1(42)=\varnothing$, $S_2(42)=\{2\}$, and $S_3(42)=\{13\}$.  The proper
-ladder slots relevant here are
-$L_{1,12}(42)=\{4\}$, $L_{1,123}(42)=\varnothing$,
-$L_{2,J}(42)=\varnothing$, and $L_{3,J}(42)=\varnothing$.
-
-The table then gives the following non-rank-jump generators.  The row
-$\Gamma_4$ with the permuted slots $P_{13}$ and $P_{23}$ gives
-$29\cdot421=12209$.  The row $\Gamma_5$ gives
-$4\cdot421=1684$ from $L_{1,12}$ and $P_{23}$, while the analogous
-coordinate permutation with an exact-rank $P_{13}$ partner is not a row of type
-$\Gamma_5$ for this ladder orientation.  The row $\Gamma_7$ gives
-$2\cdot29=58$ from $S_2$ and $P_{13}$ after relabeling.  The row $\Gamma_8$
-gives $13\cdot4=52$ from $S_3$ and the permuted ladder slot $L_{1,12}$.
-All other rows fail because one of the required slots is empty.  Hence
-\[
-\mathcal M_{42}=\{52,58,211,1684,12209\}.
-\]
-The example illustrates the theorem's reading rule: every success or failure
-is decided by a finite slot list and a coprimeness check.
-\end{example}

FILE cover_letter.txt
Editor
The Fibonacci Quarterly

Dear Editor,

We resubmit "Minimal preimages of the Fibonacci rank map: squarefree fibers
and weighted covers" to The Fibonacci Quarterly following a reject-and-resubmit
decision.

For each positive integer n, the article studies the exact fiber of the
Fibonacci rank-of-apparition map and its divisibility-minimal elements. Its
main contribution is an exact classification of those minimal elements by
irredundant witness covers, together with the canonical squarefree slice and
its exact weighted cover count. The article also settles two problems posed by
FitzGibbons, Javaheri, Miller, and Verga: whether every fixed-point-order class
of positive order contains infinitely many relatively prime integers, and
whether the basin of every fixed point x > 5 contains infinitely many
relatively prime integers. Both are answered in the stronger prime form as a
direct corollary of classical exact-rank prime existence; no new
prime-existence input is claimed.

The resubmission addresses the two structural grounds for the decision.
First, the affected upper-bound arguments are now independently checkable
within the article. It contains the numbered proposition "Classical
prime-power rank lifting," a numbered lemma establishing the prime-ladder
alternative, and the unique ladder-slot formulas needed by those arguments.
The relevant dependencies now point to numbered statements in the article. To
accommodate these proofs, the article has increased from 27 to 33 pages and
from 24 to 31 theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary environments.

Second, the priority boundary has been corrected. The article now cites Carl
G. Wagner, "Minimal multiplicative covers of an integer," Discrete Mathematics
24 (1978), 87-94, and T. Hearne and C. Wagner, "Minimal covers of finite
sets," Discrete Mathematics 5 (1973), 247-251. A numbered comparison
proposition states that the prime-atom case is the unordered form of Wagner's
condition and identifies the additional structure as the lowering of a
prime-power rank label rather than deletion of that label. The classical
minimal-cover skeleton is not claimed as new.

The former H1 and H2 conjectural language has also been corrected. H1 and H2
are now called sufficient maximum-window hypotheses. Corollary 6.9 is stated
purely conditionally, records that no positive arithmetic evidence for either
hypothesis is presently known, and states that the published
Bugeaud-Luca-Mignotte-Siksek conjecture predicts that both hypotheses fail.

The submission package includes the 33-page article, the 36-page supplement,
and the verification scripts, tests, archived outputs, literature audit,
checksums, and reproduction instructions listed in the accompanying metadata.
We ask that the supplement and computational materials be made available to
the referee.

Sincerely,

Haobo Ma

Singapore 018981, Singapore
auric@aelf.io

## Claims And Priority Boundary

The claimed new contribution is the lowered-label Fibonacci realization of
the witness-cover structure, its unique correspondence with the
divisibility-minimal exact fiber, the canonical squarefree slice, and its
exact arithmetic weights. The article also gives prime inverse rays and uses
them to answer the two FitzGibbons-Javaheri-Miller-Verga problems in the
stronger prime form.

The classical minimal-cover skeleton is imported: Wagner's minimal
multiplicative covers give the prime-atom case, and Hearne-Wagner minimal set
covers give its set-theoretic predecessor. Classical exact-rank prime
existence supplies every prime used in the inverse-ray application, so no new
prime-existence theorem is claimed. The fixed-point classification and orbit
termination used there are also imported, from Marques and Luca-Tron,
respectively. The article records other classical rank, lifting, primitive
divisor, and fibotomic inputs at their points of use.

## Resubmission Record

The article now contains numbered statements for classical prime-power rank
lifting, the prime-ladder alternative, and the ladder-slot formulas used by
the upper bounds. It also contains a numbered proposition delimiting Wagner's
classical condition from the lowered-label generalization. H1 and H2 are
identified only as sufficient maximum-window hypotheses; Corollary 6.9 is
purely conditional, no positive arithmetic evidence for either hypothesis is
claimed, and the Bugeaud-Luca-Mignotte-Siksek conjecture is recorded as
predicting that both fail.

-\section{Secondary arithmetic bounds}
-\label{sec:supp-arithmetic-bounds}

-\begin{lemma}[Known baseline for the arithmetic interface]
-\label{lem:R-baseline}
-For every $n\ge3$,
-\[
- R(n)\le 1+\omega(F_n)=O(n),
- \qquad
- \log R(n)\le\log n+O(1).
-\]
-Moreover, the cumulative primitive-prime estimates of Kiss and Stroi\'nski
-give
-\[
- \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{\log x}{x^2}
- \#\{p:\alpha(p)\le x\}
- \le \frac{3\log\varphi}{2\pi^2}.
-\]
-Neither estimate implies the conjectures below.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Every prime jump in a family $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ divides $F_n$, and a fixed
-ladder family contains at most one rank-jump factor. Thus a family contains at most all
-distinct prime divisors of $F_n$ together with one ladder jump, proving
-$R(n)\le1+\omega(F_n)$. Since
-$2^{\omega(F_n)}\le\operatorname{rad}(F_n)\le F_n$ and
-$\log F_n=n\log\varphi+O(1)$, this gives $R(n)=O(n)$ and the logarithmic
-bound. Kiss obtained the same cumulative scale from the logarithmic mass of
-primitive parts \cite{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}; the displayed explicit
-limsup is Stroi\'nski's Theorem~7
-\cite{Stroinski2016AlphaContraction}.
-
-Quantitatively, the normal-order conjecture below asks for
-$\log R(n)=o(\log\log n)$ for almost all $n$, whereas the elementary estimate
-gives only $O(\log n)$. The cumulative estimate controls all primes of rank at
-most $x$ together and likewise gives at best a logarithmic bound of order
-$\log n$ for a single window. For the mean conjecture, the elementary bound
-and the mean order of $\omega$ give only
-$O(x\log x\log\log x)$, not $o(x(\log\log x)^2)$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{remark}[Cumulative rank estimates do not imply \textup{(H2)}]
-\label{rem:cumulative-rank-estimates-insufficient}
-This nonimplication can be made quantitative without asserting that the model
-below is realized by Fibonacci ranks. Fix $0<c<\log\varphi/2$ and put
-\[
- a_0(d):=\max\left\{1,
- \left\lfloor\frac{c\phi_{\rm E}(d)}{\log(2d)}\right\rfloor\right\}.
-\]
-Elementary integral comparison gives
-\[
- \sum_{d\le y}a_0(d)\ll\frac{y^2}{\log y},\qquad
- a_0(d)\ll1+\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(d)}{\log(2d)},\qquad
- \sum_{d\le y}a_0(d)\log d\ll y^2.
-\]
-Thus this formal multiplicity sequence has the cumulative, pointwise, and
-logarithmic-mass scales supplied by the presently known estimates, including
-Theorem~\ref{article-thm:fibotomic-rank-entropy}. It is not asserted to arise from
-Fibonacci exact-rank primes, and therefore it neither proves sharpness of the
-fibotomic inequality nor supplies a realizable extremal model for it. On the
-other hand, the standard
-lower bound for Euler's function gives
-\[
- \log a_0(n)=\log n-\log\log n+O(\log\log\log(3n))
-\]
-for large $n$.
-Partial summation in \eqref{article-eq:mean-omega-input} therefore gives
-\[
- \sum_{n\le x}\omega(n)\log a_0(n)
- \sim x\log x\log\log x,
-\]
-which is larger than the scale in \textup{(H2)}. Hence cumulative exact-rank
-counts alone cannot establish the required visible-divisor maximum estimate.
-\end{remark}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Unconditional lower growth]
-\label{cor:unconditional-lower-growth}
-For almost all $n$,
-\[
- \log\#\mathcal M_n\ge
- \left(\frac{\log2}{4}+o(1)\right)(\log\log n)^2.
-\]
-If $N_y:=\prod_{p\le y}p$, then
-\[
- \log\#\mathcal M_{N_y}\ge
- \left(\frac{\log2}{4}+o(1)\right)
- \frac{(\log N_y)^2}{(\log\log N_y)^2}.
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order theorem states that
-$\omega(n)=(1+o(1))\log\log n$ for almost all $n$
-\cite{HardyRamanujan1917NormalPrimeFactors,%
-Tenenbaum2015AnalyticProbabilistic}. Substitution in the lower half of
-\eqref{article-eq:private-cover-entropy-order} proves the first assertion. The prime
-number theorem gives
-$\omega(N_y)=\pi(y)\sim y/\log y\sim\log N_y/\log\log N_y$; substituting this
-in the same lower bound proves the second assertion.
-\end{proof}

+\section{Rank level sets and witness covers}\label{sec:upper-fibers}
 
-The notation $B_n$ below is local. As a mathematical object it is simply the
-level set $\alpha^{-1}(n)$, and passing to $\mathcal M_n$ is the generic
-operation of taking minimal elements in a finite poset.
-
-\begin{definition}\label{def:birth-layer}
-For $n\ge2$ let
-\[
-D_n:=\operatorname{Div}(F_n),\qquad
-B_n:=\{q\in D_n:\ \alpha(q)=n\},\qquad
-A(n):=\#B_n.
-\]
-The set $B_n$ is partially ordered by divisibility. Its set of minimal
-elements is
-\[
-\mathcal M_n:=\{m\in B_n:\ \text{there is no }q\in B_n
-\text{ with }q\mid m\text{ and }q<m\},
-\]
-and
-\[
-\widthop(B_n):=\max\{\#\mathcal A:\ \mathcal A\subseteq B_n
-\text{ is an antichain}\}.
-\]
-We write $\mathcal P(n)$ for the set of prime divisors of $n$. Since
-$F_2=1$, we use the boundary convention
-\[
-B_2=\mathcal M_2=\varnothing,\qquad A(2)=\widthop(B_2)=0.
-\]
-\end{definition}
