-\begin{lemma}[Upper-fiber identity]\label{thm:upper-fiber}
-For every $n\ge2$,
-\[
-B_n=D_n\setminus\bigcup_{p\mid n}D_{n/p}.
-\]
-Moreover $B_n$ is an upper set in $D_n$: if $q\in B_n$, $r\in D_n$, and
-$q\mid r$, then $r\in B_n$. Consequently
-\[
-B_n=\bigcup_{m\in\mathcal M_n}\{q\in D_n:\ m\mid q\}.
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics}, an integer $q$ lies in $D_m$ if and
-only if $\alpha(q)\mid m$. Thus $q\in D_n$ lies outside
-$\bigcup_{p\mid n}D_{n/p}$ precisely when $\alpha(q)\mid n$ but
-$\alpha(q)\nmid n/p$ for every prime $p\mid n$.
-
-If $\alpha(q)=n$, then clearly $\alpha(q)\nmid n/p$ for every $p\mid n$, so
-$q$ is outside the union. Conversely, suppose $\alpha(q)\mid n$ and
-$\alpha(q)<n$. Then $n/\alpha(q)>1$; choose a prime $p$ dividing
-$n/\alpha(q)$. Since $\alpha(q)\mid n/p$, Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics}
-gives $q\in D_{n/p}$, contrary to being outside the union. Hence the
-complement is exactly the set of $q\in D_n$ with $\alpha(q)=n$, namely
-$B_n$. For $n=2$ this also gives
-$B_2=D_2\setminus D_1=\varnothing$ under the boundary convention in
-Definition~\ref{def:birth-layer}.
-
-Now let $q\in B_n$, $r\in D_n$, and $q\mid r$. Since $r\in D_n$,
-$\alpha(r)\mid n$. Since $q\mid r$, every Fibonacci number divisible by $r$
-is divisible by $q$; applying the divisibility criterion to
-$F_{\alpha(r)}$ gives $\alpha(q)\mid\alpha(r)$. But $\alpha(q)=n$, so
-$n\mid\alpha(r)$ and $\alpha(r)\mid n$, whence $\alpha(r)=n$. Therefore
-$r\in B_n$.
-
-Finally $D_n$ is finite, so every element $q\in B_n$ has at least one
-minimal element $m$ of $B_n$ below it in the divisibility order. The upper-set
-property gives the reverse containment: every element of $D_n$ divisible by
-some $m\in\mathcal M_n$ lies again in $B_n$. This proves the displayed
-decomposition.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Minimal-lcm criterion]\label{thm:minimal-generators}
-Let $n\ge2$, and let
-$m=\prod_{i=1}^r p_i^{e_i}$ be a divisor of $F_n$, with the $p_i$ distinct
-and $e_i\ge1$. Put
-\[
-\lambda_i:=\alpha(p_i^{e_i}),\qquad
-\lambda_i^-:=\alpha(p_i^{e_i-1}),
-\]
-where $\alpha(1)=1$. Then $m\in\mathcal M_n$ if and only if
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:lcm-criterion}
-\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)=n
-\quad\text{and}\quad
-\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{i-1},\lambda_i^-,
-\lambda_{i+1},\ldots,\lambda_r)<n
-\quad(1\le i\le r).
-\end{equation}
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Because $m\mid F_n$, Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives
-$\lambda_i\mid n$ for every $i$. Applying the lcm identity in
-Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} repeatedly gives
-\[
-\alpha(m)=\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r).
-\]
-Thus the first condition in \eqref{eq:lcm-criterion} is equivalent to
-$m\in B_n$.
-
-Assume first that $m\in\mathcal M_n$. Then $m\in B_n$, so the first lcm is
-$n$. For a fixed $i$, the integer $m/p_i$ is a proper divisor of $m$ and is
-still a divisor of $F_n$. Minimality of $m$ in $B_n$ implies
-$m/p_i\notin B_n$. Since $\alpha(m/p_i)\mid n$, this is equivalent to
-$\alpha(m/p_i)<n$. A second application of the lcm identity gives
-\[
-\alpha(m/p_i)=
-\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{i-1},\lambda_i^-,
-\lambda_{i+1},\ldots,\lambda_r),
-\]
-which is the lowered prime-power condition in
-\eqref{eq:lcm-criterion}.
-
-Conversely, suppose \eqref{eq:lcm-criterion} holds. The first condition gives
-$m\in B_n$. Let $q$ be any proper divisor of $m$. Then for at least one
-index $i$ the exponent of $p_i$ in $q$ is at most $e_i-1$. Hence
-\[
-\alpha(q)\mid
-\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{i-1},\lambda_i^-,
-\lambda_{i+1},\ldots,\lambda_r),
-\]
-again by the lcm identity and by monotonicity under divisibility of prime
-powers. The right-hand side is $<n$ by
-\eqref{eq:lcm-criterion}. Since $q\mid m\mid F_n$, we also have
-$\alpha(q)\mid n$, and therefore $\alpha(q)<n$. Thus no proper divisor of
-$m$ lies in $B_n$, so $m$ is minimal in $B_n$.
+Let $D_n=\operatorname{Div}(F_n)$. The exact rank fiber can be read directly
+inside this divisor lattice.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Upper-fiber identity]\label{thm:upper-fiber}
+For every $n\geq2$,
+\[
+ B_n=D_n\setminus\bigcup_{p\mid n}D_{n/p}.
+\]
+Moreover, $B_n$ is an upper set in $D_n$, and hence
+\[
+ B_n=\bigcup_{m\in\mathcal M_n}\{q\in D_n:m\mid q\}.
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+By Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics}, $q\in D_n$ lies outside every
+$D_{n/p}$ precisely when $\alpha(q)\mid n$ but $\alpha(q)\nmid n/p$ for each
+prime $p\mid n$, which is equivalent to $\alpha(q)=n$. If $q\mid r\mid F_n$
+and $\alpha(q)=n$, then $n=\alpha(q)\mid\alpha(r)\mid n$, so $r\in B_n$.
+The final identity follows by taking minimal elements in the finite upper set.
 \end{proof}
 
-\subsection*{Witness covers}
-
-\begin{definition}\label{def:witness-cover}
-An \emph{$n$-witness cover} is a finite set
-$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$ of rank-jump prime powers satisfying:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item $d(\theta)\mid n$ for every $\theta\in\Theta$;
-\item the elements of $\Theta$ are pairwise coprime;
-\item the full-coordinate supports cover all prime coordinates of $n$,
-\[
-\bigcup_{\theta\in\Theta}T_n(\theta)=\mathcal P(n);
-\]
-\item each rank-jump factor has an essential coordinate not supplied by the other rank-jump factors,
-\[
-E_n(\theta)\nsubseteq
-\bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta,\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta)
-\qquad(\theta\in\Theta).
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-The last condition is the irredundance condition. It is stated with
-$E_n$ rather than $T_n$ because overlapping full-coordinate support is
-allowed; what is forbidden is that every coordinate lost by lowering
-$\theta$ is already supplied at full exponent by the remaining rank-jump factors.
-\end{definition}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Coordinate test for lowering one rank-jump factor]
-\label{lem:coordinate-lowering-test}
-Let $n\ge2$, and let
-$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$ be a pairwise coprime set of rank-jump
-prime powers with $d(\theta_i)\mid n$ and
-\[
-\lcmop(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d(\theta_r))=n.
-\]
-Fix $\theta_i=p_i^{e_i}$, and put
-\[
-N_i^-:=\lcmop\bigl(d^-(\theta_i),\ d(\theta_j):j\ne i\bigr).
-\]
-Then $N_i^-=n$ if and only if
-\[
-E_n(\theta_i)\subseteq\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j).
-\]
-Equivalently, lowering $\theta_i$ to $p_i^{e_i-1}$ keeps the apparition lcm
-equal to $n$ exactly when every coordinate lost by the lowering is supplied at
-full exponent by some other rank-jump factor. If
-$\ell\in E_n(\theta_i)\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$, then
-$\nu_\ell(N_i^-)<\nu_\ell(n)$, so $N_i^-<n$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Since $d^-(\theta_i)\mid d(\theta_i)\mid n$ and $d(\theta_j)\mid n$ for
-$j\ne i$, the integer $N_i^-$ divides $n$. Hence $N_i^-=n$ is equivalent to
-saying that every prime coordinate $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$ occurs in $N_i^-$
-with valuation $\nu_\ell(n)$.
-
-Assume first that
-$E_n(\theta_i)\subseteq\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$, and fix
-$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$. Because the original lcm is $n$, at least one of the
-numbers $d(\theta_1),\ldots,d(\theta_r)$ supplies the full
-$\ell$-adic valuation of $n$. If such a supplier is some $d(\theta_j)$ with
-$j\ne i$, then $\ell\in T_n(\theta_j)$ and the same full valuation appears in
-$N_i^-$. The only remaining case is that $\theta_i$ itself supplies the full
-valuation and no other rank-jump factor does, so $\ell\in T_n(\theta_i)$ and
-$\ell\notin\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$. The assumed containment then gives
-$\ell\notin E_n(\theta_i)$. By the definition of $E_n(\theta_i)$,
-$\nu_\ell(d^-(\theta_i))=\nu_\ell(n)$, so the lowered factor still supplies the
-full $\ell$-coordinate in $N_i^-$. Thus every coordinate of $n$ is still
-present at full valuation, and $N_i^-=n$.
-
-Conversely, suppose that some coordinate
-$\ell\in E_n(\theta_i)$ is not in $\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$. The
-membership $\ell\in E_n(\theta_i)$ says
-$\nu_\ell(d^-(\theta_i))<\nu_\ell(n)$. For every $j\ne i$, the exclusion
-$\ell\notin T_n(\theta_j)$ says
-$\nu_\ell(d(\theta_j))<\nu_\ell(n)$. Therefore the lcm defining $N_i^-$ also
-has $\ell$-adic valuation strictly below $\nu_\ell(n)$. Since $N_i^-\mid n$,
-this proves $N_i^-<n$.
+\begin{lemma}[Minimal-lcm criterion]\label{thm:minimal-generators}
+Let $n\geq2$, and let $m=\prod_{i=1}^r p_i^{e_i}$ divide $F_n$, with the
+$p_i$ distinct. Put
+\[
+ \lambda_i=\alpha(p_i^{e_i}),\qquad
+ \lambda_i^-=\alpha(p_i^{e_i-1}).
+\]
+Then $m\in\mathcal M_n$ if and only if
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lcm-criterion}
+ \lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)=n
+\end{equation}
+and, for every $i$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-lcm-criterion}
+ \lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{i-1},\lambda_i^-,
+        \lambda_{i+1},\ldots,\lambda_r)<n.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Repeated use of Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives
+$\alpha(m)=\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)$ and replaces $\lambda_i$ by
+$\lambda_i^-$ for $m/p_i$. Thus minimality implies both displays. Conversely,
+if they hold and $q$ is a proper divisor of $m$, then for some $i$ the
+$p_i$-exponent of $q$ is at most $e_i-1$, so
+\[
+ \alpha(q)\mid\lcmop(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_i^-,\ldots,\lambda_r)<n.
+\]
+Hence no proper divisor of $m$ belongs to $B_n$.
 \end{proof}
 
-\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
-\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
-Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
-rank-jump factors with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
-if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
-$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison]\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be distinct prime jumps with
+$d_i=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover if and only if
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
  \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
  \qquad
  \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
- \quad(1\le i\le r).
+ \quad(1\leq i\leq r).
 \end{equation}
-Thus the prime-jump case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
-multiplicative cover condition.
-
-For arbitrary pairwise coprime jumps
-$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
-deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime rank jumps, the second condition becomes
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
- \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
- d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
- \quad(1\le i\le r).
+ \lcmop(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,d(\theta_r))<n
+ \quad(1\leq i\leq r).
 \end{equation}
-In particular, ladder jumps supply the predecessor-decorated case: their
-label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For a prime jump $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
-$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
-\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and Lemma~\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test}
-then identify the witness-cover conditions with
-\eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
-minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
-produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
-
-For arbitrary rank-jump factors, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
-lcm is $n$ and that lowering each rank-jump factor produces
-\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
-distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime jumps and the nontrivial lower rank
-of a ladder jump.
+For a prime jump $p_i$, $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$, so lowering its label is the
+same as deleting it. In general, the full supports cover $\mathcal P(n)$
+exactly when the lcm of the labels is $n$. After $\theta_i$ is lowered, that
+lcm remains $n$ exactly when every coordinate in $E_n(\theta_i)$ is supplied
+at full exponent by another $T_n(\theta_j)$. The private-coordinate condition
+is therefore equivalent to the strict lowered-lcm inequality.
 \end{proof}
 
-Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
-cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
-realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the predecessor-lowering
-admissibility test forced by prime-power ladders, and the correspondence with
-$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
-in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
-realization.
+\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification}]
+Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$, and write
+$m=\prod_{i=1}^r\theta_i$ with $\theta_i=p_i^{e_i}$ and the $p_i$ distinct.
+Each $\theta_i$ is a rank jump: otherwise lowering its exponent would leave
+its rank unchanged, contrary to Lemma~\ref{thm:minimal-generators}. Since
+\[
+ n=\alpha(m)=\lcmop(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d(\theta_r)),
+\]
+the sets $T_n(\theta_i)$ cover $\mathcal P(n)$. The lowered-lcm condition in
+Lemma~\ref{thm:minimal-generators} gives, for every $i$, a coordinate in
+\[
+ E_n(\theta_i)\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j).
+\]
+Thus the prime-power factors of $m$ form an $n$-witness cover.
 
-\begin{theorem}\label{thm:witness-classification}
-For every $n\ge 2$, multiplication gives a bijection
-\[
-\Theta\longmapsto \prod_{\theta\in\Theta}\theta
-\]
-from the set of $n$-witness covers onto $\mathcal M_n$. Its inverse sends
-$m\in\mathcal M_n$ to the set
-\[
-\Theta(m):=\{p^{\nu_p(m)}:p\mid m\}
-\]
-of prime-power factors occurring in the prime factorization of $m$. In
-particular,
-\[
-\mathcal M_n=\bigl\{\prod_{\theta\in\Theta}\theta:
-\Theta\text{ is an $n$-witness cover}\bigr\},
-\]
-and each element of $\mathcal M_n$ has a unique witness-cover factorization.
-Here uniqueness is inherited from unique factorization in $\mathbb Z$; the
-substantive assertion is the witness-cover admissibility criterion.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$, and write its prime factorization as
-$m=\prod_{i=1}^r\theta_i$ with $\theta_i=p_i^{e_i}$ and the $p_i$ distinct.
-Each $\theta_i$ is rank-jump: if $\alpha(p_i^{e_i-1})=\alpha(p_i^{e_i})$, then
-replacing $\theta_i$ by $p_i^{e_i-1}$ preserves the lcm, contradicting
-the minimal-generator criterion in
-Lemma~\ref{thm:minimal-generators}. Since
-$n=\lcmop(d(\theta_i))$, the sets $T_n(\theta_i)$ cover $\mathcal P(n)$. The
-condition $\alpha(m/p_i)<n$ forces
-$E_n(\theta_i)\nsubseteq\bigcup_{j\neq i}T_n(\theta_j)$; otherwise the lost
-coordinates would be supplied by other factors, keeping the lcm equal to $n$.
-Thus $\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_r\}$ is an $n$-witness cover.
-
-Conversely, let $\Theta$ be an $n$-witness cover and
-$m=\prod_{\theta\in\Theta}\theta$. By
-the lcm property recorded in Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics},
-$\alpha(m)=\lcmop(d(\theta):\theta\in\Theta)=n$. For each
-$\theta=p^e\in\Theta$, the witness condition
-provides $\ell\in E_n(\theta)\setminus\bigcup_{\eta\neq\theta}T_n(\eta)$; at
-this coordinate, $\alpha(m/p)<n$.
-Lemma~\ref{thm:minimal-generators} then gives $m\in\mathcal M_n$.
-
-It remains to record injectivity and the stated inverse.  If two witness covers
-$\Theta$ and $\Theta'$ have the same product, then unique factorization in
-$\mathbb Z$ gives the same underlying primes with the same exponents in the two
-products.  Since the elements of each witness cover are pairwise coprime prime
-powers, those prime-power factors are exactly the elements of the cover.  Hence
-$\Theta=\Theta'$.  Therefore multiplication is injective, while the first
-paragraph shows that the prime-power factor set $\Theta(m)$ of every
-$m\in\mathcal M_n$ is an $n$-witness cover and the second paragraph shows that
-every $n$-witness cover maps into $\mathcal M_n$.  Thus multiplication is the
-claimed bijection, with inverse $m\mapsto\Theta(m)$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound}
-Every $m\in\mathcal M_n$ satisfies $\omega(m)\le\omega(n)$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The witness condition provides an injection
-$\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ from $\Theta$ into $\mathcal P(n)$: choose
-$\ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus\bigcup_{\eta\neq\theta}T_n(\eta)$.
-Hence $\omega(m)=\#\Theta\le\omega(n)$.
-\end{proof}
-
+Conversely, let $\Theta$ be an $n$-witness cover and put
+$m=\prod_{\theta\in\Theta}\theta$. Coverage gives $\alpha(m)=n$. For every
+$\theta=p^e\in\Theta$, a private essential coordinate is lost when $m$ is
+replaced by $m/p$, so $\alpha(m/p)<n$. Lemma~\ref{thm:minimal-generators}
+gives $m\in\mathcal M_n$.
+
+Unique factorization recovers the pairwise coprime prime-power factors from
+their product, proving injectivity and the stated inverse. Finally, choosing
+one private coordinate for each factor gives an injection
+$\Theta\hookrightarrow\mathcal P(n)$, whence
+$\omega(m)=\#\Theta\leq\omega(n)$.
+\end{proof}

-\section{Connected-dominance criteria}
-\label{sec:supp-connected-dominance}

-\begin{lemma}[Refined private-coordinate upper bound]
-\label{lem:refined-private-coordinate-upper-bound}
-For $m\ge2$, put $s=\omega(m)$ and $r=R(m)$. Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:refined-private-coordinate-upper-bound}
- \#\mathcal M_m\le U_s(r),\qquad
- U_s(r):=\sum_{t=1}^s\binom st
-             \bigl(r2^{s-t}+1\bigr)^t.
-\end{equation}
-There is an absolute constant $K$ such that, for all $s,r\ge1$,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:refined-upper-versus-covers}
- U_s(r)\le Kr^sC_s.
-\end{equation}
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The case $m=2$ is immediate from $\mathcal M_2=\varnothing$ and $R(2)=1$.
-Suppose $m\ge3$, and let a witness cover have $t$ rank-jump factors. Choose the canonical
-private coordinate of each rank-jump factor as in the proof of
-Theorem~\ref{article-thm:minimal-generator-growth}; let $P$ be the resulting
-$t$-set and $Q$ its complement. For a fixed $x\in P$, a prime jump has full
-support $\{x\}\cup U$ for some $U\subseteq Q$, giving at most
-$r2^{s-t}$ choices. A ladder jump with essential coordinate $x$ must be a
-power of the index prime $x$, and the full-exponent equation in
-Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} determines at most one such rank-jump factor
-over all its possible full supports. Thus the rank-jump factor assigned to $x$ has at most
-$r2^{s-t}+1$ choices. Summing over $P$ and $t$ proves
-\eqref{eq:refined-private-coordinate-upper-bound}; ignoring coverage and
-coprimeness only enlarges the count.
-
-For $r\ge1$,
-\[
- U_s(r)\le r^sU_s(1).
-\]
-If $t\le3s/4$, then, uniformly in this range,
-\[
- (2^{s-t}+1)^t
- =2^{t(s-t)}(1+2^{-(s-t)})^t
- =(1+o(1))2^{t(s-t)}.
-\]
-The sum over $t>3s/4$ is
-$2^{-s^2/16+O(s)}$ times a central term of
-$b_s=\sum_t\binom st2^{t(s-t)}$. Hence $U_s(1)\sim b_s$. The published
-asymptotic \eqref{article-eq:minimal-cover-theta} gives $C_s\sim b_s$; enlarging a
-constant to cover the finitely many small values of $s$ proves
-\eqref{eq:refined-upper-versus-covers}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Blockwise criterion for connected dominance]
-\label{thm:blockwise-connected-dominance}
-Let $(n_j)$ be a sequence, put $V_j=\mathcal P(n_j)$ and
-$k_j=\omega(n_j)\to\infty$, and for nonempty $C\subseteq V_j$ put
-\[
- (n_j)_C:=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n_j)}.
-\]
-For a nontrivial partition $\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(V_j)$ define
-\[
- \Delta(\Pi):=\sum_{\substack{C,D\in\Pi\\C<D}}|C||D|
- =\frac{k_j^2-\sum_{C\in\Pi}|C|^2}{2}.
-\]
-Suppose
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:blockwise-window-condition}
- \varepsilon_j:=
- \max_{\substack{\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(V_j)\\|\Pi|\ge2}}
- \frac{\sum_{C\in\Pi}|C|\log R((n_j)_C)}{\Delta(\Pi)}
- \longrightarrow0\qquad\text{\rm(BW)}.
-\end{equation}
-Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-dominance-conclusion}
- \frac{\#(\mathcal M_{n_j}\setminus\mathcal M_{n_j}^{\rm conn})}
- {\#\mathcal M_{n_j}^{\rm conn}}
- \le\exp\left[-\left(\frac{\log2}{2}-o(1)\right)k_j\right]
- =o(1).
-\end{equation}
-A sufficient condition for \eqref{eq:blockwise-window-condition} is
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:blockwise-window-sufficient-condition}
- \max_{\varnothing\ne C\subsetneq V_j}
- \frac{\log R((n_j)_C)}{k_j-|C|}\longrightarrow0
- \qquad\text{\rm(BW$'$)}.
-\end{equation}
-In particular, \eqref{eq:connected-dominance-conclusion} holds if
-$R((n_j)_C)=1$ for every nonempty proper block $C$ and all sufficiently
-large $j$.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The unique connected-block factorization in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:mingenerator-connected-factorization} gives
-\[
- \#(\mathcal M_{n_j}\setminus\mathcal M_{n_j}^{\rm conn})
- =\sum_{\substack{\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(V_j)\\|\Pi|\ge2}}
-   \prod_{C\in\Pi}M^{\rm conn}((n_j)_C).
-\]
-Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:refined-private-coordinate-upper-bound} to each block.
-The theta asymptotic \eqref{article-eq:minimal-cover-theta} gives uniform two-sided
-bounds
-\[
- C_s\asymp(s+1)^{-1/2}2^{s^2/4+s}.
-\]
-Consequently there is an absolute constant $K_1$ such that every partition
-$\Pi$ with block sizes $s_C=|C|$ contributes, after division by $C_{k_j}$,
-at most
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:partition-contribution-bound}
- K_1^{|\Pi|}\sqrt{k_j}\,
- \exp\left\{-\frac{\log2}{2}\Delta(\Pi)
- +\sum_{C\in\Pi}|C|\log R((n_j)_C)\right\}.
-\end{equation}
-Under \textup{(BW)}, this is
-\[
- K_1^{|\Pi|}\sqrt{k_j}\,
- \exp\left\{-\left(\frac{\log2}{2}-o(1)\right)
- \Delta(\Pi)\right\},
-\]
-where the $o(1)$ is uniform over all nontrivial partitions.
-
-If every block has size at most $k_j/2$, then
-$\Delta(\Pi)\ge k_j^2/4$. There are at most $k_j^{k_j}$ set partitions,
-so the total of these terms is $\exp(-\Omega(k_j^2))$. Otherwise there is a
-unique largest block of size $k_j-q>k_j/2$. Then
-$\Delta(\Pi)\ge q(k_j-q)$, and the remaining $q$ vertices can be selected and
-partitioned in at most
-\[
- \binom{k_j}{q}\mathsf B_q\le(ek_j)^q
-\]
-ways. Summing \eqref{eq:partition-contribution-bound} over
-$1\le q<k_j/2$ therefore gives
-\[
- \exp\left[-\left(\frac{\log2}{2}-o(1)\right)k_j\right]C_{k_j}.
-\]
-Corollary~\ref{cor:theta-refined-connected-entropy} gives
-$M^{\rm conn}(n_j)\ge(1-o(1))C_{k_j}$, proving
-\eqref{eq:connected-dominance-conclusion}.
-
-Finally, if the maximum in \textup{(BW$'$)} is $\eta_j$, then every block of
-a nontrivial partition is proper and
-\[
- \sum_{C\in\Pi}|C|\log R((n_j)_C)
- \le\eta_j\sum_{C\in\Pi}|C|(k_j-|C|)
- =2\eta_j\Delta(\Pi).
-\]
-Thus \textup{(BW$'$)} implies \textup{(BW)}, and the last assertion is the
-case $\eta_j=0$.
-\end{proof}

-\section{Connected block factorizations}\label{sec:connected}
-%% ====================================================================
-
-The hypergraph decomposition below is a generic consequence of strong
-divisibility and disjoint coordinate supports. Its role here is structural:
-the substantive endpoint for the present fibers is the induced factorization
-of minimal elements and the associated partition formulas.
-
-Use the support hypergraph from
-Definition~\ref{article-def:support-hypergraph}.  Write
-$n_C:=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n)}$ for nonempty
-$C\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, put
-\[
-B_n^{\mathrm{conn}}:=\{q\in B_n:\ H_n(q)\text{ is connected}\},\qquad
-A^{\mathrm{conn}}(n):=\#B_n^{\mathrm{conn}},
-\]
-and set $M^{\mathrm{conn}}(n):=\#\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$.
-For a connected component $C$ of $H_n(q)$, let $q_C$ be the product of
-those prime-power factors whose support edge lies in $C$.
-
-\begin{lemma}[Disjoint-block coprimality]\label{thm:coprime-embedding}
-Let $\Pi$ be a set partition of $\mathcal P(n)$. For each block
-$C\in\Pi$, choose $q_C\in D_{n_C}$. Then the integers $q_C$ are pairwise
-coprime. If in addition $q_C\in B_{n_C}$ for every $C$, then
-\[
-q:=\prod_{C\in\Pi}q_C
-\]
-lies in $B_n$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $C\ne C'$, then $\gcd(n_C,n_{C'})=1$, so
-\[
-\gcd(F_{n_C},F_{n_{C'}})=F_{\gcd(n_C,n_{C'})}=F_1=1
-\]
-by Proposition~\ref{article-prop:rank-basics}. Since $q_C\mid F_{n_C}$ and
-$q_{C'}\mid F_{n_{C'}}$, the chosen factors are pairwise coprime.
-Equivalently, any common prime divisor $p$ would satisfy
-$\alpha(p)\mid n_C$ and $\alpha(p)\mid n_{C'}$, hence
-$\alpha(p)\mid\gcd(n_C,n_{C'})=1$; this is impossible for a prime, and in
-particular excludes the shared special prime $5$ and any shared exact-rank prime
-across disjoint coordinate blocks.
-
-When $q_C\in B_{n_C}$ for every $C$, we have $\alpha(q_C)=n_C$. Repeated use
-of the lcm formula in Proposition~\ref{article-prop:rank-basics} gives
-\[
-\alpha\!\left(\prod_{C\in\Pi}q_C\right)
-=\lcmop(n_C:\ C\in\Pi)=\prod_{C\in\Pi}n_C=n.
-\]
-Also $q_C\mid F_{n_C}\mid F_n$, so the pairwise coprime product divides
-$F_n$. Hence $q\in B_n$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{theorem}\label{thm:birth-connected-factorization}
-Every $q\in B_n$ has a unique factorization
-\[
-q=\prod_{C\in\pi(q)}q_C
-\]
-indexed by the connected components $\pi(q)$ of $H_n(q)$, where
-$q_C\in B_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$ for every component $C$. Conversely, if
-$\Pi$ is a set partition of $\mathcal P(n)$ and
-$q_C\in B_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$ for every $C\in\Pi$, then
-$\prod_C q_C\in B_n$ and its connected components are exactly the blocks of
-$\Pi$. Consequently
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:partition-formula}
-A(n)=\sum_{\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(\mathcal P(n))}
-\prod_{C\in\Pi}A^{\mathrm{conn}}(n_C),
-\end{equation}
-with the convention that an empty factor contributes zero whenever
-$B_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}=\varnothing$.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $q=\prod_i p_i^{e_i}\in B_n$ and let $C$ be a component of $H_n(q)$.
-Every prime-power factor contributing to $q_C$ has rank support contained in
-$C$, so $\alpha(q_C)$ divides $n_C$. Conversely, fix $\ell\in C$. Since
-$\alpha(q)=n$ is the lcm of the ranks $\alpha(p_i^{e_i})$, some factor of
-$q$ has $\ell$-adic rank exponent equal to $\nu_\ell(n)$. Its support edge
-contains $\ell$, and therefore belongs to the component $C$. Thus the same
-factor occurs in $q_C$, and the $\ell$-adic exponent of $\alpha(q_C)$ is
-$\nu_\ell(n)$. This holds for every $\ell\in C$, while no coordinate outside
-$C$ occurs in $\alpha(q_C)$; hence $\alpha(q_C)=n_C$ and
-$q_C\in B_{n_C}$. The component of $H_{n_C}(q_C)$ on the vertex set $C$ is
-connected by construction, so $q_C\in B_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$.
-
-Uniqueness follows from unique prime-power factorization of $q$ and the
-unique connected-component partition of a hypergraph. The converse is exactly
-Lemma~\ref{thm:coprime-embedding}; because each $q_C$ is connected on its
-own block and no edge of $H_n(\prod_C q_C)$ meets two different blocks, the
-components are precisely the blocks of $\Pi$.
-
-Counting the converse construction over all set partitions gives
-\eqref{eq:partition-formula}, and uniqueness shows that no element is counted
-twice.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{theorem}\label{thm:mingenerator-connected-factorization}
-Every $m\in\mathcal M_n$ has a unique factorization
-\[
-m=\prod_{C\in\pi(m)}m_C
-\]
-over the connected components of $H_n(m)$, with
-$m_C\in\mathcal M_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$ for every $C$. Conversely, if
-$\Pi$ is a set partition of $\mathcal P(n)$ and
-$m_C\in\mathcal M_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$ for every $C\in\Pi$, then
-$\prod_C m_C\in\mathcal M_n$ and has component partition $\Pi$. Hence
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:minimal-partition-formula}
-\#\mathcal M_n=
-\sum_{\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(\mathcal P(n))}
-\prod_{C\in\Pi}M^{\mathrm{conn}}(n_C).
-\end{equation}
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$. Theorem~\ref{thm:birth-connected-factorization}
-gives $m_C\in B_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$ for each component. If some
-$s_C\in B_{n_C}$ satisfied $s_C\mid m_C$ and $s_C<m_C$, then
-\[
-s_C\prod_{D\ne C}m_D
-\]
-would divide $m$. The factors are pairwise coprime by
-Lemma~\ref{thm:coprime-embedding}, and the displayed product lies in
-$B_n$ by the same theorem. This contradicts the minimality of $m$ in $B_n$.
-Therefore $m_C\in\mathcal M_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$.
-
-Conversely, let $m=\prod_{C\in\Pi}m_C$ with
-$m_C\in\mathcal M_{n_C}^{\mathrm{conn}}$. Lemma~\ref{thm:coprime-embedding}
-puts $m$ in $B_n$. If $s\mid m$ and $s\in B_n$, write
-$s=\prod_C s_C$ with $s_C\mid m_C$; pairwise coprimeness of the block
-factors makes this decomposition unique. Since
-\[
-n=\alpha(s)=\lcmop(\alpha(s_C):C\in\Pi)
-\]
-and $\alpha(s_C)$ divides $n_C$, the disjointness of the coordinate sets
-forces $\alpha(s_C)=n_C$ for every $C$. Thus $s_C\in B_{n_C}$ for every
-$C$, and minimality of $m_C$ gives $s_C=m_C$. Hence $s=m$, proving
-$m\in\mathcal M_n$. The component statement and uniqueness are the same as
-in Theorem~\ref{thm:birth-connected-factorization}. Counting unique
-decompositions yields \eqref{eq:minimal-partition-formula}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Connected inversion]\label{cor:connected-inversion}
-The connected minimal-element counts are determined from the total counts by
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-inversion}
-A^{\mathrm{conn}}(n)=
-\sum_{\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(\mathcal P(n))}
-(-1)^{|\Pi|-1}(|\Pi|-1)!
-\prod_{C\in\Pi}A(n_C).
-\end{equation}
-The same inversion holds for minimal generators:
-\[
-M^{\mathrm{conn}}(n)=
-\sum_{\Pi\in\mathsf{Part}(\mathcal P(n))}
-(-1)^{|\Pi|-1}(|\Pi|-1)!
-\prod_{C\in\Pi}\#\mathcal M_{n_C}.
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Equation~\eqref{eq:partition-formula} is the ordinary exponential formula on
-the finite set $\mathcal P(n)$ with block weight
-$C\mapsto A^{\mathrm{conn}}(n_C)$. M\"obius inversion in the partition lattice
-\cite[Section~3.7]{Stanley2012EnumerativeCombinatoricsI}
-gives
-\[
-\mu_{\mathsf{Part}}(\Pi,\hat1)=(-1)^{|\Pi|-1}(|\Pi|-1)!,
-\]
-where $\hat1$ is the partition containing all coordinates in one block.
-Applying the same partition-lattice inversion to
-\eqref{eq:minimal-partition-formula} gives the minimal-generator formula.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}\label{cor:four-support-reduction}
-If $\omega(n)=4$, every element of $B_n$ and every element of
-$\mathcal M_n$ is obtained uniquely by choosing connected blocks whose sizes
-form one of the set-partition types
-\[
-4,\qquad 3+1,\qquad 2+2,\qquad 2+1+1,\qquad 1+1+1+1.
-\]
-Consequently, after the one-, two-, and three-coordinate classifications are
-known, the only single-block data not reduced by this corollary are the
-connected four-coordinate sets $B_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$ and
-$\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$.  The latter are now classified by
-Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-arithmetic-realization}; no corresponding
-classification of the full rank level set $B_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$ is asserted.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-This is Theorems~\ref{thm:birth-connected-factorization} and
-\ref{thm:mingenerator-connected-factorization} specialized to the set
-$\mathcal P(n)$ of size four. Every disconnected partition has all blocks of
-size at most three, so its factors are controlled by the previously proved
-one-, two-, and three-coordinate classifications. The only partition with a
-block of size four is the single-block partition, which is precisely the
-connected four-coordinate case.
-\end{proof}

-\section{Four-coordinate witness kernels}\label{sec:four-coordinate-kernels}
-
-The general enumeration of irredundant covers of finite sets is classical
-\cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}.  Here the relevant objects carry the
-additional Fibonacci essential/full-support decoration.  The classification
-below concerns this decorated structure and its arithmetic realization; the
-generic cover enumeration and Hall's theorem are used as inputs.
-
-Throughout this section assume
-\[
- \mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3,\ell_4\},\qquad
- a_i=\nu_{\ell_i}(n),\qquad V=[4].
-\]
-For nonempty $J\subseteq V$ and $i\in J$, write
-\[
- P_J:=(J,J),\qquad L_{i\mid J}:=(\{i\},J),
- \qquad S_i:=(\{i\},\{i\}).
-\]
-Thus $P_J$ denotes a prime slot, $L_{i\mid J}$ a proper ladder slot when
-$\#J>1$, and $S_i$ the undifferentiated singleton slot, which may be filled by
-either a prime or a ladder jump.  Braces and commas in subscripts are
-suppressed when no ambiguity can arise.
-
-For arithmetic filling, attach to these symbols the already defined rank-jump
-slot sets
-\[
- \mathfrak C(P_J)=\{p\in\mathcal A_{J,J}(n):p\text{ is prime}\},
- \qquad
- \mathfrak C(L_{i\mid J})=
- \{p^e\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},J}(n):e>1\},
-\]
-and
-\[
- \mathfrak C(S_i)=\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n).
-\]
-The exact-rank window, M\"obius count, and unique ladder-candidate formulas
-for these sets are those of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}; its proof is
-coordinatewise and the same formulas are read here with $[3]$ replaced by
-$V$.  We use these previously established formulas without claiming a new
-arithmetic result.

-\begin{theorem}[Complete four-coordinate kernel classification]
-\label{thm:four-coordinate-kernel-classification}
-Let
-\[
- \Delta=\{(I_1,J_1),\ldots,(I_r,J_r)\}
-\]
-be a collection of nonempty pairs satisfying
-\[
- I_j\subseteq J_j\subseteq V,\qquad
- I_j=J_j\ \text{or}\ \#I_j=1,
-\]
-\[
- \bigcup_{j=1}^rJ_j=V,
- \qquad
- I_j\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne j}J_h\ne\varnothing
- \quad(1\le j\le r).
-\]
-Up to coordinate permutation and reordering of slots, $\Delta$ belongs to
-exactly one of the twenty-four rows in
-Tables~\ref{tab:four-coordinate-connected-kernels} and
-\ref{tab:four-coordinate-disconnected-kernels}.  The first thirteen rows are
-exactly those for which the hypergraph with edges $J_1,\ldots,J_r$ is
-connected.  There are $243$ labelled kernels in total, of which $133$ have
-connected full-support hypergraph and $110$ do not.
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-For every slot choose a private coordinate
-$x_j\in I_j\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne j}J_h$.  These coordinates are distinct,
-so $r\le4$.  Suppose first that the $J$-hypergraph is connected.  If $r=1$,
-coverage gives $J_1=V$, and the prime--ladder alternative gives $K_1$ or
-$K_2$.  If $r=2$, set
-\[
- A=J_1\setminus J_2,
- \quad B=J_1\cap J_2,
- \quad C=J_2\setminus J_1.
-\]
-Private coordinates and connectedness make $A,B,C$ nonempty, and they
-partition $V$.  Up to interchanging the two slots, their cardinalities are
-$(1,2,1)$ or $(1,1,2)$.  The former gives two three-element edges and the
-three prime/ladder patterns $K_3$--$K_5$.  The latter gives edges of sizes two
-and three; their sizes distinguish the slots, producing the four patterns
-$K_6$--$K_9$.
-
-If $r=3$, write the private coordinates as $x_1,x_2,x_3$ and the remaining
-coordinate as $y$.  Private-coordinate exclusion gives
-$J_j\subseteq\{x_j,y\}$.  Connectedness excludes $J_j=\{x_j\}$, hence the
-full supports form the unique three-leaf star
-$J_j=\{x_j,y\}$.  The number of prime slots is then the complete orbit
-invariant, giving $K_{10}$--$K_{13}$.  Finally, if $r=4$, the private
-coordinates exhaust $V$ and force $J_j=\{x_j\}$ for every $j$, which is
-disconnected.  This proves the completeness of the first table.
-
-For a disconnected $J$-hypergraph, its connected components partition $V$.
-A one-coordinate component is $S_i$.  A two-coordinate component consists of
-one edge and is $P_{ij}$ or $L_{i\mid ij}$.  By the complete
-three-coordinate classification, the connected three-coordinate components
-are precisely
-\[
- P_{123},\quad L_{1\mid123},\quad P_{12}P_{23},\quad
- L_{1\mid12}P_{23},\quad L_{1\mid12}L_{3\mid23}.
-\]
-The component-size partitions $2+2$, $3+1$, $2+1+1$, and $1+1+1+1$
-therefore contribute respectively $3,5,2,1$ orbits, exactly the rows
-$D_1$--$D_{11}$.  Component sizes, component types, edge sizes, and the
-prime/ladder status after those data are fixed show that no two listed rows
-are equivalent.
-
-For each row the labelled orbit size is
-$24/\#\operatorname{Stab}_{S_4}(\Delta)$.  The displayed values sum to
-\[
- 133=1+4+6+12+6+12+12+24+24+4+12+12+4
-\]
-and
-\[
- 110=3+12+12+4+12+12+24+12+6+12+1,
-\]
-respectively.  The preceding exhaustive case split proves that these orbits
-contain every labelled kernel, giving the total $243$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{proposition}[Strict separation of the two support notions]
-\label{prop:four-coordinate-support-separation}
-There exist four-coordinate minimal generators whose positive-support
-hypergraph is connected although their full-support hypergraph is not.  More
-precisely, for
-\[
- n=3^2\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11=3465,
- \qquad
- m=17\cdot61\cdot421\cdot19801=8644661177,
-\]
-one has $m\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{conn}}$, while the hypergraph with edges
-$T_n(\theta)$ for the four rank-jump factors of $m$ is disconnected.
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The four primes have exact ranks
-\[
- \alpha(17)=9,\qquad \alpha(61)=15,\qquad
- \alpha(421)=21,\qquad \alpha(19801)=33.
-\]
-Indeed,
-\[
- F_9=2\cdot17,\quad F_{15}=2\cdot5\cdot61,\quad
- F_{21}=2\cdot13\cdot421,\quad
- F_{33}=2\cdot89\cdot19801,
-\]
-and none of the displayed primes divides the Fibonacci number at a proper
-divisor of its displayed index.  With coordinates ordered as $(3,5,7,11)$,

-\begin{proof}

-\end{equation}
+The \emph{rank-pure sector} $\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$ consists of all products

-\subsection*{Organization}
+Wagner's minimal multiplicative covers
+\cite{Wagner1978MultiplicativeCovers} supply the classical prime-jump
+skeleton: deleting one lcm label must lower the lcm. Fibonacci prime-power
+lifting adds the predecessor $d^-(\theta)$, so a ladder label must be lowered
+rather than deleted. Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} identifies
+exactly which such covers are the minimal rank fibers.
 
-Section~\ref{sec:prelim} records the classical rank and primitive-divisor
-inputs. Section~\ref{sec:upper-fibers} gives the Wagner comparison and proves
-the witness-cover classification. Section~\ref{sec:prime-power-realization}
-proves the prime-power lifting, prime--ladder dichotomy, and unique ladder-slot
-formula. Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} develops the canonical squarefree slice,
-its weighted count, the labelled cover asymptotic, and worked examples.
-Section~\ref{sec:growth} proves the rank-window, fibotomic, support-entropy,
-and large-primitive-divisor bounds. Section~\ref{sec:inverse-dynamics} gives the short inverse-ray
-application, and the final section states the remaining arithmetic
-interfaces. The submitted supplement contains the connected-block
-factorization, exact support spectra, complete classifications for
-$\omega(n)\le4$, secondary asymptotics, and finite checks, all with numbered
-cross-references.
+The arithmetic realization uses the classical existence of an exact-rank
+prime for every rank $n\geq3$ except $6$ and $12$, following Carmichael and
+Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier
+\cite{Carmichael1913PrimitiveDivisors,BiluHanrotVoutier2001PrimitiveDivisorsLucas}.
+The multiplicities $a(d)$ retain information not supplied by existence alone;
+they become the weights in Theorem~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}.

-We now apply Theorem~\ref{thm:fibotomic-rank-entropy} to the standard
-primitive part of a Fibonacci number.  This requires retaining multiplicities
-in the classical Lucas cyclotomic-factor theorem, rather than only the radical

-For $n\geq13$, define
-\[
- U_n^{\rm prim}:=
- \prod_{\substack{p\mid F_n\\p\nmid 5F_1\cdots F_{n-1}}}

-\]
-Thus the product uses the discriminant-excluding Lucas-sequence convention

-\begin{lemma}[Classical primitive part of the Fibonacci cyclotomic factor]
-\label{lem:classical-primitive-part}
-For every $n\geq13$ there is an integer $c_n$ such that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:primitive-part-factorization}
- \Psi_n(1)=c_nU_n^{\rm prim},
- \qquad
- c_n=1\quad\text{or}\quad c_n\text{ is a prime divisor of }n.
-\end{equation}
-In particular,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:primitive-part-ratio}
- 1\leq\frac{\Psi_n(1)}{U_n^{\rm prim}}\leq n
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:primitive-part-log-mass}
- \log U_n^{\rm prim}
- =\phi_{\rm E}(n)\log\varphi+O(\log n).
-\end{equation}
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The Lucas cyclotomic factor denoted $\phi_n$ by Granville is
-\[
- \prod_{d\mid n}F_d^{\mu(n/d)}=\Psi_n(1)
-\]
-in the present Fibonacci specialization.  Granville's cyclotomic-factor
-theorem states that a characteristic prime of $F_n$ occurs in this factor
-with the same exponent as in $F_n$.  Every noncharacteristic prime $p$ in
-the factor occurs only to the first power and satisfies
-$n/z(p)=p^a$ for some $a\geq1$; apart from the indices $6$ and $12$, there
-is at most one such prime
-\cite[Corollaries~3 and~4]{Granville2012PrimitivePrimeFactors}.
-
-At $n\geq13$, the characteristic primes are exactly the primes satisfying
-$p\mid F_n$ and $p\nmid F_1\cdots F_{n-1}$.  None is $5$, since $z(5)=5$,
-so they are exactly the primitive primes in the convention above.  Any
-remaining prime $p$ in $\Psi_n(1)$ satisfies $p\mid n$ by
-$n/z(p)=p^a$; this also covers the possible discriminant prime $5$ at an
-index divisible by a higher power of $5$.  The cited theorem therefore gives
-\eqref{eq:primitive-part-factorization}, including equality of all primitive
-exponents.  The bound \eqref{eq:primitive-part-ratio} follows immediately.
-Finally, \eqref{eq:fibotomic-binet-error} and
-$1\leq c_n\leq n$ give \eqref{eq:primitive-part-log-mass}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Large primitive divisor--Fibonacci--Wieferich alternative]
-\label{thm:large-primitive-wieferich-alternative}
-Let $F_0=0$ and $F_1=1$.  Call a prime $p$ a primitive prime divisor of
-$F_n$ when
-\[
- p\mid F_n\qquad\text{and}\qquad p\nmid 5F_1F_2\cdots F_{n-1}.
-\]
-For every real $\varepsilon>0$, there is an integer
-$N_\varepsilon\geq13$ such that, for every $n\geq N_\varepsilon$, at least
-one of the following holds:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
-\item $F_n$ has a primitive prime divisor $p\geq n^{2-\varepsilon}$;
-\item $F_n$ has a primitive prime divisor $q$ such that $q^2\mid F_n$.
-\end{enumerate}
-In the second alternative, $z(q)=n$ and $q$ is a Wall--Sun--Sun,
-equivalently Fibonacci--Wieferich, prime.
-
-Consequently, if no Wall--Sun--Sun primes exist and
-$P_{\rm prim}(F_n)$ denotes the largest primitive prime divisor of $F_n$,
-then
-\[
- \liminf_{n\to\infty}
- \frac{\log P_{\rm prim}(F_n)}{\log n}\geq2.
-\]
-Equivalently, $P_{\rm prim}(F_n)\geq n^{2-o(1)}$.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Fix $n\geq13$ and suppose alternative \textup{(ii)} fails.  Every primitive
-prime then occurs in $F_n$ to exponent one.  The classical primitive-divisor
-theorem gives at least one such prime, and hence
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:primitive-part-max-bound}
- \log U_n^{\rm prim}
- \leq a(n)\log P_{\rm prim}(F_n).
-\end{equation}
-For $n\geq13$, the exact-rank primes counted by $a(n)$ are precisely the
-primitive prime divisors in the convention of the theorem.  By
-\eqref{eq:pointwise-exact-rank-bound} and
-\eqref{eq:primitive-part-log-mass},
-\[
- a(n)\leq
- \left(\frac{\log\varphi}{2}+o(1)\right)
- \frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{\log n},
- \qquad
- \log U_n^{\rm prim}
- =(\log\varphi+o(1))\phi_{\rm E}(n).
-\]
-Here $O(\log n)=o(\phi_{\rm E}(n))$ follows from the standard lower bound
-$\phi_{\rm E}(n)\gg n/\log\log(3n)$.  Substitution in
-\eqref{eq:primitive-part-max-bound} gives, uniformly as $n\to\infty$,
-\[
- \log P_{\rm prim}(F_n)\geq(2-o(1))\log n.
-\]
-The first alternative therefore holds for all sufficiently large $n$, with
-the threshold depending only on $\varepsilon$.
-
-It remains to identify the other alternative.  A primitive $q$ has
-$q>5$ and $z(q)=n$.  Put $h_q=\nu_q(F_{z(q)})$.  Proposition~
-\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} gives $q^2\mid F_{z(q)}$ exactly when
-$h_q\geq2$.  Since $z(q)\mid q-(5/q)$ and $q\nmid q-(5/q)$, the same
-valuation formula shows that this is equivalent to
-\[
- q^2\mid F_{q-(5/q)},
-\]
-the standard Wall--Sun--Sun or Fibonacci--Wieferich condition
-\cite{Klaska2018WallConjecture}.  The conditional conclusion follows by
-excluding alternative \textup{(ii)} for every $n$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Comparison with known large-divisor results]
-\label{rem:large-primitive-comparison}
-Stewart proved the unconditional lower bound
-$n\exp(\log n/(104\log\log n))$ for the greatest prime factor of the relevant
-Lucas cyclotomic factor, beyond an effective sequence-dependent threshold
-\cite[Theorem~1]{Stewart2013DivisorsLucasLehmer}.  Hong gives an explicit
-Fibonacci formulation: for each fixed positive integer $\kappa$, every
-sufficiently large $F_n$ has a primitive divisor outside
-$n\pm1,\ldots,\kappa n\pm1$, and hence one at least
-$(\kappa+1)n-1$ \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Hong2025BigPrimitiveDivisors}.
-The exponent $2-o(1)$ above is much stronger, but only after excluding the
-lifting anomaly.
-
-In Kiss's 1988 chapter, Theorem~2 fixes a nondegenerate Lucas sequence and a
-real $0<\lambda<1$, and proves that a positive proportion of the indices
-$n\leq x$ have a primitive prime-power factor of $R_n$ exceeding
-$n^{2-\lambda}$, for all sufficiently large $x$
-\cite[Theorem~2]{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}.  This is a positive-density
-result for the full prime power, not a pointwise lower bound for its base
-prime; indeed, Kiss notes that it does not decide whether the primes or the
-exponents are large.  By contrast, the theorem above treats every
-sufficiently large rank and separates the base-prime size from multiplicity
-at that same rank: failure of the large-base-prime alternative yields a
-repeated primitive prime of exact rank $n$, hence a Wall--Sun--Sun prime.
-Kiss's theorem gives neither that exact-rank alternative nor the all-indices
-conditional liminf displayed above.
-
-Kiss proved an earlier, different bridge to Wieferich-type primes: if, for a
-fixed $0<\delta<1$, the greatest primitive divisor of a Lucas term is below
-$n^{1+\delta}$ for almost all indices, then a positive-density set of indices
-has a term divisible by a Wieferich-type prime
-\cite{Kiss1987WieferichLucas}.  That result is neither pointwise nor an
-exact-rank alternative.  The theorem above does not resolve Wall's question;
-it says that failure of a near-quadratic primitive divisor cannot occur in an
-ordinary rank-lifting layer, but forces a Fibonacci--Wieferich anomaly at that
-exact rank.
-\end{remark}

-\label{def:three-coordinate-slot-construction}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$ and identify the prime

-\[

-\begin{theorem}[Complete low-support classification: eight support-three families]
-\label{thm:low-support-classification-package}
-Let $n\ge2$.  The minimal generators $\mathcal M_n$ are classified for
-$\omega(n)\le3$ as follows.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
-\item If $\omega(n)=1$, then $\mathcal M_n=\Atom(n)$.

- disjoint union of $\Atom(n)$ and the products

- $\theta_i\in\mathcal A_{\{i\},\{i\}}(n)$ and
- $\gcd(\theta_1,\theta_2)=1$.
-\item If $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$, then $\mathcal M_n$ is the
- set of distinct products admitted by Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification},
- after applying all coordinate permutations and the finite slot-selection
- criterion of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection}.  Equivalently, for each
- permuted row one chooses one prime power from each displayed slot set, with
- distinct underlying primes. Every such product occurs. Each element of
- $\mathcal M_n$ has a unique labelled support set $\mathsf T(m)$, while its
- unlabelled $\Gamma_i$ is determined only up to the $S_3$-orbit; a product
- produced more than once by the raw permuted enumeration is retained once.
-\end{enumerate}
-For the three-coordinate rows,
-$P_J(n)$ denotes the exact-rank prime slot, $L_{i,J}(n)$ the ladder slot with
-essential coordinate $i$ and full support $J$, and
-$S_i(n)=P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n)$ the singleton slot.  Each slot is the
-following explicit finite set:
-\[
-\begin{aligned}
-\mathfrak C(P_J)&:=\bigcup_{d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d),\\
-\mathfrak C(L_{i,J})&:=\{\lambda\in\mathcal L_i^*(n):\alpha(\lambda)\mid n,
-\ \{k:\nu_{\ell_k}(\alpha(\lambda))=\nu_{\ell_k}(n)\}=J\},\\
-\mathfrak C(S_i)&:=\mathfrak C(P_{\{i\}})\cup \mathfrak C(L_{i,\{i\}}).
-\end{aligned}
-\]
-Here $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ is the finite exact-rank window and
-$\mathcal L_i^*(n)$ is the empty-or-singleton ladder candidate set of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}. A row succeeds
-exactly when its displayed finite slot sets admit a filling by distinct
-underlying primes, equivalently when the Hall test of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} holds.  The displayed rows are
-representatives modulo relabeling of the coordinates $1,2,3$.
-Equivalently, writing $[3]=\{1,2,3\}$, suppressing braces in prime-slot
-subscripts, and letting $(i,j,k)$ range over ordered triples of distinct
-coordinates, the eight orbit representatives are
-\[
-P_{[3]},\quad L_{i,[3]},\quad P_{i,j}P_{j,k},\quad
-L_{i,\{i,j\}}P_{j,k},\quad
-L_{i,\{i,j\}}L_{k,\{j,k\}},\quad S_iP_{j,k},
-\quad S_iL_{j,\{j,k\}},\quad S_iS_jS_k,
-\]
-respectively for $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4,\Gamma_5,\Gamma_6,\Gamma_7,
-\Gamma_8,\Gamma_9$.
-Let $\mathcal G_n$ denote the finite set displayed in (i), (ii), or (iii), with
-the convention $\mathcal G_2=\varnothing$.  Then, for every $n\ge2$ with
-$\omega(n)\le3$,
-\[
-\mathcal G_n=\mathcal M_n,
-\]
-and the displayed list is a finite minimal-generator classification. The
-table should be read in three passes.  First choose one of the eight
-unlabelled support skeletons and then apply an arbitrary permutation of the
-coordinate labels $1,2,3$.  Next replace every displayed slot by its explicit
-finite candidate set $\mathfrak C(\cdot)$, so prime slots are tested through
-the rank windows $\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)$ and ladder slots through the candidate
-sets $\mathcal L_i^*(n)$. Finally apply the distinct-prime Hall test and insert
-the resulting products into a set: a row
-contributes exactly the products obtained by choosing one prime power from each
-of its candidate slots with no underlying prime repeated.  The lemmas preceding
-the theorem prove that these three finite steps are equivalent to the abstract
-witness-cover conditions, so the table is not an additional heuristic case
-split but the effective normal form for all support-three minimal generators.
-

-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-The one-coordinate assertion is Corollary~\ref{cor:one-support-complete-classification}.
-The two-coordinate assertion is Corollary~\ref{cor:two-support-complete-classification}.
-Assume now that $\omega(n)=3$. Lemma~\ref{lem:fibonacci-three-coordinate-types}
-reduces every witness cover to the eight listed abstract types and excludes
-$\Gamma_2$. Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families} translates
-an abstract slot $(I,J)$ into exactly one of the displayed prime, ladder,
-or singleton families: nonsingleton slots with $I=J$ are $P_J(n)$, proper
-ladder slots $I=\{i\}\subsetneq J$ are $L_{i,J}(n)$, and singleton slots are
-$S_i(n)=P_{\{i\}}(n)\cup L_{i,\{i\}}(n)$. Substituting these translations into
-the eight admissible abstract types of Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}
-gives precisely the rows of Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}.
-The same substitution, with braces suppressed in prime-slot subscripts,
-gives the displayed canonical-family list: the first two rows are the full
-prime and full ladder families, the next three are the two-slot overlapping
-families, the next two attach a singleton slot to a nonsingleton slot, and the
-last row is the three-singleton family.
-
-It remains only to identify the tests in the last column. For prime slots,
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests} gives
-$P_J(n)=\bigcup_{d\in\mathcal R_J^\circ(n)}\Pi_\alpha(d)$ and, after deleting
-previously used underlying primes, the stated finite multiplicity criterion.
-For ladder slots, the same proposition gives the displayed singleton-candidate
-formula for $L_{i,J}(n)$. Pairwise coprimeness of the chosen prime powers is
-exactly the distinct-underlying-prime condition because all slots are filled by
-prime powers. Hence the table's row test is the arithmetic selection test of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness}. That theorem also gives the
-converse construction and uniqueness, up to reordering slots with identical
-labelled data, while Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification} identifies the
-resulting products with the elements of $\mathcal M_n$.
-
-Thus the displayed support-dependent set $\mathcal G_n$ equals
-$\mathcal M_n$ in all cases $\omega(n)\le3$, including the boundary convention
-$\mathcal G_2=\varnothing=\mathcal M_2$.  In the three-coordinate case the
-finiteness of the prime and ladder slot sets and the exact slot enumeration
-are supplied by Proposition~\ref{prop:three-coordinate-table-checklist}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Support-three obstruction certificates]
-\label{cor:support-three-obstruction-certificates}
-Assume $\omega(n)=3$ and let a proposed support-three minimal-generator shape be
-specified by an irredundant finite list of rank-jump slots whose full-support sets
-cover the labelled coordinates $\{1,2,3\}$.  Exactly one of the following
-alternatives occurs.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
-\item The shape is the excluded skeleton $\Gamma_2$, equivalently it requires an
-rank-jump factor with $1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta)=3$; then no Fibonacci minimal
-generator has that shape.
-\item After relabeling it is one of the eight rows in
-Table~\ref{tab:three-coordinate-classification}.  The row contributes exactly
-the products obtained from the finite candidate sets
-$\mathfrak C(P_J)$, $\mathfrak C(L_{i,J})$, and $\mathfrak C(S_i)$ by choosing
-one prime power in each row slot with distinct underlying primes.
-\item The row is one of the eight admissible skeletons but the finite
-distinct-prime Hall inequalities of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} fail;
-then the row contributes no element of $\mathcal M_n$.
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus every failure in support three has a certificate of one of two kinds: the
-single structural Fibonacci obstruction $\Gamma_2$, or a finite Hall deficiency
-inside an otherwise admissible slot row.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}, every irredundant three-coordinate
-witness skeleton is one of $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_9$. The prime--ladder
-dichotomy, Lemma~\ref{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}, excludes precisely the
-case in which a rank-jump factor has a proper nonsingleton essential set inside a larger
-full-support set; among the nine skeletons this is exactly $\Gamma_2$, proving
-(a).
-
-For every remaining skeleton, Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-rank-jump-families}
-translates each abstract slot into one of the prime slots $P_J(n)$, ladder
-slots $L_{i,J}(n)$, or singleton slots $S_i(n)$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-arithmetic-tests}
-identifies these as the finite candidate sets displayed in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.  A selected row therefore
-forms a witness cover exactly when its chosen prime powers are pairwise
-coprime, and for prime powers this is exactly distinctness of underlying primes.
-Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-slot-selection} is precisely the Hall criterion for such a
-selection.  If the criterion holds, Theorem~\ref{article-thm:witness-classification}
-turns the selected witness cover into the corresponding element of
-$\mathcal M_n$; if it fails, no coprime filling of that row exists.  These are
-(b) and (c), and the alternatives exhaust all support-three possibilities.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Low-support rank level sets and counting]
-\label{cor:low-support-normal-form}
-\label{cor:low-support-birth-layer-package}
-\label{prop:low-support-cardinality-formula}
-Let $n\ge2$ with $\omega(n)\le3$, and let $\mathcal G_n$ be the finite
-minimal-generator set described in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package}.  Then $\mathcal G_n$ is
-the canonical antichain of minimal elements of $B_n$, and for every $q\in D_n$,
-\[
-q\in B_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\text{there exists }g\in\mathcal G_n\text{ with }g\mid q.
-\]
-Equivalently,
-\[
-B_n=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal G_n}\{q\in D_n:\ g\mid q\},
-\]
-where the union is taken inside the divisor lattice $D_n$ and is not asserted
-to be disjoint.  The rank-level-set cardinality is the closed finite formula
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-support-cardinality-formula}
-A(n)=
-\sum_{\varnothing\ne\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal G_n}
-(-1)^{|\mathcal S|+1}
-\tau\left(\frac{F_n}{\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)}\right),
-\end{equation}
-with the convention that the empty sum is $0$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Theorem~\ref{thm:low-support-classification-package} gives
-$\mathcal G_n=\mathcal M_n$ for $\omega(n)\le3$, including the boundary
-convention $\mathcal G_2=\varnothing=\mathcal M_2$. Minimal elements of an
-upper set are pairwise incomparable, so $\mathcal G_n$ is an antichain in
-$D_n$.  The upper-fiber identity, Lemma~\ref{article-thm:upper-fiber}, gives for every
-$n\ge2$ the principal-upper-ideal decomposition
-\[
-B_n=\bigcup_{m\in\mathcal M_n}\{q\in D_n:m\mid q\}.
-\]
-Replacing $\mathcal M_n$ by $\mathcal G_n$ gives the displayed union and the
-membership criterion.  The minimal elements of this union are exactly the
-generators in $\mathcal G_n$, because no two elements of $\mathcal G_n$ are
-comparable.
-
-It remains to count the union.  If $\mathcal G_n=\varnothing$, then
-$B_n=\varnothing$, so $A(n)=0$ and the empty-sum convention gives
-\eqref{eq:low-support-cardinality-formula}.  Otherwise, for $g\in\mathcal G_n$
-put $U_g:=\{q\in D_n:g\mid q\}$.  For a nonempty subset
-$\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal G_n$, a divisor $q$ of $F_n$ lies in
-$\bigcap_{g\in\mathcal S}U_g$ if and only if
-$\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)$ divides $q$.  Since every $g\in\mathcal G_n$ divides
-$F_n$, this least common multiple also divides $F_n$, and division by it gives a
-bijection
-\[
-\bigcap_{g\in\mathcal S}U_g
-\longleftrightarrow
-\operatorname{Div}\left(F_n/\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)\right).
-\]
-Hence
-\[
-\#\bigcap_{g\in\mathcal S}U_g=
-\tau\left(\frac{F_n}{\lcmop(g:g\in\mathcal S)}\right).
-\]
-Ordinary finite inclusion--exclusion applied to
-$B_n=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal G_n}U_g$ proves
-\eqref{eq:low-support-cardinality-formula}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Prime-only three-coordinate skeleton]
-\label{cor:primitive-three-skeleton}
-Assume $\mathcal P(n)=\{\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\}$ and that
-$n_S:=\prod_{i\in S}\ell_i^{\nu_{\ell_i}(n)}$ satisfies
-$n_S\ge 3$ and $n_S\notin\{6,12\}$ for every nonempty
-$S\subseteq[3]$. Then the four prime-only three-coordinate
-types $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_4$, $\Gamma_7$, and $\Gamma_9$ are realized in
-$\mathcal M_n$. More precisely, after choosing exact-rank primes
-$\pi_S$ with $\alpha(\pi_S)=n_S$, the following minimal generators realize
-these types:
-\[
-\pi_{123},\qquad
-\pi_{12}\pi_{23},\qquad
-\pi_1\pi_{23},\qquad
-\pi_1\pi_2\pi_3 .
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The hypothesis and Theorem~\ref{article-thm:primitive-divisors} provide the indicated
-exact-rank primes. An exact-rank prime for $n_S$ is a prime jump with
-$E_n(\pi_S)=T_n(\pi_S)=S$. The four displayed collections of coordinate
-sets are precisely the prime-only types $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_4$,
-$\Gamma_7$, and $\Gamma_9$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract-three-types}, and
-the chosen primes are pairwise distinct. The
-pairwise-coprime selection criterion of
-Lemma~\ref{lem:three-coordinate-nonemptiness} therefore gives the four
-minimal generators.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}\label{rem:wss}
-The only Wall--Sun--Sun input needed here is local.  By
-Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}, for $p\neq 2,5$ one has
-$\alpha(p^2)=\alpha(p)$ if and only if $\nu_p(F_{\alpha(p)})\ge 2$, the
-Wall--Sun--Sun condition for $p$ \cite{SunSun1992FibonacciFLT}.  Thus the
-condition merely determines whether the first odd-prime ladder step is delayed;
-we do not use any distributional assertion about such primes.
-\end{remark}

-\section{Low-support classifications}\label{sec:low-support}

-
-We now introduce the Fibonacci-specific arithmetic input. The structural
-results of Section~\ref{article-sec:upper-fibers} did not use the formulas below.
